# Material Web 3.0 (full documentation)

> Material Web 3.0: Material 3 Expressive components, styles and foundations built as web components.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/

# About

Get started with Material Web 3.0 and find the project information: quick start, migration, support, roadmap and browser support.

Getting started and project information: how to install and use Material Web 3.0, how it follows the Material 3 spec, what is coming next, and where to get help.

- [Introduction](/material-web/3.0/about/intro/): Material web, also known as Material Web Components or MWC, is a library of web components that follows Google's Material Design guidelines.
- [Spec compliance](/material-web/3.0/about/compliance/): What the spec checks, ARIA and axe results, Baseline use and size budgets say about md-gb-* components.
- [Quick Start](/material-web/3.0/about/quick-start/): For fast prototyping, use a CDN such as esm.run to load @material/web without installing it.
- [Migration](/material-web/3.0/about/migration/): Version 3.0 renames most elements from md- to md-gb- and moves them to Material 3 Expressive.
- [Roadmap](/material-web/3.0/about/roadmap/): This roadmap describes current, future, and past goals for Material Web Components.
- [Support](/material-web/3.0/about/support/): Version 3.0 targets Baseline widely available: the web platform features it uses have worked in all major browsers for at least 30 months.
- [Bundle Sizes](/material-web/3.0/about/size/): Every md-gb- component is checked against a Brotli-compressed size budget for its JavaScript and CSS (the measured size plus 10% headroom), defined in scripts/size/gb-budgets.json.
- [Browser support](/material-web/3.0/about/browser-support/): Version 3.0 only uses web platform features that are Baseline widely available.
- [AI agents](/material-web/3.0/about/ai-agents/): labs/gb/skill/ is a Claude Code skill named md-gb.
- [Debugging](/material-web/3.0/about/debugging/): The shared plumbing of the components (motion waits, overflow measure passes, and scroll steps) can record performance marks.
- [Use with shadcn/ui](/material-web/3.0/about/shadcn/): Install the md-gb elements as React components with the shadcn CLI, themed by your shadcn variables.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/intro/

# Introduction

Material web, also known as Material Web Components or MWC, is a library of web components that follows Google's Material Design guidelines.

## What is Material?

Material Design is a design system built and supported by Google designers and
developers. Guidelines for building Material apps and components are published
on [material.io](https://material.io).

Version 3.0 implements **Material 3 Expressive**, the latest evolution of
Material 3: a larger shape scale with shape morphing, spring-based motion, an
emphasized type scale, and an updated dynamic color system. The elements are
named `md-gb-*`, follow the
[WAI-ARIA](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.3/) patterns for their roles, and
only rely on web platform features that are
[Baseline](https://web.dev/baseline) widely available (newer features are
guarded and degrade gracefully).

![An example of a Material Design application.](/material-web/about/images/what-is-material.webp "What is Material?")

## What are web components?

[Web components](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_components)
are custom HTML elements with encapsulated styles and behavior. They work across
many different frameworks (such as Lit, React, Vue, and Svelte) as well as web
environments (such as Eleventy, Wordpress, and Ruby on Rails).

Many components in this library are drop-in replacements for browser elements
like `<button>` and `<input>`. Every element is prefixed with `md-gb-`.

**Example: A form with a text field and a button**

```html
<form>
  <md-gb-text-field label="Email" type="email" name="email" required></md-gb-text-field>
  <md-gb-button color="filled">Subscribe</md-gb-button>
</form>
```

## What are tokens?

[Design tokens](https://m3.material.io/foundations/design-tokens/overview) are
the building blocks of all UI elements. Here they are
[CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*)
that you can override to style components. Version 3.0 provides the system
tokens for color, typography, shape, elevation, space, and motion.

**Example: A button with an olive primary color**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">Subscribe</md-gb-button>
```

*CSS*

```css
:root {
  --md-sys-color-primary: light-dark(olive, khaki);
  --md-ref-typeface-plain: 'Open Sans', system-ui;
}
```

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/compliance/

# Spec compliance

What the spec checks, ARIA and axe results, Baseline use and size budgets say about md-gb-* components.

## How compliance is measured

The numbers on this page come from the repository itself and are regenerated
by `node scripts/m3/gen-compliance-page.mjs` (`--check` fails when this page
is stale). The M3 spec is downloaded with `npm run m3:update`, split into
**units** (a sentence, list item, table row or image description, each with an
id), and `node scripts/m3/spec-checks.mjs --offline` records what happens to
each one in `.m3-specs/spec-checks/units.json`. Only unit counts and ids are
used here, never spec text.

## Spec units

A unit is **buildable** when the classifier scores it at 0.3 or more
(it describes something a component can do, not a caption or designer advice).
**Tested** units are cited from a `*_test.ts` file under `labs/gb` or
`scripts/m3` (`spec: <unit id>`). **Excluded** units have a written reason in
`scripts/m3/exclusions/*.md` (`spec-exclude:`). **Tracked** units are known
gaps listed in `scripts/m3/CHECKLIST.md` (`spec-gap:`). **Uncovered** units
are buildable, with no status and no test; the target is 0.

15,129 units on 68 pages (components: 10,282, foundations: 2,409, styles: 2,438).
Buildable units that are neither tested nor excluded are covered another way:
a citation outside a test, a token value checked by the generated spec tests,
a unit judged covered by the LLM review, or a unit that is not a requirement
(image descriptions, overview notes). Those statuses are in `units.json` and
`.m3-specs/spec-checks/report.md`.

### Excluded units by reason

An exclusion is only valid when no code could satisfy the unit (designer
advice, app content, platform-only rules). If the library could enforce or
default it, it is tracked as a gap instead.

| Reason (from scripts/m3/exclusions) | Units |
| --- | ---: |
| Figure captions, labels and swatch descriptions with no requirement of their own | 124 |
| Figure and video captions | 62 |
| Figure, video and interaction-style captions and spec-table cells with no requirement of their own | 51 |
| Baseline variants the spec no longer recommends for new designs | 43 |
| Accessibility and interaction design guidance for designers and app authors (contrast, touch targ... | 39 |
| Usage advice and rationale for designers (when to pick a pattern, easing, duration or speed | 39 |
| Figure captions and list labels that name an example in a figure (which component or pattern the ... | 33 |
| Usage advice for designers and content guidance for the app author (what to write, when to choose... | 33 |
| Cards | 32 |
| Layout and spacing design guidance (rulers, grid concepts, component adaptation principles, input... | 29 |
| 73 further reasons | 418 |

## Token audit

`node scripts/m3/audit-gb.mjs --gaps` compares every token declaration in the
`labs/gb` token files with the M3 token database. **Match** means the value
equals the spec; **derived** means it is computed from a matching token;
**drift** differs from the spec; **no spec token** has no counterpart in the
database; **gaps** are tokens the Compose reference uses that no gb
declaration implements.

Overall: 2415 declarations, 1949 match, 23 derived, 10 drift (0 high-confidence), 433 with no spec token, 10 spec tokens not implemented.

| Component | Declarations | Match | Derived | Drift | No spec token | Gaps | Unwired |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `appbar` | 51 | 47 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `badge` | 11 | 10 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `button` | 168 | 157 | 1 | 0 | 10 | 0 | 0 |

### Drift

Each drift is listed with the token file section, the custom property and why
it differs. `E~` is a deliberate `// EDIT:` override of a generated value;
`?~` is an inferred binding that may be wrong (the audit cannot always tell
which spec token a declaration belongs to).

| Component | Section | Property | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `datepicker` | `root` | `--menu-list-item-selected-container-color` | deliberate `// EDIT:` override |
| `list` | `list-tokens.item` | `--container-color` | inferred binding that may be wrong |
| `navdrawer` | `root` | `--container-shape` | deliberate `// EDIT:` override |
| `select` | `outlined` | `--container-color` | deliberate `// EDIT:` override |
| `select` | `outlined-autocomplete` | `--container-color` | deliberate `// EDIT:` override |
| `sheet` | `side` | `--divider-color` | deliberate `// EDIT:` override |
| `sheet` | `side-modal` | `--container-shape` | deliberate `// EDIT:` override |
| `slider` | `root` | `--active-track-inner-corner-size` | inferred binding that may be wrong |
| `slider` | `root` | `--track-shape` | inferred binding that may be wrong |
| `slider` | `disabled` | `--stop-indicator-color` | inferred binding that may be wrong |

## Accessibility

Two central suites render rows in `labs/gb/components/shared/central` and run in a real browser:

- **axe** (`axe_test.ts`): axe-core with no rule disabled, on every subject of
  the central table (`subjects.ts`) plus 29 overlay rows in their
  open state (`axe-helpers.ts`).
- **ARIA 1.3** (`aria_test.ts`): the axe rows plus 34 rows that put
  components in the states ARIA depends on (selected, checked, expanded,
  grouped, with panels, with an error), checked against the WAI-ARIA 1.3 role
  and attribute rules. 27 rows are open overlays, so the checks that
  flip state skip them.

Known gaps are rows with a real violation. They move to `axe_gap.ts` and
`aria_gap.ts` (red on purpose) and are recorded in `AXE_GAPS` and
`ARIA_GAPS`. Today: axe none; ARIA none.
Suite files: `aria_gap.ts`, `aria_test.ts`, `axe_gap.ts`, `axe_test.ts`.

## Baseline

`npm run gb:baseline` maps every CSS feature in the compiled `labs/gb` CSS
to its web-features Baseline status. A feature that is not widely available
must sit inside a matching `@supports` guard or be listed with a reason in
`scripts/gb-baseline-allow.json`; anything else fails the run.

- CSS: 19,541 feature uses in 62 files; 51 features are not widely available, used 754 times (478 guarded, 276 allowed with a reason, **0 unguarded**). Result: passes.
- JavaScript (report only): 31 tracked Web API members in 207 source files; 6 are not widely available, 3 of them with at least one use that is not feature-detected.

## Size budgets

Each component has a Brotli size budget for JavaScript and CSS in
`scripts/size/gb-budgets.json`: the measured size plus 10% headroom, enforced by
the size check. Totals across 37 components: 345,176 bytes of JavaScript and 77,248 bytes of CSS.

# Quick Start

For fast prototyping, use a CDN such as esm.run to load @material/web without installing it.

## CDN

For fast prototyping, use a CDN such as [esm.run](https://esm.run/) to load
`@material/web` without installing it. The M3 Expressive elements are under
`@material/web/labs/gb/`.

### One line

The quickest start is one script. `labs/gb/all.js` defines every `md-gb-*`
element and adopts the M3 styles into the page. It loads every component, so use
it for prototypes only. The import map is optional here; it lets you also import
single files by path later. The script tags have no visible effect, so they are
a plain block (Download & copy in the page tools menu copies them):

```html
<script type="importmap">
  {"imports": {"@material/web/": "https://esm.run/@material/web/"}}
</script>
<script type="module" src="https://esm.run/@material/web/labs/gb/all.js"></script>
```

The same module, imported from a script, with a button that needs no other setup:

**Example: Every element from one import**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">Next</md-gb-button>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import '@material/web/labs/gb/all.js';
```

### Only what you use

To load only the elements a page uses, import each one. The import map resolves
the bare specifiers (it is the only part of this setup that has no visible
effect, so it is a plain block):

```html
<script type="importmap">
  {"imports": {"@material/web/": "https://esm.run/@material/web/"}}
</script>
```

**Example: A button loaded from a module**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">Next</md-gb-button>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import '@material/web/labs/gb/components/button/md-gb-button.js';
import {adoptStyles} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/adopt-styles.js';
import {styles as m3Styles} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/m3.cssresult.js';

adoptStyles(document, [m3Styles]);
```

For production, follow the [install](#install) and [build](#building) steps
below.

## Install

Install Material web components using [npm and node](https://nodejs.org).

```sh
npm install @material/web
```

## Import

Import each element from
`@material/web/labs/gb/components/<component>/md-gb-<component>.js`, and load
the design tokens once with `adoptStyles()`.

**Example: A button and a checkbox imported by path**

*HTML*

```html
<label>
  Material 3 Expressive
  <md-gb-checkbox checked></md-gb-checkbox>
</label>
<md-gb-button color="filled">Next</md-gb-button>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import '@material/web/labs/gb/components/button/md-gb-button.js';
import '@material/web/labs/gb/components/checkbox/md-gb-checkbox.js';
import {adoptStyles} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/adopt-styles.js';
import {styles as m3Styles} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/m3.cssresult.js';

adoptStyles(document, [m3Styles]);
```

## Usage

Use the `<md-gb-component>` tag in HTML markup. Each component page, such as
[Button](/material-web/3.0/components/button/), has more guidance.

**Example: A checkbox with a label and two buttons**

```html
<label>
  Material 3 Expressive
  <md-gb-checkbox checked></md-gb-checkbox>
</label>
<md-gb-button color="outlined">Back</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="filled">Next</md-gb-button>
```

## Building

Bare module specifiers such as `@material/web/...` need a tool to resolve them
until [import maps](https://github.com/WICG/import-maps) are adopted. For a
more in-depth guide, follow
[lit.dev's modern build for production](https://lit.dev/docs/tools/production/#modern-only-build).

### Rollup quick start

[Rollup](https://rollupjs.org/) with a plugin that resolves bare module
specifiers bundles the entrypoint into one file.

```sh
npm install rollup @rollup/plugin-node-resolve
npx rollup -p @rollup/plugin-node-resolve index.js -o bundle.js
```

```html
<script src="./bundle.js"></script>
```

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/migration/

# Migration

Version 3.0 renames most elements from md- to md-gb- and moves them to Material 3 Expressive.

Version 3.0 renames most elements from `md-*` to `md-gb-*` and moves them to
Material 3 Expressive. Many names stay the same, but some attributes and slots
change, and a few components are no longer recommended. This page lists the
changes. The 2.5.0 docs stay on the root of this site.

## Start with the styles

Load the 3.0 design tokens once per document:

**Example: A 3.0 button with the design tokens loaded**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">Save</md-gb-button>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import '@material/web/labs/gb/components/button/md-gb-button.js';
import {adoptStyles} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/adopt-styles.js';
import {styles as m3Styles} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/m3.cssresult.js';

adoptStyles(document, [m3Styles]);
```

Then import each `md-gb-*` element you use from
`@material/web/labs/gb/components/`.

## Element and attribute map

Element names change as listed below. Where the table says "dropped", the 2.5.0
attribute has no 3.0 counterpart and you can remove it.

| 2.5.0 | 3.0 | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `md-filled-button` | `md-gb-button` | `color="filled"` |
| `md-elevated-button` | `md-gb-button` | `color="elevated"` |
| `md-filled-tonal-button` | `md-gb-button` | `color="tonal"` |
| `md-outlined-button` | `md-gb-button` | `color="outlined"` |
| `md-text-button` | `md-gb-button` | `color="text"` |
| `md-icon-button` | `md-gb-icon-button` | `color="standard"`; `toggle` and `flip-icon-in-rtl` dropped |
| `md-filled-icon-button` | `md-gb-icon-button` | `color="filled"` |
| `md-filled-tonal-icon-button` | `md-gb-icon-button` | `color="tonal"` |
| `md-outlined-icon-button` | `md-gb-icon-button` | `color="outlined"` |
| `md-fab`, `md-branded-fab` | `md-gb-fab` | `variant` becomes `color` (`primary-container`, `secondary-container`, `tertiary-container`); `size="large"` becomes `size="lg"`; `label` becomes text content; `size`, `lowered` and `variant` dropped |
| `md-checkbox` | `md-gb-checkbox` | `touch-target` dropped |
| `md-radio` | `md-gb-radio` | `touch-target` dropped |
| `md-switch` | `md-gb-switch` | none |
| `md-slider` | `md-gb-slider` | `aria-*` label and value text attributes renamed (see below) |
| `md-divider` | `md-gb-divider` | `inset`, `inset-start` and `inset-end` dropped |
| `md-list`, `md-list-item` | `md-gb-list`, `md-gb-list-item` | `start` slot becomes `leading`, `end` becomes `trailing`, `trailing-supporting-text` becomes `trailing-text`; `headline` slot is unwrapped |
| `md-menu`, `md-menu-item` | `md-gb-menu`, `md-gb-menu-item` | `positioning`, `menu-corner` and `anchor-corner` dropped on `md-gb-menu`; the same slot changes as lists |
| `md-linear-progress` | `md-gb-progress` | `indeterminate`, `buffer` and `four-color` dropped |
| `md-circular-progress` | `md-gb-progress circular` | `indeterminate` and `four-color` dropped |
| `md-filled-text-field` | `md-gb-text-field` | none (filled is the default) |
| `md-outlined-text-field` | `md-gb-text-field` | `variant="outlined"` |
| `md-filled-select` | `md-gb-select` | `menu-positioning`, `clamp-menu-width`, `menu-align` and `quick` dropped |
| `md-outlined-select` | `md-gb-select` | `variant="outlined"`, same drops as above |
| `md-select-option` | `md-gb-select-option` | `headline` slot is unwrapped; `start` becomes `leading`, `end` becomes `trailing` |
| `md-dialog` | `md-gb-dialog` | the `content` slot is removed, so the content goes in the default slot |
| `md-tabs` | `md-gb-tabs` | `variant="secondary"` when it holds secondary tabs; `auto-activate` and `active-tab-index` dropped |
| `md-primary-tab`, `md-secondary-tab` | `md-gb-tab` | the label goes in `slot="label"`; `inline-icon`, `has-icon`, `active` and `icon-only` dropped |
| `md-chip-set` | `md-gb-chip-set` | none |
| `md-assist-chip` | `md-gb-chip` | `color="elevated"` if it was `elevated`; `label` becomes text content |
| `md-filter-chip` | `md-gb-chip` | `type="filter"`; same color rule |
| `md-input-chip` | `md-gb-chip` | `type="input"` with `removable` |
| `md-suggestion-chip` | `md-gb-chip` | `type="suggestion"`; same color rule |
| `md-icon` | `md-gb-icon` | inside a button, icon button, FAB or tab, the `slot="icon"` is removed and the icon goes in DOM order |

If the icon is not an `md-icon` (for example an inline SVG), wrap it in
`md-gb-icon`.

## Attributes to rename by hand

Converting the elements does not rename every attribute. Update these by hand:

- `md-gb-slider`: `aria-label-start` becomes `label-start`, `aria-label-end`
  becomes `label-end`, `aria-valuetext-start` becomes `valuetext-start`, and
  `aria-valuetext-end` becomes `valuetext-end`. The `aria-` prefix is reserved
  for ARIA attributes, so the 3.0 names do not use it. `value-label-start` and
  `value-label-end` keep their names.
- `md-gb-dialog`: `full-screen` applies only on compact windows. Above that,
  the dialog is a basic dialog with the same slots. Add `always-full-screen` to
  keep the full-screen layout at every window size. The 2.5.0 `md-dialog` has
  no full-screen attribute, so this is new in 3.0.

## Recommendations that changed

The Expressive spec no longer recommends some 2.5.0 patterns. The components
remain available, but for new work use the replacement below.

- **Segmented buttons** are replaced by a connected button group:
  `md-gb-button-group variant="connected"`.
- **Navigation drawer** is replaced by an expanded navigation rail:
  `md-gb-nav-rail` with `expanded`. Use `modal` when it overlays content.
- **Bottom app bar** is replaced by a docked toolbar: `md-gb-toolbar docked`.
- **Medium and large app bars** are replaced by medium and large flexible app
  bars: `md-gb-app-bar size="md"` and `size="lg"`.
- **Small FABs and surface-colored FABs** are replaced by the default FAB size
  and the container colors (`primary-container`, `secondary-container`,
  `tertiary-container`).

## Watch out for

- Chips and FABs no longer take their text from a `label` attribute. Put the
  text in the element instead, as the table shows.
- An `md-gb-*` element that is not imported is not upgraded, so it renders as
  an unknown element.
- Selectors, queries and tests that use the old `md-*` tag names need the new
  names too.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/roadmap/

# Roadmap

This roadmap describes current, future, and past goals for Material Web Components.

## Current

**Version 3.0 (`labs/gb`) is the M3 Expressive implementation of MWC.** It adds
Expressive components (such as the button group, split button, FAB menu,
carousel, loading indicator, and toolbar), dynamic color, the Expressive shape,
type, and motion systems, WAI-ARIA 1.3 conformance, and Web Platform Baseline
fallbacks. Version 2.5.0 remains in
[maintenance mode](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/discussions/5642).

## Future

**Note: No future work is planned while MWC is in
[maintenance mode](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/discussions/5642).**
These roadmap items represent what used to be planned.

### New components

Version 3.0 builds every component in the list 2.5.0 planned except these:

*   Autocomplete
*   Banner
*   Data table

The badge, bottom sheet, card, date and time pickers, navigation bar, drawer
and rail, search, segmented button, snackbar, tooltip and top app bar are in
`labs/gb`. The toolbar replaces the bottom app bar in M3 Expressive.

### Expand Material Design tokens

Version 3.0 has the shape and motion system tokens.

We also want to make it easier to use Material Design tokens, such as applying
Material typescale, shape, and color to your own components.

### Density and spacing tokens

Density allows components to take up less vertical space for larger displays.
While we have some spacing tokens already, we need a comprehensive spacing
system to fully support density across components.

### Create TSX components

[TSX](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/jsx.html) is a popular
language extension for frameworks like [React](https://reactjs.org/). We want to
make it easier and more seamless to use Material Web Components in TSX.

### Explore Material Design layouts

Components are only part of the story to build fully expressive Material Design
applications. We want to explore ways to support building applications that
follow
[Material's layout patterns](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/understanding-layout/overview).

## Past

### Follow accessibility best practices

*Completed in Q1 2024*

Everyone should be able to access and enjoy the web. We want our components to
help others build accessible experiences. The following screen readers are fully
supported:

*   VoiceOver
*   Talkback
*   ChromeVox
*   JAWS
*   NVDA

### Cards and more

    *   ✅
        [Card preview](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/c9360e2310dee2896592649f8a8f9b03e2737bf2/labs/card)
*   Features
    *   🟡 Prevent event default behavior
        *   *We fixed lots of bugs, but there's still ways we can improve.*
    *   ✅
        [Size tracking](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/c9360e2310dee2896592649f8a8f9b03e2737bf2/docs/size.md)
    *   ✅ [Docs and examples](https://material-web.dev/)

### Material 1.0

*Completed in Q3 2023*

*   Features
    *   ✅ Color theming
    *   ✅ Typography theming
*   Components
    *   ✅ Button
    *   ✅ FAB
    *   ✅ Icon button

# Support

Version 3.0 targets Baseline widely available: the web platform features it uses have worked in all major browsers for at least 30 months.

## Browsers

Version 3.0 targets **Baseline widely available**: the web platform features it
uses have worked in all major browsers for at least 30 months. Newer features
(such as `corner-shape` or `light-dark()`) are only used behind `@supports`
guards or with a fallback, so components stay usable in older engines. The
repository checks this with `npm run gb:baseline`. See
[Browser support](/material-web/3.0/about/browser-support/) for the minimum versions.

## FAQ

### How do I change the color of a button?

Components read `--md-sys-color-*` tokens. Override the key color a component
uses on the element or a class. Buttons use `primary`, and the states (hover,
focus, pressed) are derived from it.

**Example: A button that uses the error colors**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button class="danger" color="filled">Delete</md-gb-button>
```

*CSS*

```css
md-gb-button.danger {
  --md-sys-color-primary: var(--md-sys-color-error);
  --md-sys-color-on-primary: var(--md-sys-color-on-error);
}
```

### Why doesn't `prefers-color-scheme: dark` switch the theme?

The tokens use `light-dark()`, so they follow the `color-scheme` property. Set
it to follow the system, or force a scheme on any subtree.

**Example: A subtree that is always dark**

*HTML*

```html
<div class="always-dark">
  <md-gb-button color="filled">Save</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="outlined">Cancel</md-gb-button>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
:root {
  color-scheme: light dark;
}

.always-dark {
  padding: 16px;
  color-scheme: dark;
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}
```

### How do I generate my own `--md-sys-color-*` tokens?

Generate a theme from a source color at runtime, or export a stylesheet.

**Example: A button themed from a source color**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">Save</md-gb-button>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import {applyTheme} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/color/dynamic-color.js';

applyTheme(document, {source: '#006a6a'});
```

You can also design a scheme with the
[Material Theme Builder Figma plugin](https://www.figma.com/community/plugin/1034969338659738588/Material-Theme-Builder).
See [Color](/material-web/3.0/styles/color/).

### How do I style an element inside another component?

Use [CSS `::part()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/::part).
The parts of each component are listed under its CSS parts in the API
reference.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/size/

# Bundle Sizes

Every md-gb- component is checked against a Brotli-compressed size budget for its JavaScript and CSS (the measured size plus 10% headroom), defined in scripts/size/gb-budgets.json.

Every `md-gb-*` component is checked against a Brotli-compressed size budget
for its JavaScript and CSS (the measured size plus 10% headroom), defined in
`scripts/size/gb-budgets.json`. For example, `md-gb-button` stays within about
4.8 KB of JavaScript and 1.5 KB of CSS, and `md-gb-badge` within about 1 KB and
0.5 KB. Import only the components you use to keep your bundle small.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/browser-support/

# Browser support

Version 3.0 only uses web platform features that are Baseline widely available.

## Targets

Version 3.0 only uses web platform features that are Baseline widely available.
The oldest browsers the build checks against are:

| Browser    | Minimum version |
| ---------- | --------------- |
| Chrome     | 124             |
| Edge       | 124             |
| Firefox    | 125             |
| Safari     | 17.4            |
| iOS Safari | 17.4            |

`node scripts/gb-css-validate.mjs` prints these values, and the CSS is compiled
against them. They move as Baseline moves, so rerun the script to see the
current numbers.

## Features behind a fallback

Newer features are either guarded with `@supports` or allowed to be ignored
where a browser lacks them. The exceptions are listed, with the reason for each,
in `scripts/gb-baseline-allow.json`. In short:

- `field-sizing`: a textarea keeps its fixed rows and scrolls.
- `interpolate-size`: size changes to intrinsic keywords jump instead of
  animating.
- `starting-style`: an element appears without its enter transition.
- `transition-behavior`: discrete properties change at once.
- `scrollbar-gutter`: no reserved gutter, so a small layout shift when a
  scrollbar appears.
- `overscroll-behavior`: scroll chaining at the edge is not contained.
- `view-transitions`: the view transition styles never match.
- `container-scroll-state-queries`: the app bar does not switch to its stuck
  look.
- `forced-colors`: ignored where forced colors mode does not exist (Safari).

Guard your own newer CSS the same way, so older browsers keep a usable
fallback:

**Example: A textarea that grows with its content where supported**

*HTML*

```html
<textarea rows="2" aria-label="Message">Type here and add lines.</textarea>
```

*CSS*

```css
@supports (field-sizing: content) {
  textarea {
    field-sizing: content;
  }
}
```

## Check your own app

Test on the oldest version of each browser in the table, not only the current
release. To see which Baseline features the repository uses, run
`npm run gb:baseline`.

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/about/ai-agents/

# AI agents

labs/gb/skill/ is a Claude Code skill named md-gb.

## What the skill is

`labs/gb/skill/` is a Claude Code skill named `md-gb`. It teaches an agent which
`md-gb-*` element to pick, and each element's attributes, properties, slots,
events, CSS parts, custom properties, and what the app must provide itself. It
is one `SKILL.md` plus a reference file per component.

## Install it

Copy the folder into your skills directory. For all of your projects:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/md-gb
cp -r labs/gb/skill/. ~/.claude/skills/md-gb/
```

To share it with one repository, copy it to `.claude/skills/md-gb/` in that
repository instead. Claude Code loads it when you write HTML, Lit templates, or
CSS that use `md-gb-*` elements.

### Install it from this site

Without a checkout, the skill files are published at `/material-web/3.0/skill/`. The page tools
button (bottom end of every page) opens Download & copy, which has Copy agent
prompt: paste it into your agent and it
creates the skills folder, downloads `SKILL.md` and every `reference/*.md` file
listed in `/material-web/3.0/skill/index.json`, installs `@material/web`, and checks the
result.

The same menu downloads the whole API as one `custom-elements.json` (a
[Custom Elements Manifest](https://github.com/webcomponents/custom-elements-manifest)
of every element), and `/material-web/3.0/llms.txt` indexes the docs as Markdown.

## Keep it current

The skill is generated from the component sources and `scripts/m3/CHECKLIST.md`.
Do not edit it by hand. To regenerate it, run:

```sh
node scripts/m3/gen-agent-skill.mjs
```

Run the same command with `--check` to fail when the output is stale. After you
change a component, regenerate the skill and copy it again, because an installed
copy does not update itself.

## Browser agents (WebMCP)

On every page of these docs, a browser that supports
[WebMCP](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/) lets its agent search and
read the docs through five read-only tools. Nothing is registered in other
browsers. The tools use the same search as the Cmd+K dialog, and every page is
also available as Markdown at its URL plus `.md`.

- `search_docs` finds sections by keywords: `{query, limit?}`.
- `get_page` returns a page or one section as Markdown: `{path, section?}`.
- `list_pages` lists the pages, optionally of one section: `{section?}`.
- `get_component_api` returns the properties, slots, events, methods, CSS parts
  and custom properties of an element: `{tag}`.
- `get_current_page` describes the page the user is on, with its outline.

An agent calls them through the browser. This demo calls the same functions the
page registers (`window.gbDocsTools`) and shows the first three results of a
search.

**Example: Search result of the WebMCP tool**

*HTML*

```html
<output id="result">Searching…</output>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
// The page registers the tools once its script has loaded.
const tools = await new Promise<any>((resolve) => {
  const check = () => {
    const found = (parent as any).gbDocsTools;
    if (found) resolve(found);
    else setTimeout(check, 50);
  };
  check();
});
const out = document.querySelector('#result')!;
const found = await tools.search_docs({query: 'split button menu', limit: 3});
out.textContent = found.results.map((r: any) => `${r.heading}: ${r.url}`).join('\n');
```

## Watch out

- The skill covers the `md-gb-*` elements of 3.0 only. For 2.5.0 `md-*`
  elements, use the v2.5.0 documentation.
- Each reference file lists what the app must provide itself. Check those
  lines before you rely on the agent's markup.
