```css
  border-end-end-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md-end-end);
  border-end-start-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md-end-start);
}
```

Set `data-shape-family="cut"` on `<html>` to cut corners in browsers that
support `corner-shape`.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/elevation/

# Elevation

Elevation is the distance between two surfaces on the z-axis.

Elevation is the distance between two surfaces on the z-axis. It tells people
which surface sits in front, which one sits behind, and which one is the
current focus. Every surface and component has an elevation, so keep the
number of levels small.

## Levels

There are six levels, 0 to 5. Each one has a token:

- `--md-sys-elevation-shadow-0` (no shadow) to `--md-sys-elevation-shadow-5`

Levels 0 to 3 are for resting components. Levels 4 and 5 are for interaction
states, such as hover and drag. Components raise by one level when hovered or
focused: a FAB goes from level 3 to level 4, and a filled button goes from
level 0 to level 1.

The tokens are defined in `labs/gb/styles/elevation/md-elevation-tokens.scss`.
Shadow colors come from `--md-sys-color-shadow`, so they adapt to the color
scheme.

## Resting levels

Each component has a fixed resting level. Do not change it on your own.

| Level | Components |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Buttons (filled, tonal, outlined), button group, split button, icon buttons, chips, segmented button, cards (filled, outlined), carousel, list, navigation rail, tabs, slider, app bar (not scrolled), full-screen dialog, docked side sheet |
| 1 | Elevated button, elevated card, elevated chip, modal navigation drawer, modal bottom sheet, modal side sheet |
| 2 | Menu, navigation bar, rich tooltip |
| 3 | FAB (small, standard and extended), FAB menu close button, modal dialog, date picker, time picker, floating toolbar, full-screen dialog above compact windows (where it is a basic dialog) |

The search bar also rests at level 0 without a shadow, but it shows its level
by tone (see below).

## Showing elevation with tone

Elevation can be shown with a tonal surface color instead of a shadow. Two
components do this in gb:

- **Search bar**: no shadow. Its container uses `surface-container-high`, the
  tone for level 3.
- **App bar when scrolled**: no drop shadow. Its container changes from
  `surface` to `surface-container`, the tone for level 2, so it separates from
  the content under it.

Use tone when a surface only needs to be told apart from what is behind it.

## Shadows

Shadows are for two cases only: to protect an element on a busy or patterned
background, and to encourage interaction, such as a card that lifts on hover.
Otherwise rely on the tonal difference between surfaces, which is the default.
A small, sharp shadow means the surface is close to the one behind it. A larger,
softer shadow means more distance.

## Code sample

**Example: A note card that lifts from level 1 to level 2 on hover**

*HTML*

```html
<div class="note-card">Pick up milk</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.note-card {
  padding: 24px 32px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
  box-shadow: var(--md-sys-elevation-shadow-1);
  transition: box-shadow var(--md-sys-motion-spring-fast-effects-duration)
    var(--md-sys-motion-spring-fast-effects);
}

.note-card:hover {
  box-shadow: var(--md-sys-elevation-shadow-2);
}
```

## What to watch out for

- Do not hard-code shadow values. Use the level tokens so a change to the
  scale reaches every surface.
- Avoid changing the default elevation of a component. When an interaction such
  as hover changes it, make the change the same for every similar component.
- Give floating elements enough contrast with the surface beneath them, either
  through the shadow or through a tone difference.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/icons/

# Icons

md-gb-icon shows a Material Symbols icon.

`md-gb-icon` shows a Material Symbols icon. Its content is the ligature name
of the symbol, such as `home`. Find names and previews at
[fonts.google.com/icons](https://fonts.google.com/icons). Symbols come in three
styles: outlined, rounded and sharp.

The element is a thin wrapper over the font. It reads its size, color and font
variation settings from custom properties.

## Loading the font

The element's default font family is `Material Symbols`. The Google Fonts
family for the outlined style is `Material Symbols Outlined`, so set
`--md-icon-font` to the family you load:

**Example: An icon in the outlined Material Symbols family**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-icon>home</md-gb-icon>
```

*CSS*

```css
:root {
  --md-icon-font: 'Material Symbols Outlined';
}
```

Load the font once in the page head. Request only the axes you use; add `GRAD`
to use `--md-icon-grad`.

**Example: An icon with the font loaded by a link tag**

```html
<link rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Material+Symbols+Outlined:opsz,wght,FILL,GRAD@20..48,100..700,0..1,-25..200&display=block">
<md-gb-icon>home</md-gb-icon>
```

## Size and color

- `--md-icon-size` sets the size. The default is `24px`. Symbols support 20dp,
  24dp, 40dp and 48dp; use 20dp for dense layouts and 40dp or 48dp for display
  use.
- `--md-icon-color` sets the color. The default is `currentColor`.
- The optical size follows the icon size automatically, so a larger icon gets a
  matching optical size. Set `--md-icon-opsz` only to override it.

## Variable font axes

Each style has four axes. The element exposes them as custom properties:

| Property | Axis | Default | Range | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--md-icon-wght` | Weight | `400` | 100 to 700 | 400 is the 2dp stroke for standard icons. Use at least 200 at 24dp. |
| `--md-icon-fill` | Fill | `0` | 0 to 1 | 1 is filled, 0 is outlined. The change animates. |
| `--md-icon-grad` | Grade | `0` | Negative to positive | Gb sets `-25` when the color scheme is dark, where icons are light on dark. Positive values add emphasis. |
| `--md-icon-opsz` | Optical size | follows size | 20 to 48dp | Not set by default. |

Fill is the usual way to show a selected state. Use the outlined symbol when
the item is unselected and the filled one when it is selected.

## Baseline next to text

Symbols next to text need a baseline shift to line up. The element already
applies `vertical-align: -0.115em` (of its own size), which lowers the icon so
it lines up with the text beside it: about 2.8px at 24dp. Keep that `vertical-align` if you override the
style, or the icon will look too high.

## Targets

A 24dp icon needs a 48dp target by default. A 20dp icon can use a 40dp target
when a mouse and keyboard are the main input. `md-gb-icon-button` keeps a 48dp
minimum target (`--target-size`) even when the icon inside is smaller, so use it
rather than a bare icon in a clickable element.

## Accessibility

- An icon is decorative unless it has a label. `md-gb-icon` sets
  `aria-hidden="true"` by default, so screen readers skip it. That is correct
  when the text beside the icon already says what it means.
- For an icon-only control, put the accessible name on the control with
  `aria-label`, and leave the icon hidden. Only set `aria-hidden="false"` on an
  icon that must be announced on its own.
- Add a text label when the symbol is abstract, complex, or carries a key
  action. A symbol shown below 20dp should have one too.

## Examples

Change an axis or the size with the custom properties.

**Example: A default icon, a filled icon and a large bold icon**

```html
<md-gb-icon>home</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-fill: 1">home</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-size: 40px; --md-icon-wght: 500">star</md-gb-icon>
```

Put the accessible name on the control, not on the icon.

**Example: An icon-only button with an accessible name**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button aria-label="Favorite">
  <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

## What to watch out for

- An icon with no font loaded shows the ligature text, such as `favorite`, not
  a symbol. Load the font before the page relies on it.
- Do not mix styles in one icon set. Pick outlined, rounded or sharp for the
  whole product.
- Do not use the lightest weight for standard 24dp icons.
- Keep the icon's content inside the 20dp live area of the 24dp grid. It can
  reach into the 2dp padding for extra weight, but never past the 24dp edge.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/material-symbols/

# Material Symbols

md-gb-icon axes: optical size, weight, fill and grade.

Each variable font axis of `md-gb-icon` is a custom property. See
[Icons](/material-web/3.0/styles/icons/) for loading the font and the defaults.

**Example: An icon imported by path**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-icon>star</md-gb-icon>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/icon/md-gb-icon.js';
```

## Optical sizes

The optical size follows `--md-icon-size`, which supports 20, 24, 40 and 48px.

**Example: Icons at 20, 24, 40 and 48 pixels**

```html
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-size: 20px">star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon>star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-size: 40px">star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-size: 48px">star</md-gb-icon>
```

## Weights

`--md-icon-wght` runs from 100 to 700.

**Example: Icons at weights 200, 400 and 700**

```html
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-wght: 200">star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon>star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-wght: 700">star</md-gb-icon>
```

## Fill

`--md-icon-fill` is 0 (outlined) or 1 (filled), and the change animates.

**Example: An outlined and a filled icon**

```html
<md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-fill: 1">favorite</md-gb-icon>
```

## Grades

`--md-icon-grad` adds emphasis when positive. It needs `GRAD` in the font
request.

**Example: Icons at grades -25, 0 and 200**

```html
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-grad: -25">star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon>star</md-gb-icon>
<md-gb-icon style="--md-icon-grad: 200">star</md-gb-icon>
```

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/motion/

# Motion

Motion makes a UI expressive and easy to follow: springs for physics, easing and duration tokens, and transition patterns.

## Overview

Material 3 Expressive uses a physics-based motion system. Springs drive
spatial motion (position, size, rotation, corner shape) and effects springs
drive properties that must not overshoot, like color and opacity. One spring
can serve transitions, button effects and gestures, which keeps the product
feeling consistent. Each spring is exposed as a CSS `linear()` easing with a
matching duration, so a transition can use it directly.

### Motion schemes

- **Expressive** is the default. Use it for most situations, especially hero
  moments and key interactions. Spatial springs overshoot and bounce into
  place.
- **Standard** moves with minimal bounce and suits utilitarian products. Apply
  it to a subtree with the `md-motion-standard` class.

The spec's three levels of customization map to CSS like this:

1. Use a default scheme: do nothing (Expressive), or add `md-motion-standard`.
2. Create a custom scheme: override the spring custom properties in your own
   `:root` rule.
3. Swap the scheme for one element: put `md-motion-standard` on that element.

**Example: A button in a subtree that uses the standard motion scheme**

```html
<div class="md-motion-standard">
  <md-gb-button color="filled">Save</md-gb-button>
</div>
```

### Spring tokens

Spring tokens follow `--md-sys-motion-spring-<speed>-<spatial|effects>`, with
`fast`, `default` and `slow` speeds. Each has a `-duration` token:

**Example: A panel that slides with the default spatial spring**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="slide" color="filled">Slide</md-gb-button>
<div id="panel" class="panel">Panel</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.panel {
  margin-block-start: 16px;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  inline-size: fit-content;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container);
  transition: translate var(--md-sys-motion-spring-default-spatial-duration)
    var(--md-sys-motion-spring-default-spatial);
}

.panel.moved {
  translate: 160px 0;
}
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#slide').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#panel').classList.toggle('moved');
});
```

| Spring  | Expressive | Standard |
| ------- | ---------- | -------- |
| Spatial fast / default / slow | 350 / 420 / 570ms | 160 / 220 / 340ms |
| Effects fast / default / slow | 140 / 220 / 300ms | 140 / 220 / 300ms |

Springs handle interruption and retargeting well, so prefer them. For
animations without interruptions or gestures you can use the curve fallback:
`--md-sys-motion-curve-<speed>-<spatial|effects>` (a `cubic-bezier()`) with
`--md-sys-motion-curve-<speed>-<spatial|effects>-duration`. They carry the
values from the spec's web conversion table.

### Reduced motion

Reduced motion is on when the platform asks for it
(`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`) or inside an element with the
`md-motion-reduced` class (spatial motion is off there, fades stay). The spatial springs then become instant (0ms) and
the effects springs keep their timing. People still see fades and color
changes, but not sliding, scaling, parallax or shape morphing.

Do not build your own motion gate. Read the durations from the tokens so the
scheme and reduced motion apply without extra code.

### Gestures

A gesture has to keep its momentum: a fling that lets go at 2000px/s must not
restart from rest, and a settle that is aimed at a new target half way must
not jump. A CSS transition cannot do either, so `labs/gb` also has the same
springs as physics, in `labs/gb/components/shared/spring.ts`. `readSpring()`
returns the damping ratio and stiffness of a spring token (Expressive or
Standard, whichever applies to the element), and `Spring` solves it in closed
form and samples it every animation frame:

**Example: A panel driven by a spring with a release velocity**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="fling" color="filled">Fling</md-gb-button>
<div id="panel" class="panel">Panel</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.panel {
  margin-block-start: 16px;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  inline-size: fit-content;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container);
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {
  readSpring,
  Spring,
} from '@material/web/labs/gb/components/shared/spring.js';

const panel = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#panel')!;
const spring = new Spring({
  spec: readSpring(panel, 'default-spatial'),
  onFrame: (x) => (panel.style.translate = `${x}px`),
});
document.querySelector('#fling')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
  spring.start(0, 240, 1500); // from and to in px, release velocity in px/s
  setTimeout(() => spring.retarget(120), 150); // keeps position and velocity
});
```

Under reduced motion the spring jumps to its target and rests at once.
`DragSettleController` (the drag-and-settle behavior behind swipe to reveal,
drawers, sheets and pane handles) does this for you when you pass `onFrame`: the settle starts at the release
position with the release velocity, and the surface follows the frames with no
CSS transition on the moved property. Without `onFrame` it keeps the CSS
transition of the spring token.

### Shape morphing

Buttons and icon buttons (`md-gb-button`, `md-gb-icon-button`) morph their
shape when pressed and when selected. That is spatial motion, so reduced
motion turns it off and keeps the color change.

### Component authors

Components that script their motion use the helpers in
`labs/gb/components/shared/motion.ts`:

- `springDuration(element, speed, kind)` returns the duration of a spring in
  milliseconds, already 0 for spatial springs when motion is reduced.
- `isReducedMotion(element)` and `onReducedMotionChange(...)` follow the
  setting, including inside `.md-motion-reduced`.
- `waitForMotion(...)` resolves when the animations end or when its timeout
  runs out, so waiting never hangs. `waitForDuration(ms, signal)` is the
  plain timed wait.

### Not covered

- The spec's Compose APIs (`MotionScheme` objects, a `CompositionLocal` per
  element) have no web equivalent. The CSS steps above replace them.
- Springs are pre-sampled into `linear()` easings for transitions. A
  transition cannot take a starting velocity, so gestures use the solver
  described in [Gestures](#gestures) instead.

## Easing and duration

M3 Expressive moves components to springs, but transitions still use the
easing and duration system, and so can products that have not migrated yet.
The spec offers a starting pair for each case:

| Easing token | Duration token | Use it to |
| ------------ | -------------- | --------- |
| `emphasized` | `long2` (500ms) | Begin and end on screen |
| `emphasized-decelerate` | `medium4` (400ms) | Enter the screen |
| `emphasized-accelerate` | `short4` (200ms) | Exit the screen |
| `standard` | `medium2` (300ms) | Begin and end on screen, small utility transitions |
| `standard-decelerate` | `medium1` (250ms) | Enter the screen |
| `standard-accelerate` | `short4` (200ms) | Exit the screen |

**Example: A sheet that enters with the emphasized decelerate easing**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="enter" color="filled">Enter</md-gb-button>
<div id="sheet" class="sheet">Sheet</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.sheet {
  margin-block-start: 16px;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  inline-size: fit-content;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-tertiary-container);
  transition: translate var(--md-sys-motion-duration-medium4)
    var(--md-sys-motion-easing-emphasized-decelerate);
}

.sheet.moved {
  translate: 160px 0;
}
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#enter').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#sheet').classList.toggle('moved');
});
```

Tokens are `--md-sys-motion-easing-<set>[-accelerate|-decelerate]` and
`--md-sys-motion-duration-<short|medium|long|extra-long><1-4>`. Short is
50 to 200ms, medium 250 to 400ms, long 450 to 600ms and extra long 700 to
1000ms, in steps of 50ms (extra long in steps of 100ms).

How to choose:

- **Easing set.** Emphasized for most transitions, with its decelerate and
  accelerate variants for entering and exiting. Standard for small, quick,
  utility transitions.
- **Easing type.** Plain for elements that begin and end on screen,
  decelerate when entering, accelerate when leaving for good. An element that
  leaves temporarily (a drawer that comes back) uses the plain curve.
- **Duration.** Bigger transitions and larger distances take longer. Exits
  are shorter than enters, because the user's attention has already moved on.

Reduced motion does not change these tokens. Gate sliding and scaling yourself
(the transition helpers below do) or use the spring tokens, which follow the
setting.

Not covered: the spec's emphasized easing is a path curve. On the web
`--md-sys-motion-easing-emphasized` is the single `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`
approximation, so it is equal to `standard`.

## Transitions

A transition is a short animation that connects elements or full-screen views
and shows how they relate. The spec defines six patterns and notes that they
still use the easing and duration tokens above, not springs. `labs/gb`
implements them in `styles/motion/transitions/` with the View Transitions API,
and falls back to the Web Animations API when the browser lacks it (or when you
pass `viewTransition: false`).

The pattern styles are part of `m3Styles` (see
[Quick Start](/material-web/3.0/about/quick-start/#import)). Adopt them on the document,
because `::view-transition-*` rules only work there. The helpers come from
`@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js`.

Every helper takes `update`, a function that changes the DOM to the new state,
and returns a promise that resolves when the motion ends. Common options:
`reducedMotion`, `viewTransition`, `duration` and `easing`. The timings come
from `--md-transition-*` custom properties (for example
`--md-transition-shared-axis-duration`), so you can restyle a pattern in CSS.

### Container transform

For an element that becomes a new surface and shows more detail: a card that
opens a details page, a FAB that opens a sheet, a search box, a list item.
The container's bounds, corner radius and color morph while its content fades
through (Emphasized, 500ms by default). `from` and `to` can be the same element
or different ones. Swap them to collapse back.

**Example: A card that becomes a details surface and collapses back**

*HTML*

```html
<div id="card" class="surface card">
  Inbox
  <md-gb-button id="open">Open</md-gb-button>
</div>
<div id="detail" class="surface detail" hidden>
  Inbox details
  <md-gb-button id="close">Close</md-gb-button>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.surface {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 16px;
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-lg);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-high);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}

.detail {
  min-block-size: 140px;
  background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-primary-container);
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {containerTransform} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const card = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#card')!;
const detail = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#detail')!;

document.querySelector('#open')!.addEventListener('click', () =>
  containerTransform(card, () => detail, {
    update: () => {
      card.hidden = true;
      detail.hidden = false;
    },
  }),
);
// Collapse: the opened element is `from`, the card is `to`.
document.querySelector('#close')!.addEventListener('click', () =>
  containerTransform(detail, card, {
    update: () => {
      detail.hidden = true;
      card.hidden = false;
    },
  }),
);
```

### Forward and backward

For screens at consecutive levels of hierarchy, like an inbox and a message.
The screens slide along the x axis as they fade (`axis: 'y'` and `'z'` are
available too). Always pair `forward` with `backward` when the user goes back,
so the direction stays consistent.

**Example: An inbox and a message with forward and backward motion**

*HTML*

```html
<div id="stage" class="stage">
  <section id="inbox">
    <p>Inbox</p>
    <md-gb-button id="forward" color="filled">Open message</md-gb-button>
  </section>
  <section id="thread" hidden>
    <p>Message</p>
    <md-gb-button id="backward">Back</md-gb-button>
  </section>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.stage {
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-lg);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {sharedAxis} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const stage = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#stage')!;
const inbox = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#inbox')!;
const thread = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#thread')!;

document.querySelector('#forward')!.addEventListener('click', () =>
  sharedAxis(
    'forward',
    () => {
      inbox.hidden = true;
      thread.hidden = false;
    },
    {scope: stage},
  ),
);
document.querySelector('#backward')!.addEventListener('click', () =>
  sharedAxis(
    'backward',
    () => {
      thread.hidden = true;
      inbox.hidden = false;
    },
    {scope: stage},
  ),
);
```

`scope` limits the motion to one region. Without it the whole page animates.

### Lateral

For peers at the same level, like tabs or the photos in an album. Both pages
slide the full width together. The direction is `next` or `previous` and
follows the writing direction (RTL is handled).

**Example: Two peer pages that slide sideways**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="next" color="tonal">Next photo</md-gb-button>
<div id="panels" class="panels">
  <p id="photo">Photo 1</p>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.panels {
  margin-block-start: 16px;
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-lg);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {lateral} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const panels = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#panels')!;
const photo = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#photo')!;
let index = 1;

document.querySelector('#next')!.addEventListener('click', () =>
  lateral('next', () => (photo.textContent = `Photo ${++index}`), {
    scope: panels,
  }),
);
```

### Top level

For switching between top-level destinations (navigation bar, rail or drawer).
The old screen quickly fades out, then the new one fades in, so they never
overlap. These destinations are not related spatially, so there is no
directional slide; the new screen only scales up slightly as it fades in.

**Example: Switching between top-level destinations**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="library" color="tonal">Library</md-gb-button>
<main id="main" class="main">
  <p id="title">Home</p>
</main>
```

*CSS*

```css
.main {
  margin-block-start: 16px;
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-lg);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {fadeThrough} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const main = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#main')!;
const title = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#title')!;

document.querySelector('#library')!.addEventListener('click', () =>
  fadeThrough(() => (title.textContent = 'Library'), {scope: main}),
);
```

### Enter and exit

For introducing or removing a component. `enter(element, options)` shows it
(`hidden = false`) and `exit(element, options)` animates it away, then you hide
or remove it. Both resolve when the animation ends.

- **Within screen bounds** (menus, dialogs, snackbars, tooltips, FABs). The
  default `style: 'expand'` is the Android style: the component expands away
  from the nearest screen edge, without scale. `style: 'scale'` is the iOS
  style (scale in, fade out). Pick the edge with `origin`.
- **Beyond screen bounds** (drawers, sheets, banners, navigation). `style:
  'slide'` slides the component on and off from its edge. Set `temporary: true`
  for something that comes back, like a drawer, so it exits with the plain
  Emphasized curve instead of the accelerate one.

**Example: A menu that expands downwards and a drawer that slides in**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="toggle-menu" color="tonal">Menu</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button id="toggle-drawer" color="tonal">Drawer</md-gb-button>
<ul id="menu" class="panel" hidden>
  <li>Copy</li>
  <li>Paste</li>
</ul>
<nav id="drawer" class="panel drawer" aria-label="Sections" hidden>Inbox</nav>
```

*CSS*

```css
.panel {
  margin: 8px 0 0;
  padding: 12px 24px;
  inline-size: fit-content;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-high);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}

.drawer {
  position: absolute;
  inset-block: 0;
  inset-inline-start: 0;
  margin: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {enter, exit} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const menu = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#menu')!;
const drawer = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#drawer')!;

document.querySelector('#toggle-menu')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  // A menu at the top of the screen expands downwards.
  if (menu.hidden) {
    await enter(menu, {origin: 'top'});
  } else {
    await exit(menu, {origin: 'top'});
    menu.hidden = true;
  }
});

document.querySelector('#toggle-drawer')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  // A navigation drawer slides in from the start edge.
  if (drawer.hidden) {
    await enter(drawer, {style: 'slide', origin: 'start', temporary: true});
  } else {
    await exit(drawer, {style: 'slide', origin: 'start', temporary: true});
    drawer.hidden = true;
  }
});
```

Match the origin to where the component lives: a notification from the top, a
drawer from the start edge, a bottom sheet and the keyboard from the bottom.
In templates, `enterExitClasses(state, options)` returns a `classMap()` object
(`md-transition-enter`, `md-transition-from-top` and so on), and
`clearEnterExit(element)` removes the classes.

#### Hide and reveal while scrolling

A component can also leave and return based on a scroll gesture, to give more
room for browsing: a top app bar or a navigation bar that slides off the screen
edge while the user scrolls down and back on when they scroll up.
`scrollEnterExit(element, options)` does this with the slide enter and exit
motion and returns a handle with `hidden`, `show()`, `hide()` and `destroy()`.

**Example: A top bar that hides while scrolling down**

*HTML*

```html
<div class="frame">
  <header id="top-bar" class="top-bar">Inbox</header>
  <div id="content" class="content">
    <p>Scroll down to hide the bar and up to bring it back.</p>
    <p>Message from Ana</p>
    <p>Message from Ben</p>
    <p>Message from Chen</p>
    <p>Message from Dana</p>
    <p>Message from Eli</p>
    <p>Message from Fay</p>
    <p>Message from Gus</p>
    <p>Message from Hana</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.frame {
  position: relative;
  block-size: 200px;
  overflow: hidden;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}

.top-bar {
  position: absolute;
  inset-block-start: 0;
  inset-inline: 0;
  z-index: 1;
  padding: 16px;
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container);
}

.content {
  block-size: 100%;
  overflow: auto;
  padding: 64px 16px 16px;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {scrollEnterExit} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const topBar = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#top-bar')!;

// The element is sticky or fixed at the top edge.
const handle = scrollEnterExit(topBar, {target: 'content', origin: 'top'});
```

`target` is the scrolling element or its id (the window by default), `origin`
the edge it slides toward. It uses the same scroll rules as the app bar and
navigation bar, so they all behave alike: it reveals at the top and when
scrolled up, hides after a short scroll down, never hides while focus is inside
it, and reveals when focus moves into it. A hidden element is `inert`. With
reduced motion it fades instead of sliding. Call `destroy()` when the element
goes away. Components that already have `scroll-behavior="hide"` do not need
this.

#### Coplanar components

A coplanar component sits at the same elevation as the main content (a
standard side sheet), so the content shrinks to make room as it enters and
grows back as it exits. `coplanar(element, open, options)` animates the
element's size from zero to its natural size with the enter motion (and back
with the exit motion), so a flex or grid neighbor resizes with it. It shows the
element when opening and sets `hidden` when closing ends.

**Example: A side panel that makes room for the main content**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="toggle" color="tonal">Toggle panel</md-gb-button>
<div class="layout">
  <main class="main">Main content</main>
  <aside id="panel" class="panel" hidden>Side panel</aside>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.layout {
  display: flex;
  gap: 8px;
  margin-block-start: 16px;
}

.main {
  flex: 1;
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-surface);
}

.panel {
  overflow: hidden;
  padding: 16px;
  border-radius: var(--md-sys-shape-corner-md);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container);
  color: var(--md-sys-color-on-secondary-container);
  white-space: nowrap;
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {coplanar} from '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/transitions.js';

const panel = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#panel')!;
let open = false;

document.querySelector('#toggle')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
  open = !open;
  // The main content narrows as the panel opens.
  coplanar(panel, open);
});
```

`axis: 'block'` grows the element along the block axis instead of the inline
axis. With reduced motion the size changes at once and only a fade plays.
`md-gb-side-sheet` already does this itself: a standard (not modal) sheet takes
its width as `open` is set, so the content beside it shrinks with its spring
motion. Use `coplanar()` for your own panels.

### Skeleton loaders

For the step from a loading state to loaded content. The skeleton hints at
where content will appear and holds its space, so the layout does not shift.
It pulses subtly from the top left to the bottom right, and the content fades in
on top when it is ready.

**Example: A text skeleton and a skeleton that holds a paragraph**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-skeleton loading shape="text"></md-gb-skeleton>
<md-gb-skeleton id="card" loading>
  <p>Content that loads.</p>
</md-gb-skeleton>
<md-gb-button id="done" color="tonal">Finish loading</md-gb-button>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/md-gb-skeleton.js';

const card = document.querySelector('#card')!;
document.querySelector('#done')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
  card.loading = false; // The content fades in. The pulse stops.
});
```

`shape` is `rect`, `text` or `circle`. While loading the element sets
`aria-busy="true"` and makes its content inert. For markup without the element,
use the classes `md-skeleton`, `md-skeleton-text` and `md-skeleton-circle`.

### Accessibility and good practice

The spec asks transitions to follow accessibility settings, stay consistent,
keep layouts stable, avoid jump cuts, use one spatial model and direction, fade
cleanly and stay simple.

- Every helper follows `prefers-reduced-motion` and replaces sliding and
  scaling with a quick fade. Pass `reducedMotion: true` to force it, as an app
  setting would.
- Fade through never overlaps the old and new content. The content fade of a
  container transform is timed to the fastest part of the motion.
- Use one pattern per kind of navigation, and keep forward and backward
  mirrored.
- Dialogs and similar components that appear in place use the short fade
  (`--md-transition-enter-fade-duration`).

## Watch out for

- Keep most of a product on one scheme. Switch schemes only for a few key
  moments, and do it on purpose.
- Do not use motion to carry meaning on its own. Reduced motion removes it,
  so pair it with a change people can see without motion.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/motion-transitions/

# Transitions

Transition patterns connect elements and views, and skeleton loaders hold space while content loads.

The six transition patterns (container transform, forward and backward,
lateral, top level, enter and exit, and skeleton loaders) are helper functions
and classes. See [Motion](/material-web/3.0/styles/motion/#transitions) for the helpers.

## Skeleton loaders

A skeleton hints at where content will appear and holds its space while it
loads. Set `loading` and clear it when the content is ready.

**Example: A text skeleton and a skeleton that holds a paragraph**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-skeleton loading shape="text"></md-gb-skeleton>
<md-gb-skeleton id="card" loading>
  <p>Content that loads.</p>
</md-gb-skeleton>
<md-gb-button id="done" color="tonal">Finish loading</md-gb-button>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
import '@material/web/labs/gb/styles/motion/transitions/md-gb-skeleton.js';

document.querySelector('#done').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#card').loading = false;
});
```

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/styles/spacing/

# Spacing

Spacing is the distance around and between elements.

Spacing is the distance around and between elements. It shapes components
(the space between an icon and its label) and layouts (the margin between the
content and the window edge). Spacing follows an 8dp scale, and tokens keep that
scale in one place.

## Parts of spacing

There are three kinds:

- **Padding** is the space inside an element, between its edge and its
  content.
- **Gaps** are the spaces between elements in a row, column or grid.
- **Margins** are the space outside an element, between it and its parent or
  the screen edge.

Each one can be vertical, horizontal, or on one edge: top, bottom, leading or
trailing. Leading and trailing swap sides in right-to-left languages, so write
them as logical properties (`padding-inline`, `margin-inline-start`).

Define padding and gaps on the parent container first. Margins on child
elements are harder to keep uniform, so use them only for space beyond the
parent's padding, or in a layout.

## The scale

The unit is `--md-sys-space-unit`, 8px. Each token is a multiple of it. The
token name is the value times 100, so `space200` is 2 units (16px). The
in-between values (2, 4, 6 and 10px) are nested units for small gaps, such as
an icon and its label.

| Token | Value | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--md-sys-space-0` | 0px | `--md-sys-space-400` | 32px |
| `--md-sys-space-25` | 2px | `--md-sys-space-450` | 36px |
| `--md-sys-space-50` | 4px | `--md-sys-space-500` | 40px |
| `--md-sys-space-75` | 6px | `--md-sys-space-600` | 48px |
| `--md-sys-space-100` | 8px | `--md-sys-space-700` | 56px |
| `--md-sys-space-125` | 10px | `--md-sys-space-800` | 64px |
| `--md-sys-space-150` | 12px | `--md-sys-space-900` | 72px |
| `--md-sys-space-175` | 14px | | |
| `--md-sys-space-200` | 16px | | |
| `--md-sys-space-250` | 20px | | |
| `--md-sys-space-300` | 24px | | |

The tokens are defined in `labs/gb/styles/space/md-space-tokens.scss`. They
are fixed pixel values, so they do not grow with the text size.

A product can add a token that follows the same pattern. For example,
`--md-sys-space-225: calc(var(--md-sys-space-unit) * 2.25)` gives 18px.

## Adaptive spacing

Some spacing should change with the window. Three adaptive tokens do this:

- `--md-sys-space-adaptive-inline`: horizontal padding
- `--md-sys-space-adaptive-block`: vertical padding
- `--md-sys-space-adaptive-gap`: gap between elements

Each one points at a scale token that depends on the window size class. The
classes are the ones in [Adaptive layout](/material-web/3.0/foundations/adaptive-layout/).

| Class | Inline | Block | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| compact | 16px | 16px | 8px |
| medium | 24px | 24px | 16px |
| expanded | 24px | 32px | 16px |
| large | 32px | 32px | 24px |
| extra-large | 32px | 40px | 24px |

Direct children of a `.md-window` element follow that element's width, so a
layout can adapt to its pane rather than the screen. Other elements follow the
viewport. The spacing unit does not change with the window.

**Example: A list with adaptive gap and padding**

*HTML*

```html
<div class="item-list">
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Inbox</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Drafts</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Sent</md-gb-button>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
.item-list {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--md-sys-space-adaptive-gap);
  padding-inline: var(--md-sys-space-adaptive-inline);
  padding-block: var(--md-sys-space-adaptive-block);
  background: var(--md-sys-color-surface-container-low);
}
```

> The adaptive tokens are defined, but no labs/gb component reads them yet:
> component spacing is the same at every window size today. Use them in your
> own layouts, or remap a component's own spacing property to one (see below).

## How components use spacing

Components map their padding, margins and gaps to scale tokens in their own
custom properties (`--leading-space`, `--icon-label-space` and so on), so a
product can change one mapping and every use follows. For example,
`md-gb-button { --leading-space: var(--md-sys-space-adaptive-inline); }` makes a
button's leading padding follow the window class.

| Component | Scale tokens it reads |
| --- | --- |
| Button, icon button, FAB, split button, segmented button | `space50` to `space200` for leading and trailing space and the icon-label gap |
| Search bar | `space0` to `space300`: leading space `space200`, icon and input gap `space50`, glyph margin `space300` (24px), or `space150` (12px) when focused. Styles are in `labs/gb/components/search/` |
| App bar | `space0` to `space300` for icon, leading and trailing space, the title inset and bottom space, and the actions' inline margin |
| Toolbar, navigation drawer | `space50` to `space200` for container padding and item spacing |
| Chip, text field, tooltip, menu, divider, badge, tabs | `space25` to `space200` for padding, label gaps and insets |
| Date picker, time picker, carousel | `space50` to `space900` for header, actions and content padding |
| App scaffold | `space200` for the FAB's distance from the edge and the gap above the bottom bar |
| Pane scaffold | `--md-sys-layout-margin` and `--md-sys-layout-spacer` (the layout tokens), not the scale |

Every value is the same as before, so nothing changes visually. A few values
are still plain pixels: some generated button, list, FAB, button group and
navigation rail values, the dialog and sheet paddings, and the few values a
component reads in code (a carousel's leading padding, a tooltip's viewport
margin, a tab indicator's inset).

Density changes components, not the spacing scale. Each density step removes
height from the component, and the component's touch target stays 48dp. See
[Density](/material-web/3.0/foundations/density/).

## Accessibility

The spec's accessibility guidance is one point: when text is scaled up to
200%, keep the same spacing. Spacing tokens are fixed in pixels, so the spacing
stays the same while the text grows. For touch targets and focus, see
[Accessibility](/material-web/3.0/foundations/accessibility/).

## What to watch out for

- Use the scale tokens, not hardcoded pixel values. A raw `16px` will not
  follow a remapped token.
- Set spacing on the parent, not the children, unless you need space beyond
  the parent's padding.
- Use logical properties (`padding-inline`, `gap`) so right-to-left layouts
  flip correctly.
- Do not adapt spacing to density yourself. Set the `density` attribute on the
  component and let it apply its own steps.
- Keep the spacing the same at 200% text. Do not replace a token with a value
  that grows with the text.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/

# Components

Every md-gb element of Material Web 3.0: buttons, pickers, progress indicators, navigation, sheets and more, each with live examples and API.

The md-gb elements: interactive building blocks for your interface, each with live examples, guidelines and its API.

## Buttons

- [Button Group](/material-web/3.0/components/button-group/): A button group arranges related buttons and can manage their selection, density and overflow.
- [Buttons](/material-web/3.0/components/button/): Buttons help people initiate actions, from sending an email, to sharing a document, to liking a post.
- [FAB menu](/material-web/3.0/components/fab-menu/): A FAB menu opens from a FAB to show several related actions, and the FAB becomes its close button.
- [Floating action button (FAB)](/material-web/3.0/components/fab/): A FAB represents the most important action on a screen, and an extended FAB adds a text label.
- [Icon Buttons](/material-web/3.0/components/icon-button/): Icon buttons help people take supplementary actions with a single tap.
- [Segmented button](/material-web/3.0/components/segmented-button/): A segmented button set lets people pick one or several options from two to five segments, such as a time range or a view.
- [Split button](/material-web/3.0/components/split-button/): A split button pairs a main action with a trailing button that opens a menu of related actions.

## Date & time pickers

- [Date picker](/material-web/3.0/components/date-picker/): A date picker lets people select a date or a range of dates.
- [Time picker](/material-web/3.0/components/time-picker/): Time pickers let people choose an hour and minute on a clock dial, or type them into fields.

## Loading & progress

- [Loading indicator](/material-web/3.0/components/loading-indicator/): A loading indicator shows that a short process is running, with a shape that morphs through Material shapes while it turns.
- [Progress indicators](/material-web/3.0/components/progress/): Progress indicators inform people about the status of ongoing processes, such as loading an app or submitting a form.
- [Pull to refresh](/material-web/3.0/components/pull-to-refresh/): A pull to refresh container lets people pull its content down to reload it, with a loading indicator that shows progress.

## Navigation

- [Navigation Bar](/material-web/3.0/components/navigation-bar/): A navigation bar lets people switch between a small number of top-level destinations, and can hide as the page scrolls.
- [Navigation Drawer](/material-web/3.0/components/navigation-drawer/): A Material Design navigation drawer.
- [Navigation Rail](/material-web/3.0/components/navigation-rail/): A navigation rail lets people switch between top-level destinations on larger windows, and expands to show full labels.

## Sheets

- [Sheets](/material-web/3.0/components/sheets/): Sheets show supplementary content and actions anchored to the bottom or the side of the window.

## All other components

- [App Bar](/material-web/3.0/components/app-bar/): An app bar sits at the top of a screen and shows its title, navigation and actions, and can hide or compress as the page scrolls.
- [Badge](/material-web/3.0/components/badge/): A badge shows a small dot or a count to signal new or changed information.
- [Card](/material-web/3.0/components/card/): A card contains content and actions about a single subject.
- [Carousel](/material-web/3.0/components/carousel/): A carousel is a scrollable list of visual items that change size as they move through the layout.
- [Checkbox](/material-web/3.0/components/checkbox/): Checkboxes let people select one or more items from a set, or turn an option on or off.
- [Chips](/material-web/3.0/components/chip/): Chips help people enter information, make selections, filter content, or trigger actions.
- [Dialogs](/material-web/3.0/components/dialog/): Dialogs provide important prompts in a user flow.
- [Divider](/material-web/3.0/components/divider/): A divider is a thin line that groups content in lists and containers.
- [Lists](/material-web/3.0/components/list/): Lists are continuous, vertical indexes of text and images, with optional selection, reordering, expanding and swipe actions.
- [Menus](/material-web/3.0/components/menu/): Menus show a temporary set of actions or choices, opened from a button, a text field or a context.
- [Radio](/material-web/3.0/components/radio/): Radio buttons let people select one option from a set of options.
- [Search](/material-web/3.0/components/search/): A search bar lets people enter a query and find matching results, with a search view that shows suggestions and results.
- [Select](/material-web/3.0/components/select/): Select menus let people choose one option from a list that opens on a temporary surface.
- [Sliders](/material-web/3.0/components/slider/): Sliders let people view and select a value, or a range of values, along a track.
- [Snackbar](/material-web/3.0/components/snackbar/): Snackbars tell people about a process an app has performed or will perform, without interrupting them.
- [Switch](/material-web/3.0/components/switch/): Switches toggle the state of an item on or off.
- [Tabs](/material-web/3.0/components/tabs/): Tabs organize groups of related content that are at the same level of hierarchy.
- [Text field](/material-web/3.0/components/text-field/): Text fields let people enter and edit text.
- [Toolbar](/material-web/3.0/components/toolbar/): A toolbar holds actions that relate to the content on the screen, docked to an edge or floating above it.
- [Tooltip](/material-web/3.0/components/tooltip/): Tooltips add context to a button or other element, as a short plain label or a richer panel with a subhead and actions.

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/button-group/

# Button Group

A button group arranges related buttons and can manage their selection, density and overflow.

**Example: A standard button group of three buttons**

```html
<md-gb-button-group aria-label="Text alignment">
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Left</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Center</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Right</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Choose standard or connected.** In a standard group, buttons respond to the one that is pressed; a [connected group](#connected) joins them into one control.
*   **Keep buttons alike.** Use the same size and shape for every button, and mix sizes only for hero moments.
*   **Group related buttons.** Mix colors and widths to emphasize what matters and to group related actions.
*   **Let it adapt.** On narrow screens, trailing buttons can collapse into an [overflow menu](#overflow-menu).

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A button group holds `md-gb-button` elements, each with an optional icon.

**Example: A button group of three buttons with an icon and a label**

```html
<md-gb-button-group>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">
    <md-gb-icon>content_cut</md-gb-icon>
    Cut
  </md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">
    <md-gb-icon>content_copy</md-gb-icon>
    Copy
  </md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">
    <md-gb-icon>content_paste</md-gb-icon>
    Paste
  </md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

## Examples

### Connected

Set `variant="connected"` for buttons that sit together as a single control.

**Example: A connected button group**

```html
<md-gb-button-group variant="connected" aria-label="View">
  <md-gb-button color="outlined">Day</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="outlined">Week</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="outlined">Month</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

### Selection

Set `selection` to `single` or `multiple` and give each button a `value`. Add `required` to keep one selected in a single-select group. A group fires `input` and `change` when selection changes.

**Example: A single-select button group with Week selected**

```html
<md-gb-button-group variant="connected" selection="single" required aria-label="View">
  <md-gb-button value="day" color="outlined">Day</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button value="week" color="outlined" selected>Week</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button value="month" color="outlined">Month</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

### Icons

Buttons in a group can be icon-only. Give each one an `aria-label`.

**Example: A button group of icon buttons**

```html
<md-gb-button-group aria-label="Reactions">
  <md-gb-button color="tonal" aria-label="Like">
    <md-gb-icon>thumb_up</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal" aria-label="Favorite">
    <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal" aria-label="Share">
    <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

### Density

Set `density` from 0 (default) to -3 to make the buttons shorter. Touch targets stay 48px.

**Example: A button group with density -2**

```html
<md-gb-button-group density="-2" aria-label="Text alignment">
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Left</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Center</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Right</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

### Overflow menu

Add `overflow-menu` to collapse the buttons that don't fit into a menu at the trailing edge. Choosing a menu entry clicks the original button.

**Example: A button group with an overflow menu in a narrow container**

```html
<md-gb-button-group overflow-menu aria-label="Actions" style="width: 240px">
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Copy</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Paste</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Cut</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="tonal">Delete</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-button-group>
```

## Accessibility

*   The group does not need a label of its own, but a name such as `aria-label="Text alignment"` helps when the buttons form a set.
*   Label each button as you would a [button](/material-web/3.0/components/button/); icon-only buttons need `aria-label`.
*   Tab enters the group, Arrow keys move between buttons, and Enter or Space activates the focused button.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-button-group&gt;

A Material Design button group.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density of the buttons inside, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the buttons' height (button-groups.md: "Button groups adapt to the height of the buttons inside, including when density is applied"); touch targets stay 48px. A button's own non-zero <code>density</code> wins. Values are clamped to that range.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the button group is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>overflowMenu</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the buttons at the trailing edge that do not fit collapse into a trailing overflow menu, and come back when the group has room again (button-groups.md, Adaptive design: "Buttons at the trailing edge of the button group can be customized to collapse into an overflow menu at smaller breakpoints, and become visible again at larger sizes."). The group is as wide as its container allows: give it a width, or put it in a narrower container, to make buttons overflow. Choosing a menu entry clicks the original button.</span> | <code>overflow-menu</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>required</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether selection is required in single-select mode.</span> | <code>required</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>resizing</code><br><span class="gb-desc">How the group and its buttons resize (button-groups.md, Resizing). <code>fixed</code>: every button keeps the width its own size and width give it. <code>flexible</code>: the group fills the width of its container and its buttons grow with it; an icon button does not stretch past its set width, and a button with <code>resizing="fixed"</code> keeps its width. A button with <code>resizing="flexible"</code> in a fixed group grows when the group is given more width. Unset: a connected group is flexible (it spans its surface), a standard group is fixed.</span> | <code>resizing</code> | <code>ButtonGroupResizing</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>selection</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The selection mode.</span> | <code>selection</code> | <code>ButtonGroupSelection</code> | <code>"none"</code> |
| <code>variant</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The visual variant of the button group.</span> | <code>variant</code> | <code>ButtonGroupVariant</code> | <code>"standard"</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display buttons. |
| <code>overflow</code> | Replaces the default overflow button (see <code>overflowMenu</code>). |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when selection changes. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">InputEvent</span> | Fired when selection changes. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--between-space</code> |  |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Button height removed per density step. |
| <code>--inner-corner-size</code> |  |
| <code>--motion-spring-fast-spatial</code> |  |
| <code>--motion-spring-fast-spatial-duration</code> |  |
| <code>--outer-corner-size</code> |  |
| <code>--outer-corner-square-size</code> |  |
| <code>--pressed-inner-corner-size</code> |  |
| <code>--pressed-item-width-multiplier</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/button/

# Buttons

Buttons help people initiate actions, from sending an email, to sharing a document, to liking a post.

**Example: A filled button and an outlined button**

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">Save</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="outlined">Cancel</md-gb-button>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Label the action.** A button's text describes what happens when it is pressed, such as "Save" or "Join now".
*   **Match emphasis to importance.** Use [filled](#colors) for the final action of a flow, [tonal](#colors) and [outlined](#colors) for medium emphasis, and [text](#colors) for the lowest priority.
*   **Use elevated sparingly.** Elevated buttons add a shadow, so reserve them for buttons that need separation from a patterned background.
*   **Add an icon to draw attention.** An [icon](#with-an-icon) can help communicate the action.

## Anatomy

A button is one element holding a label and an optional icon (default slot). It renders a native `<button>` or, with `href`, a link.

**Example: A filled button with an icon and a label**

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled">
  <md-gb-icon>send</md-gb-icon>
  Send
</md-gb-button>
```

## Examples

### Colors

Choose one of five colors with the `color` attribute: filled, elevated, tonal, outlined, or text.

**Example: Elevated, filled, tonal, outlined and text buttons**

```html
<md-gb-button color="elevated">Elevated</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="filled">Filled</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="tonal">Tonal</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="outlined">Outlined</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="text">Text</md-gb-button>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to `xs`, `sm` (default), `md`, `lg`, or `xl`.

**Example: Buttons from extra small to extra large**

```html
<md-gb-button size="xs">XS</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button size="sm">Small</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button size="md">Medium</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button size="lg">Large</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button size="xl">XL</md-gb-button>
```

### With an icon

Put an `md-gb-icon` before the label, or after it for an action that leaves the page.

**Example: A tonal button with a send icon and a text button with an open-in-new icon**

```html
<md-gb-button color="tonal">
  <md-gb-icon>send</md-gb-icon>
  Send
</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="text">
  Open
  <md-gb-icon>open_in_new</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-button>
```

### Square shape

Add `square` to change the shape of the button from round to square.

**Example: A filled button with a square shape**

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled" square>Square</md-gb-button>
```

### Toggle

Set `type="toggle"` to make a button that stays selected after it is pressed. Add `selected` for the initial state.

**Example: An icon toggle button**

```html
<md-gb-button type="toggle" color="outlined" aria-label="Favorite">
  <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-button>
```

### Disabled and soft-disabled

A disabled button can't be focused with the keyboard. A `soft-disabled` button stays focusable, which helps discoverability in toolbars.

**Example: A disabled button and a soft-disabled button**

```html
<md-gb-button color="filled" disabled>Disabled</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button color="filled" soft-disabled>Soft-disabled</md-gb-button>
```

### Opening a popover or menu

Like a native button, an `md-gb-button` (and `md-gb-icon-button`) takes `popovertarget` (with `popovertargetaction`) or `commandfor` (with `command`) naming an element in the same tree. A menu opened this way also opens with the arrow keys.

**Example: A button that opens a menu**

```html
<md-gb-button color="tonal" popovertarget="button-menu">Options</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="button-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-item>Rename</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Duplicate</md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

## Accessibility

*   Buttons need a visible label; add an [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) to icon-only buttons or when the label needs to be more descriptive.
*   Buttons activate with Enter and Space and are reachable with Tab.
*   Disabled buttons leave the tab order. Use `soft-disabled` to keep one focusable, as the [ARIA guidance on disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls) allows.
*   Toggle buttons expose their state with `aria-pressed`.

**Example: A button whose aria-label describes the action more fully**

```html
<md-gb-button aria-label="Add a new contact" color="elevated">Add</md-gb-button>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-button&gt;

A Material Design button.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The color of the button.</span> | <code>color</code> | <code>"filled" | "elevated" | "tonal" | "outlined" | "text"</code> | <code>'text'</code> |
| <code>download</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The filename to use when downloading the linked resource. If not specified, the browser will determine a filename. This is only applicable when the button is used as a link (<code>href</code> is set).</span> | <code>download</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The URL that the link button points to.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>referrerPolicy</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Sets the underlying <code>HTMLAnchorElement</code>'s <code>referrerpolicy</code> attribute when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>referrerpolicy</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>rel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Sets the underlying <code>HTMLAnchorElement</code>'s <code>rel</code> attribute when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>rel</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>selected</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the button is selected, when <code>type="toggle"</code>. TODO: replace reflected <code>[selected]</code> with <code>:state(selected)</code></span> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>size</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The size of the button.</span> | <code>size</code> | <code>"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xs" | "xl"</code> | <code>'sm'</code> |
| <code>softDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the button is "soft-disabled" (disabled but still focusable). Use this when a button needs increased visibility when disabled. See https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls for more guidance on when this is needed.</span> | <code>soft-disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>square</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Changes the shape of the button to be square.</span> | <code>square</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Where to display the linked <code>href</code> URL for a link button. Common options include <code>_blank</code> to open in a new tab.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>type</code><br><span class="gb-desc">A string indicating the behavior of the button. - "submit" (default): A button that submits its associated form. - "reset": A button that resets its associated form. - "button": A normal button. - "toggle": A toggle button using the <code>selected</code> property. - "link": An anchor link (<code>&lt;a&gt;</code>). Type is always "link" when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>type</code> | <code>string</code> |  |
| <code>unfilledIcon</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Set when the icon has no filled version: a selected toggle button then shows the icon in semibold weight instead of filled.</span> | <code>unfilled-icon</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display a label and optional icon. |
| <code>container</code> | Used to set a custom background container for the button. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a toggle button is selected or unselected. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">InputEvent</span> | Fired when a toggle button is selected or unselected. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(btn)</code> | The button's root element. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | The resolved shape; defaults to the round or square shape. |
| <code>--container-shape-round</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape-square</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-label-space</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--md-icon-fill</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-color</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-width</code> |  |
| <code>--state-layer-color</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-space</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/fab-menu/

# FAB menu

A FAB menu opens from a FAB to show several related actions, and the FAB becomes its close button.

**Example: A FAB menu with three actions**

```html
<md-gb-fab-menu aria-label="Message actions">
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Messages
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">archive</md-gb-icon>
    Archive
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">share</md-gb-icon>
    Share
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
</md-gb-fab-menu>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Open it from a FAB.** The menu appears where the FAB was, and not from an extended FAB or any other component.
*   **Keep it related.** A menu holds 2 to 6 closely related actions under one purpose, such as sharing.
*   **Align to the trailing edge.** The FAB and menu sit at the trailing edge of the window, mirrored in right-to-left languages.
*   **Always label items.** Every item needs a text label.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A FAB menu holds items and a FAB that toggles it. Both icons can be replaced.

**Example: An open FAB menu with custom toggle icons and two items**

```html
<md-gb-fab-menu open aria-label="Compose actions">
  <md-gb-icon slot="icon">add</md-gb-icon>
  <md-gb-icon slot="close-icon">close</md-gb-icon>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">edit</md-gb-icon>
    Note
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">checklist</md-gb-icon>
    List
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
</md-gb-fab-menu>
```

## Examples

### Colors

Set `color` to `primary` (default), `secondary` or `tertiary`.

**Example: A tertiary FAB menu**

```html
<md-gb-fab-menu color="tertiary" aria-label="Photo actions">
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">edit</md-gb-icon>
    Edit
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">delete</md-gb-icon>
    Delete
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
</md-gb-fab-menu>
```

### Size

Set `size` to `md` or `lg` for a larger FAB.

**Example: A large FAB menu**

```html
<md-gb-fab-menu size="lg" aria-label="Photo actions">
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">edit</md-gb-icon>
    Edit
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">delete</md-gb-icon>
    Delete
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
</md-gb-fab-menu>
```

### Start alignment

Set `align="start"` to align the items to the start edge, as for a FAB at the leading side.

**Example: A FAB menu aligned to the start**

```html
<md-gb-fab-menu align="start" aria-label="Photo actions">
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">edit</md-gb-icon>
    Edit
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">delete</md-gb-icon>
    Delete
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
</md-gb-fab-menu>
```

### Open and events

Set `open` to open the menu from code. The `toggle` event fires before it opens or closes and `activate` fires before an item closes it; cancel either to keep the menu as it is.

**Example: A FAB menu that stays open when an item is activated**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-fab-menu open aria-label="Photo actions">
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">edit</md-gb-icon>
    Edit
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
  <md-gb-fab-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">delete</md-gb-icon>
    Delete
  </md-gb-fab-menu-item>
</md-gb-fab-menu>
<output id="status" role="status"></output>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
const menu = document.querySelector('md-gb-fab-menu')!;
const status = document.querySelector('#status')!;
menu.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  status.textContent = 'Activated';
  // Cancel to keep the menu open.
  event.preventDefault();
});
```

## Accessibility

*   Name the menu with `aria-label`, such as "Message actions". It labels the toggle button.
*   The toggle button exposes whether the menu is expanded or collapsed.
*   Tab moves through the button and the items, and Enter or Space activates the focused one.
*   A menu over scrolling content shouldn't hide focused elements. Register it with `setupScrollPadding()` from `appbar/scroll-padding.js`.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-fab-menu&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>align</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The alignment of the items. Defaults to the end, as the FAB.</span> | <code>align</code> | <code>FabMenuAlign</code> | <code>FAB_MENU_ALIGNS.end</code> |
| <code>color</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The color of the FAB, close button and items.</span> | <code>color</code> | <code>FabMenuColor</code> | <code>FAB_MENU_COLORS.primary</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the menu is open.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>size</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The size of the FAB. The close button is always the same size.</span> | <code>size</code> | <code>FabSize</code> | <code>'default'</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The menu's items, typically <code>&lt;md-gb-fab-menu-item&gt;</code>s. |
| <code>close-icon</code> | The close button's icon. Defaults to a "close" icon. |
| <code>icon</code> | The FAB's icon. Defaults to an "add" icon. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>activate</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;FabMenuActivateDetail&gt;</span> | Fired when an item is activated, before the menu closes. Cancel it to keep the menu open. |
| <code>toggle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">ToggleEvent</span> | Fired when the menu opens or closes from user interaction, before the change. Cancel it to keep the menu as it is. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(button)</code> | The FAB that toggles the menu. |
| <code>::part(fab-menu)</code> | The menu's root element. |
| <code>::part(list)</code> | The menu's list of items. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--close-button-between-space</code> |  |
| <code>--close-button-container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--close-button-container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--close-button-container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--close-button-container-width</code> |  |
| <code>--close-button-icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--item-between-space</code> |  |
| <code>--item-container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--item-container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--item-container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--item-icon-label-space</code> |  |
| <code>--item-icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--item-label-text</code> |  |
| <code>--item-label-text-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--item-label-text-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--item-leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--item-trailing-space</code> |  |

### &lt;md-gb-fab-menu-item&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The item's label. FAB menu items should always have a label. |
| <code>icon</code> | The item's leading icon. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(item)</code> | The item's container. |

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/fab/

# Floating action button (FAB)

A FAB represents the most important action on a screen, and an extended FAB adds a text label.

**Example: A FAB with an edit icon**

```html
<md-gb-fab aria-label="Compose">
  <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **One main action.** Use a FAB for the most important action on a screen. It floats in front of other content.
*   **Pick a size.** Choose by visual hierarchy: the default FAB, a medium FAB (most recommended) or a [large FAB](#sizes).
*   **Add a label for emphasis.** An [extended FAB](#extended) shows a text label next to its icon. It can [collapse](#collapse-on-scroll) while a page scrolls.
*   **Place it consistently.** A FAB can sit at the start, center or end, above a navigation bar or nested in it.

## Anatomy

A FAB holds an icon in its default slot. Set `label` to make it an extended FAB.

**Example: A FAB with a share icon**

```html
<md-gb-fab aria-label="Share">
  <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
```

## Examples

### Extended

Set `label` for an extended FAB. The label is its accessible name.

**Example: An extended FAB with an icon and the label Compose**

```html
<md-gb-fab label="Compose">
  <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
```

### Without an icon

An extended FAB is the only FAB that can leave out its icon.

**Example: An extended FAB with only a label**

```html
<md-gb-fab label="Reroute"></md-gb-fab>
```

### Colors

Set `color` to `primary`, `primary-container` (default), `secondary`, `secondary-container`, `tertiary` or `tertiary-container`.

**Example: FABs in primary, secondary and tertiary container colors**

```html
<md-gb-fab color="primary-container" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
<md-gb-fab color="secondary-container" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
<md-gb-fab color="tertiary-container" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to `md` or `lg`. The default is the standard FAB. `sm` is a 40dp FAB that the spec no longer recommends.

**Example: A default, a medium and a large FAB**

```html
<md-gb-fab aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
<md-gb-fab size="md" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
<md-gb-fab size="lg" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
```

### Collapsed

Set `expanded="false"` to collapse an extended FAB to an icon-only FAB. Set the `expanded` property to change it later.

**Example: A collapsed extended FAB**

```html
<md-gb-fab label="Compose" expanded="false">
  <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-fab>
```

### Collapse on scroll

Set `scroll-target` to the id of a scrolling container, or `window`. The FAB collapses while it scrolls down and expands while it scrolls up. A cancelable `toggle` event fires first.

**Example: An extended FAB that collapses while its list scrolls down**

*HTML*

```html
<div id="content">
  <p>Message 1</p>
  <p>Message 2</p>
  <p>Message 3</p>
  <p>Message 4</p>
  <p>Message 5</p>
  <p>Message 6</p>
  <p>Message 7</p>
  <p>Message 8</p>
  <md-gb-fab label="Compose" scroll-target="content">
    <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-fab>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
#content {
  inline-size: 100%;
  block-size: 240px;
  overflow: auto;
}

md-gb-fab {
  position: sticky;
  inset-block-end: 16px;
}
```

## Accessibility

*   An icon-only FAB needs an `aria-label` that describes its action, such as "Compose a new message".
*   An extended FAB uses its `label` as its name, also while collapsed. Add `aria-label` only for more context.
*   An icon-only FAB shows a tooltip on hover and focus. Set `tooltip="false"` to turn it off.
*   A FAB fixed over scrolling content shouldn't hide focused elements. Register it with `setupScrollPadding()` from `appbar/scroll-padding.js`.
*   Tab focuses the FAB, and Enter or Space activates it.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-fab&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code> | <code>color</code> | <code>FabColor</code> | <code>'primary-container'</code> |
| <code>expanded</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the extended FAB shows its label. When <code>false</code>, the label collapses and the FAB becomes an icon-only FAB. Set the attribute to <code>expanded="false"</code> to collapse it from markup.</span> | <code>expanded</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>true</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The extended FAB's label. Without one, the FAB is icon-only.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>scrollTarget</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Opt-in: the <code>id</code> of a scroll container (in the same root), or <code>window</code>. The FAB collapses while it scrolls down and expands while it scrolls up.</span> | <code>scroll-target</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>size</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The size. With a <code>label</code>, <code>default</code>, <code>md</code> and <code>lg</code> are the small, medium and large extended FABs. <code>sm</code> is the small (40dp) icon-only FAB, which the spec no longer recommends.</span> | <code>size</code> | <code>FabSize</code> | <code>'default'</code> |
| <code>tooltip</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Shows a tooltip with the FAB's name (the <code>label</code>, else <code>aria-label</code>) on hover and keyboard focus. On by default for an icon-only FAB, whose icon has no visible text (floating-action-button.md: on web, a FAB should display a tooltip with its text label); <code>tooltip="false"</code> turns it off.</span> | <code>tooltip</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>true</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The icon. Text placed here is shown but does not collapse; use <code>label</code> for an extended FAB. |

| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(fab)</code> | The FAB's root element. |
| <code>::part(label)</code> | The extended FAB's label. |

| <code>--container-width</code> |  |

| <code>--trailing-space</code> |  |
