# Icon Buttons

Icon buttons help people take supplementary actions with a single tap.

**Example: A row of icon buttons, one for each color**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" aria-label="Favorite">
  <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="tonal" aria-label="Share">
  <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="outlined" aria-label="Settings">
  <md-gb-icon>settings</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button aria-label="More options">
  <md-gb-icon>more_vert</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use a clear icon.** Pick a system icon whose meaning people already know, and give the button an accessible name that describes the action.
*   **Describe the action on hover.** On the web, add a [tooltip](#tooltip) so the action is named while hovering or focusing the button.
*   **Pick the color by emphasis.** [Filled](#colors) is the most prominent, [tonal](#colors) and [outlined](#colors) are medium, and the standard color suits the lowest priority.
*   **Show state with a toggle.** A [toggle](#toggle) button uses the outlined icon when unselected and the filled icon when selected.

## Anatomy

An icon button is one element that holds an icon (default slot). It renders a native `<button>` or, with `href`, a link.

**Example: A filled icon button with a send icon**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" aria-label="Send">
  <md-gb-icon>send</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

## Examples

### Colors

Choose one of four colors with the `color` attribute: filled, tonal, outlined, or standard (the default).

**Example: Filled, tonal, outlined and standard icon buttons**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" aria-label="Video call">
  <md-gb-icon>videocam</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="tonal" aria-label="Video call">
  <md-gb-icon>videocam</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="outlined" aria-label="Video call">
  <md-gb-icon>videocam</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button aria-label="Video call">
  <md-gb-icon>videocam</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to `xs`, `sm` (default), `md`, `lg`, or `xl`.

**Example: Filled icon buttons from extra small to extra large**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" size="xs" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" size="md" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" size="lg" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" size="xl" aria-label="Add">
  <md-gb-icon>add</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Widths

Set `width` to `narrow` or `wide`. The default width sits in between.

**Example: Narrow, default and wide icon buttons**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="tonal" width="narrow" aria-label="Edit">
  <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="tonal" aria-label="Edit">
  <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="tonal" width="wide" aria-label="Edit">
  <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Square shape

Add `square` to change the shape of the button from round to square.

**Example: A filled icon button with a square shape**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" square aria-label="Delete">
  <md-gb-icon>delete</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Toggle

Set `type="toggle"` to make a button that stays selected after it is pressed. Add `selected` for the initial state. The selected button shows the filled icon; if an icon has no filled version, add `unfilled-icon` and it gets a heavier weight instead.

**Example: An unselected and a selected toggle icon button**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button type="toggle" color="outlined" aria-label="Favorite">
  <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button type="toggle" color="outlined" selected aria-label="Bookmark">
  <md-gb-icon>bookmark</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Tooltip

Add `tooltip` to show the button's `aria-label` on hover and keyboard focus. Write the label as the action, not the icon's name.

**Example: An icon button with a tooltip**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button tooltip aria-label="Add to favorites">
  <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Links

Set `href` to render the button as a link. Use `target` and `rel` as you would on an anchor.

**Example: An icon button that links to another page**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button href="https://m3.material.io/components/icon-buttons" target="_blank" aria-label="Open the guidelines">
  <md-gb-icon>open_in_new</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Density

Set `density` from `0` (default) down to `-3` to remove 4px of height per step. The touch target stays at least 48px. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

**Example: A filled icon button at density -2**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" density="-2" aria-label="Search">
  <md-gb-icon>search</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

### Disabled and soft-disabled

A disabled button can't be focused with the keyboard. A `soft-disabled` button stays focusable, which helps discoverability in toolbars.

**Example: A disabled icon button and a soft-disabled icon button**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" disabled aria-label="Share">
  <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-icon-button color="filled" soft-disabled aria-label="Share">
  <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

## Accessibility

*   An icon button has no visible text, so always give it an [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) that describes the action.
*   Icon buttons activate with Enter and Space and are reachable with Tab.
*   Disabled buttons leave the tab order. Use `soft-disabled` to keep one focusable, as the [ARIA guidance on disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls) allows.
*   Toggle buttons expose their state with `aria-pressed`.

**Example: A toggle icon button that exposes its pressed state**

```html
<md-gb-icon-button type="toggle" aria-label="Add to favorites">
  <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-icon-button&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The color of the button.</span> | <code>color</code> | <code>IconButtonColor</code> | <code>'standard'</code> |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the container height (and the width of a default-width button); the icon keeps its size and the touch target stays at least 48px. Values are clamped to that range. Density 0 inherits the density of an enclosing <code>md-gb-button-group</code>. icon-buttons.md: don't apply density by default; let people opt in to a denser layout.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>download</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The filename to use when downloading the linked resource.</span> | <code>download</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The URL that the link button points to.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>referrerPolicy</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Sets the underlying <code>HTMLAnchorElement</code>'s <code>referrerpolicy</code> attribute when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>referrerpolicy</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>rel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Sets the underlying <code>HTMLAnchorElement</code>'s <code>rel</code> attribute when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>rel</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>selected</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the button is selected, when <code>type="toggle"</code>. TODO: replace reflected <code>[selected]</code> with <code>:state(selected)</code></span> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>size</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The size of the button.</span> | <code>size</code> | <code>IconButtonSize</code> | <code>'sm'</code> |
| <code>softDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the button is "soft-disabled" (disabled but still focusable).</span> | <code>soft-disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>square</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Changes the shape of the button to be square.</span> | <code>square</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Where to display the linked <code>href</code> URL for a link button.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>tooltip</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Shows a tooltip with the button's accessibility label (<code>aria-label</code>) on hover and keyboard focus. The label should describe the action, not name the icon.</span> | <code>tooltip</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>type</code><br><span class="gb-desc">A string indicating the behavior of the button. - "submit" (default): A button that submits its associated form. - "reset": A button that resets its associated form. - "button": A normal button. - "toggle": A toggle button using the <code>selected</code> property. - "link": An anchor link (<code>&lt;a&gt;</code>). Type is always "link" when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>type</code> | <code>string</code> |  |
| <code>unfilledIcon</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Set when the icon has no filled version: a selected toggle button then shows the icon in semibold weight instead of filled.</span> | <code>unfilled-icon</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>width</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Changes the width of the button.</span> | <code>width</code> | <code>IconButtonWidth</code> | <code>''</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display an icon. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a toggle button is selected or unselected. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">InputEvent</span> | Fired when a toggle icon button is selected or unselected. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(icon-btn)</code> | The icon button's root element. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-height</code> | Container height at density 0. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | The resolved shape; defaults to the round or square shape. |
| <code>--container-shape-round</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape-square</code> |  |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Container height removed per density step. |
| <code>--icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--md-icon-fill</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-color</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-width</code> |  |

| <code>--trailing-space</code> |  |

# Segmented button

A segmented button set lets people pick one or several options from two to five segments, such as a time range or a view.

**Example: A single-select set of three segments with Day selected**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Time range">
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="day" selected>Day</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="week">Week</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="month">Month</md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Prefer a connected button group.** Material 3 Expressive no longer recommends segmented buttons; the connected [button group](/material-web/3.0/components/button-group/) has mostly the same function with an updated look.
*   **Keep it to two to five segments.** For more options or more complex choices, use [chips](/material-web/3.0/components/chip/).
*   **Pick the selection mode.** A set is [single-select](#examples) by default; add [multiselect](#multi-select) when people can choose several.
*   **Use icons, labels or both.** Make sure each [icon-only](#icons) segment has an accessible name.

## Anatomy

A segmented button set holds segments. Each segment has a label and an optional icon.

**Example: A segmented button set whose segments have an icon and a label**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="View">
  <md-gb-segmented-button selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">view_list</md-gb-icon>
    List
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">grid_view</md-gb-icon>
    Grid
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

## Examples

### Multi-select

Add `multiselect` to the set so people can select more than one segment. A selected segment shows a checkmark; add `no-checkmark` to a segment to hide it.

**Example: A multi-select set of filters**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Filters" multiselect>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="vegan" selected>Vegan</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="gluten-free">Gluten free</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="nut-free">Nut free</md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

### Icons

Put an `md-gb-icon` in the `icon` slot, with or without a label. An icon-only segment needs an `aria-label`.

**Example: A set of segments with icons and labels, and a set with icons only**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Layout">
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="list" selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">view_list</md-gb-icon>
    List
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="grid">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">grid_view</md-gb-icon>
    Grid
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Text alignment">
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="left" selected aria-label="Left">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">format_align_left</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="center" aria-label="Center">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">format_align_center</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="right" aria-label="Right">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">format_align_right</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

### Required

In a single-select set, add `required` so a segment always stays selected and the selected one can't be unselected.

**Example: A required single-select set**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Cup size" required>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="small">Small</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="medium" selected>Medium</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="large">Large</md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

### Disabled

Add `disabled` to a segment, or to the set to disable every segment.

**Example: A set with a disabled segment**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Sort by">
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="name" selected>Name</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="date">Date</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="size" disabled>Size</md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

### Density

Set `density` on the set from `0` (default, 40px tall) down to `-3` to remove 4px of height per step. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

**Example: A set at density -2**

```html
<md-gb-segmented-button-set aria-label="Range" density="-2">
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="day" selected>Day</md-gb-segmented-button>
  <md-gb-segmented-button value="week">Week</md-gb-segmented-button>
</md-gb-segmented-button-set>
```

### In a form

The set is form-associated. Give it a `name` and it submits the selected segment's `value`, one entry for each selected segment in a multi-select set. It fires `input` and `change` when people change the selection.

**Example: A form whose segmented button set submits the chosen range**

*HTML*

```html
<form>
  <md-gb-segmented-button-set name="range" aria-label="Time range">
    <md-gb-segmented-button value="day" selected>Day</md-gb-segmented-button>
    <md-gb-segmented-button value="week">Week</md-gb-segmented-button>
  </md-gb-segmented-button-set>
  <output></output>
</form>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
const form = document.querySelector('form');
const output = document.querySelector('output');
const show = () => {
  output.textContent = `range=${new FormData(form).get('range')}`;
};
form.addEventListener('change', show);
show();
```

## Accessibility

*   Give the set an `aria-label` that says what the choice is about.
*   In a single-select set the segments are radios, and in a multi-select set they are checkboxes. Tab enters the set, the arrow keys move between segments, and Space or Enter selects the focused one.
*   Icon-only segments need an `aria-label`.
*   A disabled segment is skipped by the keyboard.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-segmented-button&gt;

One segment of a Material Design segmented button set.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the segment is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>focusable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the segment is the set's tab stop (roving <code>tabindex</code>). Set by <code>md-gb-segmented-button-set</code>.</span> |  | <code>boolean</code> | <code>true</code> |
| <code>groupDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the parent set is disabled. Set by <code>md-gb-segmented-button-set</code>.</span> |  | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Label text, rendered before the default slot's content.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>mode</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The selection mode of the parent set: <code>radio</code> semantics for <code>single</code>, <code>checkbox</code> for <code>multiple</code>. Set by <code>md-gb-segmented-button-set</code>.</span> |  | <code>SegmentedButtonMode</code> | <code>'single'</code> |
| <code>noCheckmark</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to hide the checkmark that shows when selected.</span> | <code>no-checkmark</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selected</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the segment is selected.</span> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The value submitted with the set's form when selected.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The label text. |
| <code>icon</code> | An optional leading icon, such as <code>&lt;md-gb-icon&gt;</code>. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(button)</code> | The segment's <code>&lt;button&gt;</code>. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-height</code> | Segment height at density 0. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | Outer corner radius of the first and last segments. |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Height removed per density step. |
| <code>--icon-label-space</code> | Space between the icon and the label. |
| <code>--icon-size</code> | Icon and checkmark size. |
| <code>--label-text</code> | Label typography. |
| <code>--label-text-axes</code> | Label font variation settings. |
| <code>--label-text-tracking</code> | Label letter spacing. |
| <code>--leading-space</code> | Padding before the content. |
| <code>--min-width</code> | Minimum segment width. |
| <code>--outline-color</code> | Outline color. |
| <code>--outline-width</code> | Outline width. |
| <code>--target-size</code> | Minimum touch target height. |
| <code>--trailing-space</code> | Padding after the content. |

### &lt;md-gb-segmented-button-set&gt;

A Material Design segmented button set.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default, 40px) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the height. Values are clamped to that range.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>SegmentedButtonDensity</code> |  |
| <code>multiselect</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether more than one segment can be selected.</span> | <code>multiselect</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>required</code><br><span class="gb-desc">In single-select mode, whether a segment must stay selected: the selected segment can't be unselected.</span> | <code>required</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The <code>md-gb-segmented-button</code> segments. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the user changes the selection. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">InputEvent</span> | Fired when the user changes the selection. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-height</code> | Segment height at density 0. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | Outer corner radius of the first and last segments. |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Height removed per density step. |
| <code>--icon-label-space</code> | Space between the icon and the label. |
| <code>--icon-size</code> | Icon and checkmark size. |
| <code>--label-text</code> | Label typography. |
| <code>--label-text-axes</code> | Label font variation settings. |
| <code>--label-text-tracking</code> | Label letter spacing. |
| <code>--leading-space</code> | Padding before each segment's content. |
| <code>--min-width</code> | Minimum segment width. |
| <code>--outline-color</code> | Outline color. |
| <code>--outline-width</code> | Outline width. |
| <code>--target-size</code> | Minimum touch target height. |
| <code>--trailing-space</code> | Padding after each segment's content. |

# Split button

A split button pairs a main action with a trailing button that opens a menu of related actions.

**Example: A split button with a Save action and a menu of save options**

```html
<md-gb-split-button>
  <button slot="leading">Save</button>
  <button slot="trailing" aria-label="More save options" popovertarget="save-menu"></button>
  <md-gb-menu id="save-menu">
    <md-gb-menu-item>Save as copy</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Save as template</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu>
</md-gb-split-button>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **One main action plus related ones.** The leading button runs the most common action, and the menu holds the alternatives.
*   **Same sizes as buttons.** Split buttons come in the five button sizes, so they can sit next to [buttons](/material-web/3.0/components/button/) and icon buttons of the same size.
*   **Trailing menu icon.** The trailing button always shows the menu icon. Its color doesn't change when the menu opens; it only turns.

## Anatomy

A split button holds a leading button, a trailing button and the menu the trailing button opens.

**Example: A split button with an icon, a label and a menu**

```html
<md-gb-split-button>
  <button slot="leading">
    <md-gb-icon>send</md-gb-icon>
    Send
  </button>
  <button slot="trailing" aria-label="More send options" popovertarget="anatomy-menu"></button>
  <md-gb-menu id="anatomy-menu">
    <md-gb-menu-item>Send later</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Schedule send</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu>
</md-gb-split-button>
```

## Examples

### Colors

Split buttons are `filled` by default. Set `color` to `elevated`, `tonal` or `outlined`.

**Example: A tonal split button**

```html
<md-gb-split-button color="tonal">
  <button slot="leading">Reply</button>
  <button slot="trailing" aria-label="More reply options" popovertarget="reply-menu"></button>
  <md-gb-menu id="reply-menu">
    <md-gb-menu-item>Reply all</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Forward</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu>
</md-gb-split-button>
```

### Sizes

Set `size` to `xs`, `sm` (the default), `md`, `lg` or `xl`.

**Example: A large split button**

```html
<md-gb-split-button size="lg">
  <button slot="leading">Send</button>
  <button slot="trailing" aria-label="More send options" popovertarget="send-menu"></button>
  <md-gb-menu id="send-menu">
    <md-gb-menu-item>Send later</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Schedule send</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu>
</md-gb-split-button>
```

### Leading icon

The leading button can have an icon, a label, or both.

**Example: A split button with an icon and a label**

```html
<md-gb-split-button>
  <button slot="leading">
    <md-gb-icon>download</md-gb-icon>
    Download
  </button>
  <button slot="trailing" aria-label="More download options" popovertarget="download-menu"></button>
  <md-gb-menu id="download-menu">
    <md-gb-menu-item>Download as PDF</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Download as text</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu>
</md-gb-split-button>
```

## Accessibility

*   Both parts are native `<button>`s you provide, so give the trailing button an `aria-label` that says what the menu holds, such as "More save options". Add one to an icon-only leading button too.
*   The two buttons are separate tab stops. The trailing button toggles the menu with `popovertarget`, and the menu follows the [menu](/material-web/3.0/components/menu/) keyboard behavior.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-split-button&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code> | <code>color</code> | <code>SplitButtonColor</code> | <code>'filled'</code> |
| <code>selected</code> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>size</code> | <code>size</code> | <code>SplitButtonSize</code> | <code>'sm'</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to render the trailing button's popover menu. |
| <code>leading</code> | Requires a <code>&lt;button&gt;</code> for the main action. |
| <code>trailing</code> | Requires a <code>&lt;button&gt;</code> for the menu action. Use <code>popovertarget</code> to display a menu. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(leading-btn)</code> | The split button's main action. |
| <code>::part(split-btn)</code> | The split button's root element. |
| <code>::part(trailing-btn)</code> | The split button's menu action. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--between-space</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--inner-corner-size</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--outer-corner-size</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-space</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/date-picker/

# Date picker

A date picker lets people select a date or a range of dates.

**Example: A docked date picker with a text field**

```html
<md-gb-date-picker label="Event date"></md-gb-date-picker>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Match the context.** Use the docked picker, a calendar under a text field, on medium and expanded windows. Use a [modal](#modal) picker on compact ones.
*   **Pick or type.** A modal picker has a calendar mode and an input mode for typing a date.
*   **Select a range.** Add [`range`](#range) to choose a start and an end date.
*   **Offer a way to clear.** Add `clearable` so people can remove a selection.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A date picker is one element. A docked picker renders a text field and a calendar popup; a modal picker renders a dialog.

**Example: A date picker with a label**

```html
<md-gb-date-picker label="Due date"></md-gb-date-picker>
```

## Examples

### Modal

Set `variant="modal"` and call `show()` to open the picker in a dialog. Use `mode="input"` to start with the date input.

**Example: A button that opens a modal date picker**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-picker">Pick a date</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-date-picker id="picker" variant="modal"></md-gb-date-picker>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
document.querySelector('#open-picker')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('md-gb-date-picker')!.show();
});
```

### Range

Add `range` to select a start and an end date. The value is an ISO interval such as `2026-08-17/2026-08-23`.

**Example: A docked date range picker**

```html
<md-gb-date-picker range label="Trip dates"></md-gb-date-picker>
```

### Value, min and max

Set `value` to an ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Limit the choices with `min` and `max`.

**Example: A date picker with a value and limits**

```html
<md-gb-date-picker label="Check-in" value="2026-08-17" min="2026-08-01" max="2026-12-31"></md-gb-date-picker>
```

### Full screen

Add `fullscreen` to a modal picker for compact windows. It has a close button and a Save button.

**Example: A full-screen modal range picker**

```html
<md-gb-date-picker variant="modal" fullscreen range open></md-gb-date-picker>
```

## Accessibility

*   Name the field with `label`, such as "Event date", and use `supporting-text` to show the expected format.
*   Calendar targets stay 48px, so `density` only affects the text fields.
*   Page Up and Page Down move by month, and Shift with them moves by year.
*   The modal picker closes with Escape, and the docked picker confirms with Enter.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-date-picker&gt;

A Material Design date picker (docked or modal, single date or range).

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>clearable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Shows a Clear button that removes the selection.</span> | <code>clearable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density of the picker's text fields (the docked field and the modal input mode's fields), from 0 (default) to -3, as <code>md-gb-text-field</code> <code>density</code>. Values are clamped to that range. The calendar itself never gets denser (date-pickers.md, Accessibility: "Interactive targets for all elements meet Material's 48x48dp minimum touch target requirement. Increasing density would negatively impact accessibility by limiting tappable/clickable targets"): its dates, menus and buttons keep their size, including inside a dense container.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>error</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Forces the error state of the docked field.</span> | <code>error</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>errorText</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The message shown on the docked field while <code>error</code> is set.</span> | <code>error-text</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>firstDayOfWeek</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The first day of the week, 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday). -1 (default) uses the locale's.</span> | <code>first-day-of-week</code> | <code>number</code> | <code>-1</code> |
| <code>fullscreen</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Modal: the full-screen layout the spec recommends on compact windows. The dialog covers the window and has a close (x) icon button and a **Save** button in place of Cancel and OK.</span> | <code>fullscreen</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>hideActions</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Hides the Cancel and OK buttons; a selection is committed right away.</span> | <code>hide-actions</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>inline</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Renders the calendar surface in the page flow, always visible, instead of a docked popup (without the text field) or a modal dialog.</span> | <code>inline</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>isDateDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Returns true for dates that can't be selected (in addition to dates outside <code>min</code> / <code>max</code>). Receives an ISO date.</span> |  | <code>(date: string) =&gt; boolean</code> | <code>null</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Docked: the text field label. Defaults to "Date" (range: "Dates").</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>locale</code><br><span class="gb-desc">A BCP 47 locale. Defaults to the document's <code>lang</code>, else the browser's.</span> | <code>locale</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>max</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The latest selectable date (ISO).</span> | <code>max</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>min</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The earliest selectable date (ISO).</span> | <code>min</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>mode</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Modal: shows the calendar (<code>picker</code>) or the date input (<code>input</code>).</span> | <code>mode</code> | <code>DatePickerMode</code> | <code>'picker'</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the popup (docked) or dialog (modal) is open.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>quick</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Skips animations.</span> | <code>quick</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>range</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Selects a start and end date.</span> | <code>range</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>required</code><br><span class="gb-desc">A value is required: with no date (or a range without an end date) the picker is invalid (<code>valueMissing</code>).</span> | <code>required</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>strings</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Overrides for the user-facing strings.</span> |  | <code>Partial&lt;DatePickerStrings&gt;</code> | <code>&#123;&#125;</code> |
| <code>supportingText</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Docked: the field's supporting text. Defaults to the date format, e.g. MM/DD/YYYY.</span> | <code>supporting-text</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The committed value: an ISO date (<code>YYYY-MM-DD</code>), or an ISO interval (<code>start/end</code>) when <code>range</code> is set. Empty when nothing is selected.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>variant</code><br><span class="gb-desc"><code>docked</code> (default) or <code>modal</code>.</span> | <code>variant</code> | <code>DatePickerVariant</code> | <code>'docked'</code> |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>cancel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | The selection was dismissed (Cancel, Escape or a click outside). Cancelable: canceling keeps the picker open. |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;DatePickerValueDetail&gt;</span> | The value was committed (OK, Enter, typing in the docked field, or a pick with <code>hide-actions</code>). |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | The popup or dialog began closing; <code>reason</code> is <code>confirm</code> or <code>cancel</code>. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;DatePickerValueDetail&gt;</span> | The pending selection changed (a date was picked or a valid date typed). |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | The popup or dialog opened. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>cancel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; boolean</span> | Discards the pending selection: fires a cancelable <code>cancel</code> event, then closes the popup or dialog. |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Closes the popup or dialog without changing the value (use <code>confirm()</code> to commit the pending selection). |
| <code>confirm</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; boolean</span> | Commits the pending selection to <code>value</code> (firing <code>change</code> if it changed) and closes the popup or dialog. In the date input mode, invalid text shows its error and keeps the picker open. |
| <code>focus</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(options?: FocusOptions) =&gt; void</span> | [MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/focus) |
| <code>show</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens the calendar popup (docked) or dialog (modal). The pending selection starts from <code>value</code>, and focus moves to the selected date (or today). |
| <code>showMonth</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(year: number, month: number) =&gt; void</span> | Shows the given month (<code>year</code>, <code>month</code> 1-12) in the calendar. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(actions)</code> | The text buttons row. |
| <code>::part(container)</code> | The picker surface. |
| <code>::part(field)</code> | The docked text field. |
| <code>::part(grid)</code> | The month grid. |
| <code>::part(header)</code> | The header (modal headline region, or docked menus). |

# Time picker

Time pickers let people choose an hour and minute on a clock dial, or type them into fields.

**Example: An inline time picker set to 7:00**

```html
<md-gb-time-picker value="07:00"></md-gb-time-picker>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Dial or input.** The dial is quick for picking an approximate time, and typing is faster for an exact one. People can [switch](#input-mode) between them unless you hide the toggle.
*   **Inline or modal.** Show the picker [inline](#inline-and-modal) in a form, or as a [modal](#inline-and-modal) when it opens from a field or button.
*   **Match the locale.** The picker follows the 12 or 24 hour clock of its `locale`. Set [`hour-cycle`](#hour-cycle) to force one.

## Anatomy

A time picker has a headline, the hour and minute selectors, an AM or PM toggle in 12 hour mode, a dial, and the actions.

**Example: A time picker with its headline, selectors, dial and actions**

```html
<md-gb-time-picker value="09:30"></md-gb-time-picker>
```

## Examples

### Inline and modal

Add `modal` to show the picker in a dialog with a scrim. Open it with `show()`. It fires `change` when a time is confirmed and `cancel` when it is dismissed.

**Example: A modal time picker opened from a Set alarm button**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="set-alarm">Set alarm</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-time-picker id="alarm" modal headline="Set alarm"></md-gb-time-picker>
<output id="time" for="alarm"></output>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
const alarm = document.querySelector('#alarm');
document.querySelector('#set-alarm').addEventListener('click', () => {
  alarm.show();
});
alarm.addEventListener('change', (event) => {
  document.querySelector('#time').textContent = event.target.value;
});
```

### Input mode

Set `mode="input"` to start with hour and minute fields instead of the dial. Add `hide-mode-toggle` to remove the switch between the two.

**Example: A time picker with hour and minute fields**

```html
<md-gb-time-picker mode="input" value="07:00"></md-gb-time-picker>
```

### Hour cycle

Set `hour-cycle` to `12` or `24`. The `value` is always a 24 hour `HH:MM` string.

**Example: A 24 hour time picker set to 20:00**

```html
<md-gb-time-picker hour-cycle="24" value="20:00"></md-gb-time-picker>
```

### Orientation

The dial sits below the time selectors (`vertical`), except in short landscape windows, where it moves beside them (`horizontal`). Set `orientation` to choose one.

**Example: A time picker with a horizontal layout**

```html
<md-gb-time-picker orientation="horizontal" value="07:00"></md-gb-time-picker>
```

### Density

Set `density` from 0 (default) to -3 to make the picker more compact.

**Example: A time picker with a density of -3**

```html
<md-gb-time-picker mode="input" density="-3" value="07:00"></md-gb-time-picker>
```

## Accessibility

*   Input mode is an alternative to the dial, and every control has a label. Localize the labels with attributes such as `select-hour-label`, `hour-label`, `cancel-label` and `confirm-label`.
*   A modal picker is a `<dialog>`: focus moves into it and returns to the opener on close, and Escape cancels.
*   In the dial, the arrow keys change the selected hour or minute.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-time-picker&gt;

A Material Design time picker component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>cancelLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Cancel action label.</span> | <code>cancel-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Cancel'</code> |
| <code>confirmLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">OK action label.</span> | <code>confirm-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'OK'</code> |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default) to -3 (time-pickers.md "Density", "High-density time picker"). Each step down removes 4px from the time selectors (80px), input fields (72px), the period selector (which follows their height) and the dial (256px); the time selectors, fields and dial labels stay at least 48px. The horizontal layout, used when the viewport is short, keeps the full-size dial ("Don't apply density to the time picker dial when the viewport is constrained. Instead, use an input picker"). Values are clamped to that range.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>dialModeLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the mode toggle in input mode.</span> | <code>dial-mode-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Switch to clock mode'</code> |
| <code>headline</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The headline. Defaults to "Select time" (dial) or "Enter time" (input).</span> | <code>headline</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>hideActions</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Hides the Cancel and OK actions; every change commits the value.</span> | <code>hide-actions</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>hideModeToggle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Hides the dial / input mode toggle button.</span> | <code>hide-mode-toggle</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>hourCycle</code><br><span class="gb-desc"><code>12</code> (with an AM/PM period selector), <code>24</code>, or <code>''</code> (default) to follow the locale's clock (<code>Intl.DateTimeFormat</code>).</span> | <code>hour-cycle</code> | <code>TimePickerHourCycle</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>hourLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Hour field label (input mode).</span> | <code>hour-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Hour'</code> |
| <code>inputModeLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the mode toggle in dial mode.</span> | <code>input-mode-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Switch to text input mode'</code> |
| <code>locale</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The locale used for the 12/24-hour default and the AM/PM labels. Defaults to the browser locale.</span> | <code>locale</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>minuteLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Minute field label (input mode).</span> | <code>minute-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Minute'</code> |
| <code>modal</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Renders the picker as a modal dialog, shown with <code>show()</code> or <code>open</code>.</span> | <code>modal</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>mode</code><br><span class="gb-desc"><code>dial</code> (clock dial) or <code>input</code> (hour and minute text fields).</span> | <code>mode</code> | <code>TimePickerMode</code> | <code>'dial'</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether a modal picker is open. Setting it opens or closes the picker.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>orientation</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The dial layout: <code>vertical</code>, <code>horizontal</code>, or <code>''</code> (default) to pick one from the viewport (horizontal in short landscape viewports).</span> | <code>orientation</code> | <code>"" | TimePickerOrientation</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>periodLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the period selector.</span> | <code>period-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Select AM or PM'</code> |
| <code>quick</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Skips transitions.</span> | <code>quick</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>required</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether a time is required: with no time the picker is invalid (<code>valueMissing</code>) and blocks the form's submit.</span> | <code>required</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selectHourLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the hour selector and the dial in hour mode.</span> | <code>select-hour-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Select hour'</code> |
| <code>selection</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Which part of the time the dial edits.</span> |  | <code>TimePickerSelection</code> | <code>'hour'</code> |
| <code>selectMinuteLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the minute selector and the dial in minute mode.</span> | <code>select-minute-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Select minutes'</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The committed time as a 24-hour <code>HH:MM</code> string (<code>&lt;input type="time"&gt;</code> format), or <code>''</code> when no time is set.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>string</code> |  |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>cancel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when picking is canceled (Cancel, Escape, scrim click). Cancelable for a modal picker; canceling keeps it open. |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a new <code>value</code> is committed (OK, or the end of an interaction with <code>hide-actions</code>). |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a modal picker closes. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired whenever the picked time changes (dial drag, key, typed digits, period). Read the pending time from <code>pendingValue</code>. |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a modal picker opens. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>cancel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; void</span> | Discards the pending time and fires <code>cancel</code>; a modal picker closes unless the event is canceled (canceling keeps the pending time). What the Cancel action does. |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Closes a modal picker without committing. Fires a cancelable <code>close</code> event with <code>detail.reason</code>, then <code>closed</code> after the exit transition. |
| <code>confirm</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Commits the pending time to <code>value</code> (firing <code>change</code> when it differs) and closes a modal picker. What the OK action does. |
| <code>show</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens a modal picker on the committed time, starting with the hours. Fires <code>open</code>. |
| <code>toggleMode</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Switches between the dial and input modes. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(actions)</code> | The actions row. |
| <code>::part(container)</code> | The picker container (a <code>&lt;dialog&gt;</code> when modal). |
| <code>::part(dial)</code> | The clock dial. |
| <code>::part(headline)</code> | The headline. |

# Loading indicator

A loading indicator shows that a short process is running, with a shape that morphs through Material shapes while it turns.

**Example: An indeterminate loading indicator**

```html
<md-gb-loading-indicator aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-loading-indicator>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use it for short waits.** A loading indicator suits processes that finish in under five seconds, and replaces most uses of an indeterminate circular [progress indicator](/material-web/3.0/components/progress/).
*   **Reflect real work.** It always represents an ongoing process and is never only decorative.
*   **Don't switch to determinate.** Avoid it for processes that start indeterminate and later report progress; use a progress indicator there.
*   **Use it for refreshing.** A [pull to refresh](/material-web/3.0/components/pull-to-refresh/) container shows a contained loading indicator.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A loading indicator is one element: a shape, with an optional container behind it.

**Example: A loading indicator**

```html
<md-gb-loading-indicator aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-loading-indicator>
```

## Examples

### Contained

Add `contained` to put the shape on a container, which helps it stand out over content.

**Example: A contained loading indicator**

```html
<md-gb-loading-indicator contained aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-loading-indicator>
```

### Determinate

Set `value` from 0 to 1 to show progress. Without it, the indicator is indeterminate.

**Example: A loading indicator at 40 percent**

```html
<md-gb-loading-indicator value="0.4" aria-label="Downloading"></md-gb-loading-indicator>
```

## Accessibility

*   The indicator is a `progressbar`, so give it an [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) that says what is loading.
*   A determinate indicator exposes its value to assistive technology.
*   With reduced motion, the shape stops morphing and only turns slowly.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-loading-indicator&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>contained</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the indicator has a container.</span> | <code>contained</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Progress from 0 to 1. When set, the indicator is determinate; when unset (the default), it is indeterminate.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>number</code> |  |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(indicator)</code> | The indicator container. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--active-indicator-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-indicator-size</code> |  |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--container-width</code> |  |
| <code>--progress</code> |  |
| <code>--size</code> | The container size, clamped to 24dp-240dp (48dp default). |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/progress/

# Progress indicators

Progress indicators inform people about the status of ongoing processes, such as loading an app or submitting a form.

**Example: A linear progress indicator at 50 percent and an indeterminate circular one**

```html
<md-gb-progress value="0.5" aria-label="Upload progress"></md-gb-progress>
<md-gb-progress circular aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-progress>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Pick the variant.** Use [linear](#linear) for progress across a page or container and [circular](#circular) for a compact spot such as a button or a card.
*   **Use the same style for the same process.** Keep one configuration for all the instances of a process, like loading.
*   **Show real progress when you know it.** Set a [value](#determinate) for determinate progress, and leave it off when the length of the process is unknown.
*   **Use wavy sparingly.** A [wavy](#wavy) active indicator is more expressive; use it where that fits your product.
*   **For short waits, use a loading indicator.** The [loading indicator](/material-web/3.0/components/loading-indicator/) replaces most indeterminate circular progress indicators.

## Anatomy

A progress indicator is one element: an active indicator over a track. It is linear unless `circular` is set.

**Example: An indeterminate linear progress indicator**

```html
<md-gb-progress aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-progress>
```

## Examples

### Linear

The default indicator animates along a horizontal track.

**Example: An indeterminate and a determinate linear progress indicator**

```html
<md-gb-progress aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-progress>
<md-gb-progress value="0.6" aria-label="Download progress"></md-gb-progress>
```

### Circular

Add `circular` to animate clockwise along a circular track.

**Example: An indeterminate and a determinate circular progress indicator**

```html
<md-gb-progress circular aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-progress>
<md-gb-progress circular value="0.6" aria-label="Download progress"></md-gb-progress>
```

### Determinate

Set `value` from 0 to 1 when you know how far along the process is. Without a `value`, the indicator is indeterminate.

**Example: Linear progress indicators at 25, 50 and 75 percent**

```html
<md-gb-progress value="0.25" aria-label="Step 1 of 4"></md-gb-progress>
<md-gb-progress value="0.5" aria-label="Step 2 of 4"></md-gb-progress>
<md-gb-progress value="0.75" aria-label="Step 3 of 4"></md-gb-progress>
```

### Wavy

Add `wavy` to give the active indicator a wave. It works on linear and circular indicators, determinate or not.

**Example: A wavy linear indicator and a wavy circular indicator**

```html
<md-gb-progress wavy value="0.5" aria-label="Upload progress"></md-gb-progress>
<md-gb-progress circular wavy aria-label="Loading"></md-gb-progress>
```

## Accessibility

*   A progress indicator is a `progressbar`. Give it an [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) that says what is in progress, such as "Download progress".
*   A determinate indicator exposes its value from 0 to 100 to assistive technology. An indeterminate one has no value.

**Example: A progress indicator labelled Download progress**

```html
<md-gb-progress value="0.5" aria-label="Download progress"></md-gb-progress>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-progress&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>circular</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the indicator is circular instead of linear.</span> | <code>circular</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Progress from 0 to 1. When set, the indicator is determinate; when unset (the default), it is indeterminate.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>number</code> |  |
| <code>wavy</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the active indicator is wavy instead of flat (the default).</span> | <code>wavy</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(indicator)</code> | The indicator container. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--active-indicator-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-indicator-thickness</code> |  |
| <code>--height</code> | Linear only. |
| <code>--progress</code> |  |
| <code>--size</code> | Circular only. |
| <code>--stop-indicator-color</code> |  |
| <code>--stop-indicator-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--stop-indicator-size</code> |  |
| <code>--stop-indicator-trailing-space</code> |  |
| <code>--track-active-indicator-space</code> |  |
| <code>--track-color</code> |  |
| <code>--track-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--track-thickness</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/pull-to-refresh/

# Pull to refresh

A pull to refresh container lets people pull its content down to reload it, with a loading indicator that shows progress.

**Example: A list of news stories that refreshes when pulled down**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-pull-to-refresh id="news" indicator-label="Refreshing news" style="block-size: 200px">
  <ul>
    <li>Markets rally on new data</li>
    <li>City opens a new bike lane</li>
    <li>Local team wins the final</li>
    <li>Weather turns cooler this week</li>
    <li>New library hours start Monday</li>
    <li>Festival lineup announced</li>
  </ul>
</md-gb-pull-to-refresh>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
const news = document.querySelector('#news');
const loadNews = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
news.addEventListener('refresh', async () => {
  await loadNews();
  news.refreshing = false;
});
```

Pull to refresh is the pull-to-refresh behavior of the [loading indicator](/material-web/3.0/components/loading-indicator/), which it shows while the content reloads.

## Usage guidelines

*   **Refresh content people expect to change.** Use it on feeds and lists that update, such as news or messages.
*   **Always offer another way.** Pulling isn't available to everyone, so provide a [refresh button](#refresh-button) that people can use with a single pointer or the keyboard.
*   **Show it is working.** The container keeps the indicator in view until you set `refreshing` back to `false`.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A pull to refresh container holds the scrolling content (default slot). An indicator appears above it while people pull and while it refreshes.

**Example: A pull to refresh container holding a list**

```html
<md-gb-pull-to-refresh indicator-label="Refreshing tasks" style="block-size: 120px">
  <ul>
    <li>Water the plants</li>
    <li>Pay the rent</li>
    <li>Call the dentist</li>
  </ul>
</md-gb-pull-to-refresh>
```

## Examples

### Refresh button

Call `refresh()` from a button to start the same refresh without a gesture. It fires `refresh` and sets `refreshing`.

**Example: A refresh button above a pull to refresh list**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-icon-button id="reload" aria-label="Refresh">
  <md-gb-icon>refresh</md-gb-icon>
</md-gb-icon-button>
<md-gb-pull-to-refresh id="feed" indicator-label="Refreshing the feed" style="block-size: 160px">
  <ul>
    <li>New recipe: lemon pasta</li>
    <li>Ten tips for sourdough</li>
    <li>What to cook this weekend</li>
    <li>Pantry staples to stock</li>
  </ul>
</md-gb-pull-to-refresh>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
const feed = document.querySelector('#feed');
document.querySelector('#reload').addEventListener('click', () => feed.refresh());
feed.addEventListener('refresh', () => {
  setTimeout(() => {
    feed.refreshing = false;
  }, 1500);
});
```

### Circular indicator

Set `indicator="circular"` to use a circular arrow and progress indicator instead of the default contained loading indicator.

**Example: A pull to refresh list with a circular indicator**

```html
<md-gb-pull-to-refresh indicator="circular" indicator-label="Refreshing messages" style="block-size: 160px">
  <ul>
    <li>Ali: Brunch this weekend?</li>
    <li>Sandra: Summer BBQ</li>
    <li>Trevor: Oui oui</li>
    <li>Britta: Recipe to try</li>
  </ul>
</md-gb-pull-to-refresh>
```

### Threshold and disabled

Set `threshold` to the distance in pixels people must pull before releasing starts a refresh (the default is 80). Add `disabled` to turn pulling off.

**Example: A pull to refresh list that needs a 120px pull**

```html
<md-gb-pull-to-refresh threshold="120" indicator-label="Refreshing orders" style="block-size: 160px">
  <ul>
    <li>Order 1042: shipped</li>
    <li>Order 1041: delivered</li>
    <li>Order 1040: delivered</li>
    <li>Order 1039: returned</li>
  </ul>
</md-gb-pull-to-refresh>
```

## Accessibility

*   Pulling needs a drag, so also provide a button or another control that calls `refresh()`, usable with a single pointer or the keyboard.
*   While refreshing, the indicator is a `progressbar` named by `indicator-label` (the default is "Refreshing"), and the label is announced politely. Write a label that says what is refreshing, such as "Refreshing news".

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-pull-to-refresh&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether pulling is turned off (Compose <code>enabled = false</code>).</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>indicator</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The indicator: <code>loading</code> (M3 Expressive contained loading indicator) or <code>circular</code> (circular arrow and progress indicator).</span> | <code>indicator</code> | <code>PullToRefreshIndicator</code> | <code>'loading'</code> |
| <code>indicatorLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the indicator, e.g. "Refreshing news".</span> | <code>indicator-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>DEFAULT_LABEL</code> |
| <code>refreshing</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether content is refreshing. Set by a pull past the threshold (or <code>refresh()</code>); set it back to false once the content has refreshed.</span> | <code>refreshing</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>threshold</code><br><span class="gb-desc">How far (px) the indicator must be pulled before releasing it refreshes (Compose <code>PullToRefreshDefaults.PositionalThreshold</code>, 80dp).</span> | <code>threshold</code> | <code>number</code> | <code>PULL_TO_REFRESH_THRESHOLD_PX</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The scrolling content. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>refresh</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a pull (or <code>refresh()</code>) starts a refresh. Cancel it to keep <code>refreshing</code> false. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>refresh</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; boolean</span> | Starts a refresh without a gesture, e.g. from a refresh button: fires <code>refresh</code> and, unless it is cancelled, sets <code>refreshing</code>. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(indicator)</code> | The indicator container. |
| <code>::part(scroller)</code> | The element that scrolls the content. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--indicator-color</code> |  |
| <code>--indicator-container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--indicator-container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--indicator-container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--indicator-container-width</code> |  |
| <code>--indicator-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--indicator-max-distance</code> | How far the indicator moves below the top edge at the threshold. |
| <code>--motion-effects-duration</code> |  |
| <code>--motion-effects-easing</code> |  |
| <code>--motion-settle-duration</code> |  |
| <code>--motion-settle-easing</code> |  |

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/navigation-bar/

# Navigation Bar

A navigation bar lets people switch between a small number of top-level destinations, and can hide as the page scrolls.

**Example: A navigation bar with four destinations and Home active**

```html
<md-gb-nav-bar aria-label="Primary">
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item active href="#home">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">home</md-gb-icon>
    Home
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item href="#explore">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">explore</md-gb-icon>
    Explore
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item href="#library">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">library_music</md-gb-icon>
    Library
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item href="#profile">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">person</md-gb-icon>
    Profile
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
</md-gb-nav-bar>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use it in compact and medium windows.** From expanded windows up, switch to a [navigation rail](/material-web/3.0/components/navigation-rail/).
*   **Keep three to five destinations.** They should be of equal importance.
*   **Keep destinations consistent.** The same destinations appear on every screen of the app.
*   **Pick the item layout.** Use [vertical](#item-layout) items in compact windows and horizontal items from medium windows.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A navigation bar holds items. Each item has an icon, a label and an optional badge.

**Example: A navigation bar with one item that has an icon, a badge and a label**

```html
<md-gb-nav-bar aria-label="Chat">
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item active>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">chat_bubble</md-gb-icon>
    <md-gb-badge slot="badge">3</md-gb-badge>
    Chats
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">call</md-gb-icon>
    Calls
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
</md-gb-nav-bar>
```

## Examples

### Item layout

Set `item-layout` to `vertical` (the default) or `horizontal`. With `auto`, items are vertical in compact windows and horizontal from 600px.

**Example: A navigation bar with horizontal items**

```html
<md-gb-nav-bar item-layout="horizontal" aria-label="Library">
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item active>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">auto_awesome</md-gb-icon>
    For you
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">bookmark</md-gb-icon>
    Saved
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">settings</md-gb-icon>
    Settings
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
</md-gb-nav-bar>
```

### Badges

Set `badge` on an item to show a count, or `badge="dot"` for a small dot that signals something new.

**Example: Navigation bar items with a count badge and a dot badge**

```html
<md-gb-nav-bar aria-label="Mail">
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item active badge="4">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item badge="dot">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">chat_bubble</md-gb-icon>
    Chat
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">videocam</md-gb-icon>
    Meet
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
</md-gb-nav-bar>
```

### Links

Give an item an `href` (and optionally `target` and `rel`) to make the destination a link, as in the first example. The item then has the `link` role and the selected one is marked `aria-current="page"`. Without `href` an item is a tab that just reports the selection.

### Hide on scroll

Set `scroll-behavior="hide"` to hide the bar when the page scrolls down and show it again on scroll up. By default it follows the window; set `scroll-target` to the id of another scrolling element. Fix the bar to the bottom of the page.

**Example: A navigation bar that hides while its list scrolls down**

*HTML*

```html
<div id="messages">
  <p>Message 1</p>
  <p>Message 2</p>
  <p>Message 3</p>
  <p>Message 4</p>
  <p>Message 5</p>
  <p>Message 6</p>
  <p>Message 7</p>
  <p>Message 8</p>
  <md-gb-nav-bar scroll-behavior="hide" scroll-target="messages" aria-label="Mail">
    <md-gb-nav-bar-item active>
      <md-gb-icon slot="icon">inbox</md-gb-icon>
      Inbox
    </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
      <md-gb-icon slot="icon">send</md-gb-icon>
      Sent
    </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  </md-gb-nav-bar>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
#messages {
  inline-size: 100%;
  block-size: 240px;
  overflow: auto;
}

md-gb-nav-bar {
  position: sticky;
  inset-block-end: 0;
}
```

### Selection

The `active` item shows the current destination, and `selected-index` selects an item by position. The bar fires `change` when the selection changes.

**Example: A navigation bar that reports the selected index**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-nav-bar aria-label="Sections">
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item active>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">home</md-gb-icon>
    Home
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">search</md-gb-icon>
    Search
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
  <md-gb-nav-bar-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">settings</md-gb-icon>
    Settings
  </md-gb-nav-bar-item>
</md-gb-nav-bar>
<output id="selection" role="status">Selected item 0</output>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
const bar = document.querySelector('md-gb-nav-bar')!;
const selection = document.querySelector('#selection')!;
bar.addEventListener('change', () => {
  selection.textContent = 'Selected item ' + bar.selectedIndex;
});
```

## Accessibility

*   Give the bar an `aria-label` such as "Primary navigation".
*   Without links the bar is a tab list and its items are tabs, with exactly one selected. Tab moves focus into the bar, the arrow keys move between items, and Enter and Space select one.
*   When the items have an `href` the bar is a navigation landmark of links and the selected one is `aria-current="page"`. Enter follows a link; Space doesn't.
*   Every item needs a visible label, which is also its accessible name. If the label is ambiguous, add a more descriptive `aria-label` to the item.
*   A hidden bar never hides while focus is inside it or when the page scrolls from a key press, and it reappears when focus moves into it. Leave `scroll-behavior` off if screen reader users rely on the bar.
*   Disabled items leave the tab order.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-nav-bar&gt;

A Material Design gBreeze navigation bar custom element.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>autoSelect</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not to automatically select a tab when it is focused.</span> | <code>autoselect</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>itemLayout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The layout orientation of items: <code>vertical</code>, <code>horizontal</code>, or <code>auto</code> (vertical in compact windows, horizontal from medium windows, 600px).</span> | <code>item-layout</code> | <code>NavBarLayout</code> | <code>'vertical'</code> |
| <code>orientation</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Orientation of the tablist ('horizontal' or 'vertical').</span> | <code>orientation</code> | <code>"horizontal" | "vertical"</code> | <code>'horizontal'</code> |
| <code>scrollBehavior</code><br><span class="gb-desc">How the bar reacts to scrolling: <code>hide</code> hides it on scroll down.</span> | <code>scroll-behavior</code> | <code>"hide"</code> |  |
| <code>scrollTarget</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The id of the element whose scrolling drives <code>scroll-behavior</code>. Defaults to the window.</span> | <code>scroll-target</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>selectedIndex</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The 0-based index of the currently active navigation bar item. Alias for <code>selectedTabIndex</code>.</span> | <code>selected-index</code> | <code>number</code> |  |
| <code>selectedTabIndex</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The index of the currently selected tab.</span> | <code>selectedtabindex</code> | <code>number</code> |  |

### &lt;md-gb-nav-bar-item&gt;

A Material Design gBreeze navigation bar item custom element.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>active</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the navigation bar item is active. Alias for <code>selected</code>.</span> | <code>active</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>badge</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Optional badge text (or 'dot' / 'true' for a small dot badge).</span> | <code>badge</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the navigation bar item is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The URL the destination links to. The item is then a link (role <code>link</code>, <code>aria-current="page"</code> while selected) instead of a tab.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>itemLayout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The layout orientation of the item ('vertical' or 'horizontal').</span> | <code>item-layout</code> | <code>NavBarItemLayout</code> | <code>'vertical'</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Optional label text if not provided via default slot.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>rel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The link's <code>rel</code> attribute, when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>rel</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>tabpanel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">ID of the associated <code>md-aria-tabpanel</code> element.</span> | <code>tabpanel</code> | <code>string</code> |  |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Where to open the linked <code>href</code>, e.g. <code>_blank</code>.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>unfilledIcon</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the icon has no filled style. The active destination then uses the semibold icon weight instead of the filled icon.</span> | <code>unfilled-icon</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display the item's label text. |
| <code>badge</code> | Used to display a custom badge on the item's icon. |
| <code>icon</code> | Used to display the item's icon (<code>md-gb-icon</code>). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>click</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Activates the destination: follows its link, else clicks the tab. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(indicator)</code> | The active indicator / icon container element. |
| <code>::part(label)</code> | The label text container element. |
| <code>::part(nav-bar-item)</code> | The navigation bar item's presentational container. |
