# Navigation Drawer

A Material Design navigation drawer.

**Example: A standard navigation drawer with Inbox selected**

```html
<md-gb-nav-drawer open aria-label="Mail">
  <h2 slot="headline">Mail</h2>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#inbox" selected badge="24">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">inbox</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#sent">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">send</md-gb-icon>
    Sent
  </md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
</md-gb-nav-drawer>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use it for top-level destinations.** A drawer lists the main sections of an app, with the current one selected.
*   **Choose standard or modal.** A standard drawer (above) sits beside the content on large windows; a [modal drawer](#modal-drawer) opens over a scrim on small ones.
*   **Group with labels.** Use section labels and dividers to organize long lists.
*   **Keep labels short.** Long [labels](#text-labels-only) truncate.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A drawer holds an optional headline, section labels, dividers, and items.

**Example: A drawer with a headline, section label, items, badge and divider**

```html
<md-gb-nav-drawer open aria-label="Mail">
  <h2 slot="headline">Mail</h2>
  <h2 class="nav-drawer-section-label">Folders</h2>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#anatomy-inbox" selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">inbox</md-gb-icon>
    <span slot="badge">24</span>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#anatomy-drafts">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">draft</md-gb-icon>
    Drafts
  </md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-divider></md-gb-divider>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#anatomy-trash">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">delete</md-gb-icon>
    Trash
  </md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
</md-gb-nav-drawer>
```

## Examples

### Modal drawer

Set `modal` to open the drawer over a scrim. Escape, the scrim, or swiping closes it.

**Example: A button that opens a modal navigation drawer**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-menu">Menu</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-nav-drawer id="menu" modal aria-label="Mail">
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#inbox" selected>Inbox</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#sent">Sent</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
</md-gb-nav-drawer>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-menu').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#menu').show();
});
```

### Modal drawer without swipe

Set `gestures-disabled` on a modal drawer to turn off swipe-to-close. Escape, the scrim, and `close()` still work.

**Example: A modal navigation drawer that can't be swiped closed**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-fixed-menu">Menu</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-nav-drawer id="fixed-menu" modal gestures-disabled aria-label="Mail">
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#inbox" selected>Inbox</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#sent">Sent</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
</md-gb-nav-drawer>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-fixed-menu').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#fixed-menu').show();
});
```

### Text labels only

Items work without icons. Labels that are too long truncate, and `disabled` items are not interactive.

**Example: A navigation drawer with text labels only**

```html
<md-gb-nav-drawer open aria-label="Settings">
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#general" selected>General</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item href="#privacy">Privacy</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
  <md-gb-nav-drawer-item disabled>Billing</md-gb-nav-drawer-item>
</md-gb-nav-drawer>
```

## Accessibility

*   The drawer renders a `<nav>` landmark; give it a name with `aria-label`.
*   The selected item is the current page and is exposed with `aria-current`.
*   A modal drawer is a dialog: it traps focus, closes with Escape, and returns focus to what opened it.
*   Tab moves through the items; Enter activates a link item.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-nav-drawer&gt;

A Material Design navigation drawer custom element.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>gesturesDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether swiping a modal drawer closed is turned off (Compose <code>gesturesEnabled = false</code>). Escape, the scrim and <code>close()</code> still close it.</span> | <code>gestures-disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The accessible name of the navigation landmark. Use it instead of <code>aria-label</code> when the host sits outside any landmark: the host's <code>aria-label</code> moves to a data attribute that checkers (axe <code>region</code>) still read as a name on a host that has no landmark role.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>modal</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the drawer is modal: it opens over a scrim that blocks the rest of the app, instead of sitting next to the content.</span> | <code>modal</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the drawer is open.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>quick</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to skip the open and close transitions.</span> | <code>quick</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Navigation items (<code>md-gb-nav-drawer-item</code>), section labels (headings or <code>.nav-drawer-section-label</code>) and dividers (<code>md-gb-divider</code> or <code>&lt;hr&gt;</code>). |
| <code>headline</code> | Optional headline shown above the items. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the user selects a different item. |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired when the drawer starts closing. |
| <code>closed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired when the drawer has closed and finished animating. |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the drawer starts opening. |
| <code>opened</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the drawer has opened and finished animating. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Closes the drawer. Resolves once it has finished animating. |
| <code>show</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens the drawer. Resolves once it has finished animating. |
| <code>toggle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens the drawer when closed, closes it when open. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(dialog)</code> | The modal drawer's <code>&lt;dialog&gt;</code>. |
| <code>::part(drawer)</code> | The drawer sheet. |
| <code>::part(nav)</code> | The <code>&lt;nav&gt;</code> landmark. |
| <code>::part(scrim)</code> | The modal drawer's scrim. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--active-focus-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-focus-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-hover-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-hover-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-indicator-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-indicator-height</code> |  |
| <code>--active-indicator-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--active-indicator-width</code> |  |
| <code>--active-label-text</code> |  |
| <code>--active-label-text-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--active-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-pressed-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--active-pressed-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--container-padding-block</code> |  |

| <code>--container-shape</code> | Radius of the end corners. |

| <code>--divider-inset</code> |  |

| <code>--headline-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-focus-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-focus-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-hover-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-hover-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-pressed-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--inactive-pressed-label-text-color</code> |  |

### &lt;md-gb-nav-drawer-item&gt;

A Material Design navigation drawer item custom element.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>badge</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Trailing badge label text, such as an unread count. Ignored when content is slotted into <code>badge</code>.</span> | <code>badge</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The URL the item links to. Renders a link (<code>&lt;a&gt;</code>) when set.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>rel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The link's <code>rel</code> attribute, when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>rel</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>selected</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item is the selected (current) destination.</span> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>tabStop</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item is in the tab order. The parent <code>md-gb-nav-drawer</code> manages this to provide a single tab stop with arrow key navigation.</span> |  | <code>boolean</code> | <code>true</code> |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Where to open the linked <code>href</code>, e.g. <code>_blank</code>.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>''</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The item's label text. |
| <code>badge</code> | Trailing badge label text (overrides the <code>badge</code> property). |
| <code>icon</code> | The item's leading icon (<code>md-gb-icon</code>). Filled when selected. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>blur</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | [MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/blur) |
| <code>focus</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(options?: FocusOptions) =&gt; void</span> | Focuses the item's link or button. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(badge)</code> | The trailing badge label container. |
| <code>::part(icon)</code> | The icon container. |
| <code>::part(item)</code> | The item's link or button. |
| <code>::part(label)</code> | The label text container. |

# Navigation Rail

A navigation rail lets people switch between top-level destinations on larger windows, and expands to show full labels.

**Example: A navigation rail with a menu button and four destinations**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Primary" collapsible>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected href="#inbox">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item href="#chat">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">chat_bubble</md-gb-icon>
    Chat
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item href="#spaces">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">groups</md-gb-icon>
    Spaces
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item href="#meet">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">videocam</md-gb-icon>
    Meet
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use it in medium windows and larger.** On compact windows use a [navigation bar](/material-web/3.0/components/navigation-bar/) instead.
*   **Keep three to seven destinations.** Add an optional FAB or menu button in the header.
*   **Keep it in the same place.** The rail stays at the leading edge on every screen of the app.
*   **Let it expand.** A [collapsed](#collapsible) rail shows icons and short labels, and an expanded rail shows horizontal items and can replace a navigation drawer.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A rail has an optional header, such as a menu button or a FAB, and items. Each item has an icon, a label and an optional badge.

**Example: A rail with a menu button, a FAB and items, one with a badge**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Mail">
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="header" aria-label="Open menu"><md-gb-icon>menu</md-gb-icon></md-gb-icon-button>
  <md-gb-fab slot="header" aria-label="Compose"><md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon></md-gb-fab>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected href="#anatomy-inbox">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">inbox</md-gb-icon>
    <span slot="badge">3</span>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item href="#anatomy-sent">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">send</md-gb-icon>
    Sent
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

## Examples

### Links

Give an item an `href` (and optionally `target` and `rel`) to make the destination a link, as in the first example. The item then has the `link` role and the selected one is marked `aria-current="page"`. Without `href` an item is a tab that just reports the selection.

### Collapsible

Add `collapsible` to show a built-in menu button in the header that expands and collapses the rail. To use your own button, put it in the `header` slot and call `toggle()`, `expand()` or `collapse()`. Set `expanded` to start expanded. The rail fires `toggle` when it expands or collapses.

**Example: A collapsible rail that starts expanded**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Mail" collapsible expanded>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">send</md-gb-icon>
    Sent
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">drafts</md-gb-icon>
    Drafts
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

### Header

Use the `header` slot for a menu button and a FAB above the items.

**Example: A rail with a menu button and a compose FAB**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Mail">
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="header" aria-label="Open menu">
    <md-gb-icon>menu</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  <md-gb-fab slot="header" label="Compose">
    <md-gb-icon>edit</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-fab>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">send</md-gb-icon>
    Sent
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

### Alignment

Set `alignment` to `top` (the default), `center` or `bottom` to place the items along the rail.

**Example: A rail with its items centered**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Primary" alignment="center">
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">home</md-gb-icon>
    Home
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">search</md-gb-icon>
    Search
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">settings</md-gb-icon>
    Settings
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

### Badges

Set `badge` on an item to show a count, or `badge="dot"` for a small dot.

**Example: Rail items with a count badge and a dot badge**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Mail">
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected badge="4">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item badge="dot">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">chat_bubble</md-gb-icon>
    Chat
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

### Secondary items

Add `secondary` to an item that should show only while the rail is expanded, such as a less important destination.

**Example: An expanded rail with a secondary destination**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Mail" collapsible expanded>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item secondary>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">delete</md-gb-icon>
    Trash
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

### Modal

Add `modal` so the expanded rail opens over the content with a scrim. Add `hide-when-collapsed` to take the collapsed rail out of the layout entirely; the app's menu button then calls `toggle()` to show it. On Android, the back gesture collapses a modal rail.

**Example: A collapsible modal rail**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Mail" modal collapsible>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">mail</md-gb-icon>
    Inbox
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">send</md-gb-icon>
    Sent
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

### Appearance

Add `divider` to draw a line at the rail's edge, `elevated` to lift it above scrolling content, and `narrow` to use the 80dp collapsed width.

**Example: A narrow rail with a divider**

```html
<md-gb-nav-rail aria-label="Primary" narrow divider>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item selected>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">home</md-gb-icon>
    Home
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
  <md-gb-nav-rail-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">search</md-gb-icon>
    Search
  </md-gb-nav-rail-item>
</md-gb-nav-rail>
```

## Accessibility

*   Give the rail an `aria-label` such as "Primary navigation".
*   Without links the rail is a tab list and its items are tabs, with exactly one selected. Tab moves focus into the rail, the arrow keys move between items, and Enter and Space select one.
*   When the items have an `href` the rail is a navigation landmark of links and the selected one is `aria-current="page"`. Enter follows a link; Space doesn't.
*   Every item needs a visible label, which is also its accessible name.
*   Give a menu button in the header an `aria-label`, such as "Open menu".
*   A modal rail collapses on Escape and when the scrim is pressed. Keep the menu button available as the single-pointer alternative to swiping it closed.
*   Disabled items leave the tab order.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-nav-rail&gt;

A Material Design navigation rail custom element.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>alignment</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Vertical alignment of items ('top', 'center', or 'bottom').</span> | <code>alignment</code> | <code>NavRailAlignment</code> | <code>'top'</code> |
| <code>autoSelect</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not to automatically select a tab when it is focused.</span> | <code>autoselect</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>collapsible</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the navigation rail renders a built-in expand/collapse menu button in the header when no toggle button is slotted into <code>slot="header"</code>.</span> | <code>collapsible</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>divider</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether a vertical divider marks the edge of the rail next to the app's content.</span> | <code>divider</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>elevated</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the rail is elevated to level 1, to distinguish it from content that scrolls underneath it.</span> | <code>elevated</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>expanded</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the navigation rail is expanded to show horizontal items.</span> | <code>expanded</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>hideWhenCollapsed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Hide when collapsed (navigation-rail.md): the collapsed rail is not shown and takes no space, so the body content fills in. The expanded rail (always modal in this mode) appears over the content when the app's menu button calls <code>expand()</code> or <code>toggle()</code>; keep that menu button accessible.</span> | <code>hide-when-collapsed</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>itemLayout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The layout orientation of items ('vertical' or 'horizontal').</span> | <code>item-layout</code> | <code>NavRailItemLayout</code> | <code>'vertical'</code> |
| <code>modal</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the expanded navigation rail is modal: it opens over the content with a scrim, with modal elevation and shape.</span> | <code>modal</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>narrow</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the collapsed rail uses the narrow width (<code>md.comp.nav-rail.collapsed.narrow.container.width</code>, 80dp).</span> | <code>narrow</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selectedIndex</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The 0-based index of the currently active navigation rail item. Alias for <code>selectedTabIndex</code>.</span> | <code>selected-index</code> | <code>number</code> |  |
| <code>selectedTabIndex</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The index of the currently selected tab.</span> | <code>selectedtabindex</code> | <code>number</code> |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display navigation rail items (<code>md-gb-nav-rail-item</code>). |
| <code>header</code> | Used to display optional header controls (menu button, FAB). |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the selected item changes. |
| <code>toggle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;expanded: boolean, reason?: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired when the expanded state is toggled. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>collapse</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Collapses the navigation rail. |
| <code>expand</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Expands the navigation rail. |
| <code>handleBack</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Handles a back request (the Android back gesture or button) on the modal expanded rail: plays the predictive back motion, then collapses the rail. Call it for an in-app back control that should behave like the system back. Resolves after the back motion. |
| <code>toggle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(force?: boolean) =&gt; boolean</span> | Toggles the expanded state of the navigation rail. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(header)</code> | The navigation rail's header container. |
| <code>::part(items)</code> | The navigation rail's items container. |
| <code>::part(menu-button)</code> | The built-in expand/collapse menu button when <code>collapsible</code>. |
| <code>::part(nav-rail)</code> | The navigation rail's root container. |
| <code>::part(scrim)</code> | The modal rail's scrim, while expanded. A <code>modal</code> rail expands over the content with a scrim, like Compose <code>ModalWideNavigationRail</code>. Clicking the scrim, pressing Escape or swiping the rail toward its edge collapses it. The scrim (and the menu button of a <code>collapsible</code> rail) are the single-pointer alternatives to the swipe. While a modal rail is expanded, focus moves into it, Tab stays inside it, page scrolling is locked, and focus returns to the previous element when it collapses. The <code>toggle</code> event's <code>detail.reason</code> says why a modal rail collapsed (<code>escape</code>, <code>back</code>, <code>scrim</code> or <code>swipe</code>). Predictive back applies to the modal expanded rail (navigation-rail.md): while it is expanded the rail listens for back requests with a <code>CloseWatcher</code> (the Android back gesture or button, and Escape), falling back to Escape on the document where <code>CloseWatcher</code> is missing. A back request plays the predictive back motion (the rail pops off its edge, Compose <code>ModalWideNavigationRail</code> scales) and collapses the rail. A FAB (<code>md-gb-fab</code> with a <code>label</code>) in the header is an extended FAB while the rail is expanded and an icon FAB while it is collapsed. |

### &lt;md-gb-nav-rail-item&gt;

A Material Design navigation rail item custom element.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>active</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the navigation rail item is active. Alias for <code>selected</code>. TODO: replace reflected <code>[active]</code> with <code>:state(selected)</code></span> | <code>active</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>badge</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Optional badge text (or 'dot' / 'true' for a small dot badge).</span> | <code>badge</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the navigation rail item is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The URL the destination links to. The item is then a link (role <code>link</code>, <code>aria-current="page"</code> while selected) instead of a tab.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>itemLayout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The layout orientation of the item ('vertical' or 'horizontal').</span> | <code>item-layout</code> | <code>NavRailItemLayout</code> | <code>'vertical'</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Optional label text if not provided via default slot.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>rel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The link's <code>rel</code> attribute, when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>rel</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>secondary</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the destination is secondary: it shows only while the rail is expanded.</span> | <code>secondary</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>tabpanel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">ID of the associated <code>md-aria-tabpanel</code> element.</span> | <code>tabpanel</code> | <code>string</code> |  |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Where to open the linked <code>href</code>, e.g. <code>_blank</code>.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>unfilledIcon</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the icon has no filled style. The active destination then uses the semibold icon weight instead of the filled icon.</span> | <code>unfilled-icon</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display the item's label text. |
| <code>badge</code> | Used to display a custom badge on the item's icon. |
| <code>icon</code> | Used to display the item's icon (<code>md-gb-icon</code>). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>click</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Activates the destination: follows its link, else clicks the tab. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(indicator)</code> | The active indicator / icon container element. |
| <code>::part(label)</code> | The label text container element. |
| <code>::part(nav-rail-item)</code> | The navigation rail item's presentational container. |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/sheets/

# Sheets

Sheets show supplementary content and actions anchored to the bottom or the side of the window.

**Example: A modal bottom sheet with file actions**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-actions">Show actions</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-bottom-sheet id="actions" modal label="File actions">
  <md-gb-list>
    <md-gb-list-item>Share</md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-list-item>Get link</md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-list-item>Make a copy</md-gb-list-item>
  </md-gb-list>
</md-gb-bottom-sheet>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-actions').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#actions').show();
});
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Secondary content.** Sheets hold extra content and actions, not the main content of the app.
*   **Match the window size.** Use a [bottom sheet](#bottom-sheets) in compact and medium windows and a [side sheet](#side-sheets) in wider ones.
*   **Standard or modal.** A standard sheet sits beside the content so people can keep using it. A modal sheet blocks the page under a scrim until it is closed.

## Anatomy

A bottom sheet has a container and an optional drag handle. A side sheet adds a headline, a close button and actions.

**Example: A bottom sheet and a side sheet, each opened by a button**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-bottom">Bottom sheet</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-button id="open-side">Side sheet</md-gb-button>

<md-gb-bottom-sheet id="bottom" modal label="Share">
  <p>Share this photo with friends.</p>
</md-gb-bottom-sheet>

<md-gb-side-sheet id="side" modal>
  <span slot="headline">Filters</span>
  <p>Narrow the results by date or author.</p>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions">Apply</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-side-sheet>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-bottom').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#bottom').show();
});
document.querySelector('#open-side').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#side').show();
});
```

## Examples

### Bottom sheets

A bottom sheet rests at a partial height and expands when dragged or when its handle is activated. Without `modal` it is a standard sheet with no scrim. Set `state="expanded"` to open it at full height.

**Example: A bottom sheet that opens expanded**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-expanded">Show details</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-bottom-sheet id="expanded" modal state="expanded" label="Photo details">
  <p>Taken on June 3 in Lisbon.</p>
</md-gb-bottom-sheet>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-expanded').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#expanded').show();
});
```

### Without a drag handle

Add `hide-drag-handle` to remove the handle and dragging. Add `skip-partially-expanded` for a sheet that has no partial height.

**Example: A bottom sheet without a drag handle**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-plain">Show options</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-bottom-sheet id="plain" modal hide-drag-handle label="Sort options">
  <p>Sort by name, date, or size.</p>
</md-gb-bottom-sheet>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-plain').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#plain').show();
});
```

### Side sheets

A side sheet has a `headline`, a close button and an `actions` slot. Add `divider` to separate the actions, and `detached` to float the sheet with margins.

**Example: A modal side sheet with Save and Cancel actions**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-filters">Filters</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-side-sheet id="filters" modal headline="Filters">
  <p>Narrow the results by date or author.</p>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions">Save</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" color="outlined">Cancel</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-side-sheet>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-filters').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#filters').show();
});
```

### Back button

Set `has-back-button` on a side sheet to let people go back to an earlier region. The sheet fires `back` when it is pressed.

**Example: A side sheet with a back button**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-detail">Details</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-side-sheet id="detail" modal has-back-button headline="Details">
  <p>Created by Ada on May 2.</p>
</md-gb-side-sheet>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-detail').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#detail').show();
});
```

## Accessibility

*   A modal sheet is a `<dialog>`: focus moves into it, stays inside, and returns to the opener on close. Escape and a click on the scrim close it.
*   Name a bottom sheet with `label`. A side sheet is named by its `headline`, or by `label` when it has none.
*   The drag handle is a button, so keyboard users can expand and collapse the sheet. Localize `drag-handle-label`, `close-label` and `back-label`.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-bottom-sheet&gt;

A Material Design bottom sheet.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>closeLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the close icon button of a full-screen sheet.</span> | <code>close-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Close'</code> |
| <code>collapseLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the collapse icon button of a full-screen sheet.</span> | <code>collapse-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Collapse'</code> |
| <code>dragHandleLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the drag handle button.</span> | <code>drag-handle-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Drag handle'</code> |
| <code>hideDragHandle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to hide the drag handle (which also disables dragging).</span> | <code>hide-drag-handle</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the sheet dialog.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Bottom sheet'</code> |
| <code>modal</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the sheet is modal: shown above a scrim, blocking the rest of the page, and closed by Escape or a scrim click.</span> | <code>modal</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the sheet is open. Setting it calls <code>show()</code> or <code>close()</code>.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>quick</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to skip the opening and closing motion.</span> | <code>quick</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>skipPartiallyExpanded</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the sheet has no partially expanded height: it opens expanded and the drag handle closes it.</span> | <code>skip-partially-expanded</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>state</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The resting height while open: <code>partially-expanded</code> or <code>expanded</code>. Updated when the user drags or activates the drag handle.</span> | <code>state</code> | <code>BottomSheetState</code> | <code>BOTTOM_SHEET_STATES.partiallyExpanded</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The sheet content. It scrolls when taller than the sheet. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired when the sheet begins closing. Cancelable; canceling keeps it open. |
| <code>closed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired after the closing motion. |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the sheet begins opening. Cancelable. |
| <code>opened</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired after the opening motion. |
| <code>state-change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the user moves the sheet to another height (<code>state</code>). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Closes the sheet. Resolves after the closing motion. |
| <code>expand</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Expands the sheet to its full height. |
| <code>handleBack</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Handles a back request (the Android back gesture or button, which a modal sheet receives through its dialog): plays the predictive back motion and closes the sheet with reason <code>back</code>. If the <code>close</code> event is canceled, the sheet settles back. Resolves after the closing motion. Call it for an in-app back control that should behave like the system back. |
| <code>partialExpand</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Moves the sheet to its partially expanded height, when it has one. |
| <code>render</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; TemplateResult&lt;1&gt;</span> | Invoked on each update to perform rendering tasks. This method may return any value renderable by lit-html's <code>ChildPart</code> - typically a <code>TemplateResult</code>. Setting properties inside this method will *not* trigger the element to update. |
| <code>show</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens the sheet. Resolves after the opening motion. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(container)</code> | The sheet container. |
| <code>::part(content)</code> | The container of the default slot. |
| <code>::part(dialog)</code> | The <code>&lt;dialog&gt;</code> holding the sheet; its <code>::backdrop</code> is the scrim. |
| <code>::part(drag-handle)</code> | The drag handle button. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> | Container color. |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> | Container box shadow. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | Top corner radius. |
| <code>--drag-handle-color</code> | Drag handle color. |
| <code>--drag-handle-height</code> | Drag handle height. |
| <code>--drag-handle-padding-block</code> | Space above and below the drag handle. |
| <code>--drag-handle-width</code> | Drag handle width. |
| <code>--max-width</code> | Maximum container width. |
| <code>--partially-expanded-height</code> | Maximum visible height of a partially expanded modal sheet. |
| <code>--peek-height</code> | Visible height of a partially expanded standard sheet. |
| <code>--scrim-color</code> | Scrim color of a modal sheet. |
| <code>--scrim-opacity</code> | Scrim opacity of a modal sheet. |
| <code>--top-margin</code> | Minimum space above the expanded sheet. |
| <code>--wide-margin</code> | Top and side margins when the sheet is wider than its max width. |

### &lt;md-gb-side-sheet&gt;

A Material Design side sheet.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>backLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the back icon button.</span> | <code>back-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Back'</code> |
| <code>closeLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the close icon button.</span> | <code>close-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Close'</code> |
| <code>detached</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the sheet floats inset from the window edges with rounded corners, instead of touching them.</span> | <code>detached</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>divider</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to draw dividers: along the inline start edge of a standard docked sheet, and above the actions.</span> | <code>divider</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>gesturesDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to turn off swipe to dismiss on a modal sheet.</span> | <code>gestures-disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>hasBackButton</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to show the back icon button before the headline.</span> | <code>has-back-button</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>headline</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The headline text.</span> | <code>headline</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>hideCloseButton</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to hide the close icon button. Material requires a close affordance in every side sheet; provide another one when hiding it.</span> | <code>hide-close-button</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the sheet dialog, used when it has no headline.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>modal</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the sheet is modal: shown above a scrim, blocking the rest of the page, and closed by Escape or a scrim click.</span> | <code>modal</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the sheet is open. Setting it calls <code>show()</code> or <code>close()</code>.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>quick</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to skip the opening and closing motion.</span> | <code>quick</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The sheet content. It scrolls vertically when taller than the sheet. |
| <code>actions</code> | Action buttons at the bottom of the sheet, such as Save and Cancel. |
| <code>headline</code> | Headline content; replaces the <code>headline</code> text. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>back</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the back icon button is activated. |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired when the sheet begins closing. Cancelable; canceling keeps it open. |
| <code>closed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent&lt;&#123;reason: string&#125;&gt;</span> | Fired after the closing motion. |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the sheet begins opening. Cancelable. |
| <code>opened</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired after the opening motion. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(reason?: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Closes the sheet. Resolves after the closing motion. |
| <code>handleBack</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Handles a back request (the Android back gesture or button, which a modal sheet receives through its dialog): plays the predictive back motion and closes the sheet with reason <code>back</code>. If the <code>close</code> event is canceled, the sheet settles back. Resolves after the closing motion. Call it for an in-app back control that should behave like the system back. |
| <code>render</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; TemplateResult&lt;1&gt;</span> | Invoked on each update to perform rendering tasks. This method may return any value renderable by lit-html's <code>ChildPart</code> - typically a <code>TemplateResult</code>. Setting properties inside this method will *not* trigger the element to update. |
| <code>show</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens the sheet. Resolves after the opening motion. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(actions)</code> | The container of the actions slot. |
| <code>::part(container)</code> | The sheet container. |
| <code>::part(content)</code> | The container of the default slot. |
| <code>::part(dialog)</code> | The <code>&lt;dialog&gt;</code> holding the sheet; its <code>::backdrop</code> is the scrim. |
| <code>::part(header)</code> | The header row. |
| <code>::part(headline)</code> | The headline. |

| <code>--container-margin</code> | Inset from the window edges (16px when detached). |

| <code>--max-width</code> | Maximum container width. |
| <code>--padding-inline</code> | Start and end padding. |
| <code>--scrim-color</code> | Scrim color of a modal sheet. |
| <code>--scrim-opacity</code> | Scrim opacity of a modal sheet. |

# App Bar

An app bar sits at the top of a screen and shows its title, navigation and actions, and can hide or compress as the page scrolls.

**Example: An app bar with a menu button, a title, a subtitle and a search action**

```html
<md-gb-app-bar>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="leading" aria-label="Open menu">
    <md-gb-icon>menu</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  Inbox
  <span slot="subtitle">24 unread</span>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="trailing" aria-label="Search">
    <md-gb-icon>search</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
</md-gb-app-bar>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Keep it about the page.** An app bar shows the title, navigation and a few actions that belong to the current page.
*   **Limit the actions.** Show one action, two if needed, and put many actions in a toolbar. Avoid an overflow menu when you can.
*   **Pick a size.** Use [medium or large](#sizes) for a more expressive headline, and a [small](#sizes) bar once content scrolls.
*   **Let it respond to scrolling.** It can [hide or compress](#scroll-behavior) while people scroll.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

An app bar holds a leading navigation button, a title with an optional subtitle or image, and trailing actions.

**Example: An app bar with a leading button, a title, a subtitle and trailing actions**

```html
<md-gb-app-bar>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="leading" aria-label="Back">
    <md-gb-icon>arrow_back</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  Trip to Lisbon
  <span slot="subtitle">3 days</span>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="trailing" aria-label="Share">
    <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="trailing" aria-label="Favorite">
    <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
</md-gb-app-bar>
```

## Examples

### Sizes

Set `size` to `md` or `lg` for a taller bar. The default is `sm`.

**Example: A medium app bar with a back button and a title**

```html
<md-gb-app-bar size="md">
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="leading" aria-label="Back">
    <md-gb-icon>arrow_back</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  Settings
</md-gb-app-bar>
```

### Centered text

Add `centered` to center the title and subtitle.

**Example: An app bar with a centered title**

```html
<md-gb-app-bar centered>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="leading" aria-label="Open menu">
    <md-gb-icon>menu</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  Photos
</md-gb-app-bar>
```

### Search

Set `variant="search"` and put a text input in the `search` slot.

**Example: A search app bar**

```html
<md-gb-app-bar variant="search">
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="leading" aria-label="Back">
    <md-gb-icon>arrow_back</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  <input slot="search" type="search" aria-label="Search mail">
</md-gb-app-bar>
```

### Scroll behavior

Set `scroll-behavior` to `hide` to hide the bar while scrolling down, or to `compress` to turn a medium or large bar into a small one. Use `scroll-target` with the id of a scrolling element, or leave it out to follow the window.

**Example: A large app bar that compresses while its list scrolls**

*HTML*

```html
<div id="content">
  <md-gb-app-bar size="lg" scroll-behavior="compress" scroll-target="content">
    <md-gb-icon-button slot="leading" aria-label="Back">
      <md-gb-icon>arrow_back</md-gb-icon>
    </md-gb-icon-button>
    Recipes
  </md-gb-app-bar>
  <p>Lemon pasta</p>
  <p>Sourdough</p>
  <p>Pad thai</p>
  <p>Summer salad</p>
  <p>Tomato soup</p>
  <p>Apple pie</p>
  <p>Fried rice</p>
  <p>Banana bread</p>
</div>
```

*CSS*

```css
#content {
  inline-size: 100%;
  block-size: 280px;
  overflow: auto;
}

md-gb-app-bar {
  position: sticky;
  inset-block-start: 0;
}
```

### Overflow actions

On small windows only a few trailing actions show. The rest are listed in the `overflowchange` event, and the `overflow` slot holds a menu button that appears while actions are collapsed.

**Example: An app bar with trailing actions and an overflow button**

```html
<md-gb-app-bar>
  Gallery
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="trailing" aria-label="Search">
    <md-gb-icon>search</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="trailing" aria-label="Share">
    <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="trailing" aria-label="Favorite">
    <md-gb-icon>favorite</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
  <md-gb-icon-button slot="overflow" aria-label="More options">
    <md-gb-icon>more_vert</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-icon-button>
</md-gb-app-bar>
```

## Accessibility

*   The title is the app bar's text, so make it match the page. Add context in an `aria-label` if the title alone is unclear.
*   Label every icon-only button with `aria-label`.
*   Tab moves through the buttons, and Enter or Space activates the focused one.
*   A sticky or fixed app bar can cover focused content. Call `setupScrollPadding()` from `scroll-padding.js` so focused elements scroll clear of it.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-app-bar&gt;

A Material Design app bar component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>centered</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the title and subtitle are centered instead of leading-aligned (the M3 Expressive "centered text" configuration). Defaults to <code>false</code>.</span> | <code>centered</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>scrollBehavior</code><br><span class="gb-desc">How the app bar reacts to scrolling: <code>hide</code> (hide on scroll down, reveal on scroll up) or <code>compress</code> (medium and large flexible app bars become small until scrolled back to the top).</span> | <code>scroll-behavior</code> | <code>"hide" | "compress"</code> |  |
| <code>scrolled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the app bar is in its scrolled state. Defaults to <code>false</code>. A medium or large flexible app bar in its scrolled state is shown as a small one (app-bars.md: "When scrolled, medium flexible and large flexible app bars can transform into small app bars").</span> | <code>scrolled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>scrollTarget</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The id of the element whose scrolling drives <code>scroll-behavior</code>. Defaults to the window.</span> | <code>scroll-target</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>size</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The size of the app bar (<code>sm</code>, <code>md</code>, <code>lg</code>). Defaults to <code>sm</code>.</span> | <code>size</code> | <code>AppBarSize</code> | <code>'sm'</code> |
| <code>variant</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The behavioral variant of the app bar (<code>standard</code> or <code>search</code>). Defaults to <code>standard</code>.</span> | <code>variant</code> | <code>AppBarVariant</code> | <code>'standard'</code> |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/badge/

# Badge

A badge shows a small dot or a count to signal new or changed information.

**Example: A dot badge, a badge with a count and a badge with a capped count**

```html
<md-gb-badge></md-gb-badge>
<md-gb-badge>3</md-gb-badge>
<md-gb-badge>99+</md-gb-badge>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use a dot for something new.** A badge without content signals new or changed information.
*   **Use a count for a number.** A large badge shows a number, such as unread messages.
*   **Keep counts short.** Content is limited to four characters, including a `+`, so large numbers show as `999+`.
*   **Attach it to an icon.** [Anchor](#anchored) the badge to the top trailing corner of the icon it describes.

## Anatomy

A badge is a single element. Without content it is a dot; with content it is a larger badge.

**Example: A badge with a count of 5**

```html
<md-gb-badge>5</md-gb-badge>
```

## Examples

### Count

Set `value` to show a number. Counts above `max` (999 by default) show as `max+`.

**Example: A badge with a count over the maximum**

```html
<md-gb-badge value="1200"></md-gb-badge>
```

### Anchored

Add `anchored` to place the badge on the top trailing corner of its positioned parent.

**Example: A bell icon with a count badge**

```html
<span style="position: relative; display: inline-flex">
  <md-gb-icon>notifications</md-gb-icon>
  <md-gb-badge anchored>3</md-gb-badge>
</span>
```

## Accessibility

*   A dot badge is announced with its `label`, which defaults to "New notification". Set it to match your content.
*   Place the badge after the label of the destination it belongs to, so it is read in that order.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-badge&gt;

A Material Design badge component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>anchored</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Anchors the badge to the top trailing corner of its positioned parent (the icon's bounding box).</span> | <code>anchored</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Screen reader text for a small (non-counting) badge. Spec: non-counting badges announce "New notification", read after the destination's label.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'New notification'</code> |
| <code>max</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The largest count shown before it is truncated to <code>max+</code>.</span> | <code>max</code> | <code>number</code> | <code>999</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">A count to display. Counts above <code>max</code> show as <code>max+</code> (spec: limit content to four characters, including a +). Slotted content is shown when unset.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>number</code> |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The large badge's label, e.g. a count. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(badge)</code> | The badge container. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--padding-inline</code> |  |
| <code>--shape</code> |  |
| <code>--size</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/card/

# Card

A card contains content and actions about a single subject.

**Example: An outlined card with a headline, supporting text and two actions**

```html
<md-gb-card>
  <h2>Weekend in Lisbon</h2>
  <p>Flights and hotel for 2 nights.</p>
  <md-gb-button color="outlined">Details</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button color="filled">Book</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-card>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **One subject per card.** A card shows related content and actions about a single topic, arranged so the hierarchy is clear.
*   **Choose a color.** Use [elevated, filled or outlined](#colors) to set how much the card stands out from its background.
*   **Make it an entry point.** An [interactive card](#interactive) can lead to more detail or another page.
*   **Lay out collections.** Cards work in a grid, a vertical list or a carousel.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A card is a container with 16dp of inline padding around its content. The `container` slot replaces its background.

**Example: A card with a custom container and content**

```html
<md-gb-card>
  <div slot="container" style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
  Lemon pasta, ready in 20 minutes
</md-gb-card>
```

## Examples

### Colors

Set `color` to `elevated`, `filled` or `outlined` (default).

**Example: Elevated, filled and outlined cards**

```html
<md-gb-card color="elevated">Elevated</md-gb-card>
<md-gb-card color="filled">Filled</md-gb-card>
<md-gb-card color="outlined">Outlined</md-gb-card>
```

### Interactive

Add `interactive` to make the whole card a button. Add `href` to make it a link instead, and label it with `aria-label`.

**Example: A card that links to a details page**

```html
<md-gb-card interactive href="/trips/lisbon" aria-label="Open Weekend in Lisbon" color="filled">
  Weekend in Lisbon
</md-gb-card>
```

### Selectable

Add `selectable` to an interactive card so activating it toggles `selected`. A selected card shows a check mark.

**Example: A selectable card that starts selected**

```html
<md-gb-card interactive selectable selected aria-label="Weekend in Lisbon" color="filled">
  Weekend in Lisbon
</md-gb-card>
```

### Disabled

A `disabled` card can't be activated.

**Example: A disabled interactive card**

```html
<md-gb-card interactive disabled aria-label="Sold out" color="filled">
  Sold out
</md-gb-card>
```

## Accessibility

*   An interactive card has the button role, or the link role with `href`. Give it an accessible name with `aria-label` when its content isn't enough.
*   A card that isn't interactive is a plain container and needs no role. Its actions are focusable on their own.
*   Hide purely decorative images from assistive technology.
*   If a card can be dragged, offer a single-pointer alternative such as a menu with move and delete actions.
*   Tab moves to the next card or actionable element, and Enter or Space activates it.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-card&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The color of the card.</span> | <code>color</code> | <code>CardColor</code> | <code>'outlined'</code> |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the card is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>dragged</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the card is picked up and being dragged (raised elevation). The app moves the card. Spec Cards &gt; Accessibility &gt; Dragging and dismissing (WCAG 2.5.7): also offer a single-pointer alternative, e.g. a menu opened by tapping a "more" button or pressing and holding the card, with move and delete actions (see the "Reorder (drag or menu)" demo). Don't let the menu cover the card.</span> | <code>dragged</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Makes an interactive card a link (spec: directly actionable cards have the button or link role).</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>interactive</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the card is interactive.</span> | <code>interactive</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selectable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether an interactive card can be selected: activating it toggles <code>selected</code> (selection.md lists cards among the components that can be selected).</span> | <code>selectable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selected</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether a <code>selectable</code> card is selected. A selected card shows a check mark and a change in surface color.</span> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The link target, when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>''</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display the card's content. The card has 16dp left/right padding; set <code>--padding-inline: 0</code> for full-bleed content. Add padding to content, not the host &lt;md-gb-card&gt; element. |
| <code>container</code> | Used to set a custom background container for the card. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(card)</code> | The card's root element. |
| <code>::part(card-btn)</code> | The card's main action (a button, or a link when <code>href</code> is set), when interactive. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--disabled-content-opacity</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-color</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-width</code> |  |
| <code>--state-layer-color</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/carousel/

# Carousel

A carousel is a scrollable list of visual items that change size as they move through the layout.

**Example: A multi-browse carousel of three destinations**

```html
<md-gb-carousel aria-label="Destinations" style="--item-width: 186px">
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Mountains">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Mountains</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Coastline">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Coastline</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Desert">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Desert</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
</md-gb-carousel>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Lead with visuals.** Items emphasize an image and can carry a brief label that adapts to the item size.
*   **Choose a layout.** Use `multi-browse` for varied sizes, `hero` to feature an item, `uncontained` for items that run edge to edge, and `full-screen` for one item at a time.
*   **Match scrolling to the layout.** Snap scrolling suits multi-browse, hero and full-screen. Free scrolling suits uncontained.

This component is new in [M3 Expressive](https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive).

## Anatomy

A carousel holds `md-gb-carousel-item` elements. Each has a visual in its default slot and an optional label.

**Example: A carousel of three items, each with a visual and a label**

```html
<md-gb-carousel aria-label="Cities" style="--item-width: 186px">
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Lisbon">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Lisbon</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Kyoto">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Kyoto</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Oslo">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Oslo</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
</md-gb-carousel>
```

## Examples

### Hero

Set `layout="hero"` to feature a large item with small items beside it. Add `alignment="center"` to center it.

**Example: A hero carousel**

```html
<md-gb-carousel layout="hero" aria-label="Featured trips" style="--item-width: 186px">
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Mountains">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Coastline">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Desert">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
</md-gb-carousel>
```

### Uncontained

Set `layout="uncontained"` for items of one size that scroll freely. `uncontained-multi-aspect` allows items with different aspect ratios.

**Example: An uncontained carousel**

```html
<md-gb-carousel layout="uncontained" aria-label="Albums" style="--item-width: 186px">
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Morning">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Noon">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Evening">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Night">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Dawn">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
</md-gb-carousel>
```

### Linked items

Give an item `href` to make it a link. Without it, the item is a button.

**Example: Carousel items that link to pages**

```html
<md-gb-carousel aria-label="Destinations" style="--item-width: 186px">
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Mountains" href="/mountains">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Mountains</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Coastline" href="/coastline">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Coastline</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Desert" href="/desert">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
    <span slot="label">Desert</span>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
</md-gb-carousel>
```

### Scroll mode and orientation

Set `scroll-mode` to `snap` or `free`, and `orientation` to `horizontal` or `vertical`. The full-screen layout scrolls vertically by default.

**Example: A full-screen carousel that snaps to one story at a time**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-carousel layout="full-screen" scroll-mode="snap" aria-label="Stories">
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Morning">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-primary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Noon">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-secondary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
  <md-gb-carousel-item label="Evening">
    <div style="background: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary-container)"></div>
  </md-gb-carousel-item>
</md-gb-carousel>
```

*CSS*

```css
md-gb-carousel {
  inline-size: 100%;
  block-size: 280px;
}
```

## Accessibility

*   The carousel is a region with the role description "carousel". Name it with `aria-label`.
*   Each item's `label` is its accessible name, read with its position in the set.
*   Tab or the arrow keys move between items, and Enter or Space activates the focused one.
*   Give images a text alternative, or hide decorative ones.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-carousel&gt;

A Material Design carousel.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>alignment</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Start or center alignment of the hero layout.</span> | <code>alignment</code> | <code>CarouselAlignment</code> | <code>'start'</code> |
| <code>layout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The carousel layout.</span> | <code>layout</code> | <code>CarouselLayout</code> | <code>'multi-browse'</code> |
| <code>orientation</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The scrolling axis. Defaults to vertical for the full-screen layout and horizontal for the others.</span> | <code>orientation</code> | <code>CarouselOrientation</code> |  |
| <code>scrollMode</code><br><span class="gb-desc"><code>snap</code> snaps items into the layout when released; <code>free</code> lets them stop anywhere. Defaults to <code>free</code> for uncontained layouts and <code>snap</code> for the others.</span> | <code>scroll-mode</code> | <code>CarouselScrollMode</code> |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The <code>md-gb-carousel-item</code> elements. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>next</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(behavior?: ScrollBehavior) =&gt; void</span> | Scrolls to the next item. |
| <code>previous</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(behavior?: ScrollBehavior) =&gt; void</span> | Scrolls to the previous item. |
| <code>relayout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Recomputes the layout. The carousel does this on resize and when items or properties change; call it after changing <code>--item-width</code> or other layout tokens. |
| <code>scrollToItem</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(index: number, behavior?: ScrollBehavior) =&gt; void</span> | Scrolls an item to its snapped position in the layout. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(carousel)</code> | The container. |
| <code>::part(scroller)</code> | The scroll container (<code>role="list"</code>). |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> | Item container color, behind its visual. |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> | Item elevation. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | Item corner radius. |
| <code>--full-screen-item-spacing</code> | Space between full-screen items. |
| <code>--height</code> | Carousel height (default 221px, Compose samples). |
| <code>--item-spacing</code> | Space between items. |
| <code>--item-width</code> | Preferred large item width (multi-browse, hero) or item width (uncontained). <code>auto</code> picks a layout default. |
| <code>--label-padding</code> | Item label padding. |
| <code>--label-scrim-color</code> | Scrim behind item labels. |
| <code>--label-text</code> | Item label typography. |
| <code>--label-text-axes</code> | Item label font variation settings. |
| <code>--label-text-color</code> | Item label color. |
| <code>--label-text-tracking</code> | Item label letter spacing. |
| <code>--padding-block</code> | Top/bottom container padding. |
| <code>--padding-inline</code> | Leading/trailing container padding. |
| <code>--small-item-max-width</code> | Maximum small item width. |
| <code>--small-item-min-width</code> | Minimum small item width. |

### &lt;md-gb-carousel-item&gt;

A Material Design carousel item.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Makes the item a link to this URL.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>label</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The accessible name of the item. Defaults to its label text.</span> | <code>label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>outlined</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item has an outline (<code>with-outline</code> tokens).</span> | <code>outlined</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The link target, with <code>href</code>.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The item visual, such as an <code>&lt;img&gt;</code> or <code>&lt;video&gt;</code>. It is sized to cover the item. |
| <code>label</code> | Brief label text shown over the visual. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(action)</code> | The button or link that activates the item. |
| <code>::part(content)</code> | The masked visual and label. |
| <code>::part(frame)</code> | The masked outline, elevation and focus ring. |
| <code>::part(item)</code> | The item root. |
| <code>::part(label)</code> | The label container. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--carousel-item-fraction</code> | Read-only: the item's current size between the carousel's smallest (0) and large (1) item sizes. |
| <code>--carousel-item-size</code> | Read-only: the item's current masked size along the scrolling axis. |
| <code>--with-outline-outline-color</code> | Outline color of outlined items. |
| <code>--with-outline-outline-width</code> | Outline width of outlined items. |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/checkbox/

# Checkbox

Checkboxes let people select one or more items from a set, or turn an option on or off.

**Example: A checkbox with the label Remember me**

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox></md-gb-checkbox>
  Remember me
</label>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Select from a set.** Use checkboxes when people can pick any number of options from a list, or to turn one option on or off.
*   **Label every checkbox.** The label is the adjacent text, and it should say what checking the box does.
*   **Use a parent for a group.** A parent checkbox shows an [indeterminate](#indeterminate) state when only some of its children are checked.
*   **Don't apply density by default.** Let people opt in to a [denser layout](#density).

## Anatomy

A checkbox is one element. A `<label>` next to it, or around it, provides the text.

**Example: A checkbox inside a label**

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox></md-gb-checkbox>
  Send me updates
</label>
```

## Examples

### Checked and indeterminate

Add `checked` for a selected checkbox. Add `indeterminate` for a parent whose children are partly selected.

**Example: A checked checkbox and an indeterminate checkbox**

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox checked></md-gb-checkbox>
  Email
</label>
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox indeterminate></md-gb-checkbox>
  All notifications
</label>
```

### Error

Add `error` to mark a checkbox as invalid. With `required`, it must be checked to submit a form.

**Example: A required checkbox in the error state**

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox required error></md-gb-checkbox>
  I accept the terms
</label>
```

### Disabled

A `disabled` checkbox can't be changed.

**Example: A disabled checkbox**

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox disabled></md-gb-checkbox>
  Unavailable option
</label>
```

### Density

Set `density` from 0 (default) to -3 to shrink the checkbox. The touch target stays 48px.

**Example: A checkbox with density -2**

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox density="-2"></md-gb-checkbox>
  Compact option
</label>
```

### Parent and children

Call `linkParentCheckbox(parent, children)` from `checkbox-group.js`. Checking the parent checks every child, and a partial selection makes the parent indeterminate.

**Example: A parent checkbox linked to two child checkboxes**

*HTML*

```html
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox id="all"></md-gb-checkbox>
  All notifications
</label>
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox class="channel" checked></md-gb-checkbox>
  Email
</label>
<label>
  <md-gb-checkbox class="channel"></md-gb-checkbox>
  Push
</label>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {linkParentCheckbox} from '@material/web/labs/gb/components/checkbox/checkbox-group.js';

const parent = document.querySelector('md-gb-checkbox#all')!;
const children = [...document.querySelectorAll('md-gb-checkbox.channel')];
linkParentCheckbox(parent, children);
```

## Accessibility

*   The adjacent `<label>` text is the checkbox's accessible name. Use `aria-label` when there is no visible label or it needs more detail.
*   Space toggles the focused checkbox, and Tab moves between checkboxes.
*   A checkbox exposes its checked, unchecked or mixed state.

**Example: A checkbox with only an aria-label**

```html
<md-gb-checkbox aria-label="Select all messages"></md-gb-checkbox>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-checkbox&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>checked</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the checkbox is selected.</span> | <code>checked</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the checkbox's layout box (48px) and state layer (40px); the touch target stays 48px. Values are clamped to that range. checkbox.md: don't apply density by default; let people opt in to a denser layout.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>error</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the checkbox is invalid.</span> | <code>error</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>indeterminate</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the checkbox is indeterminate. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#indeterminate_state_checkboxes</span> | <code>indeterminate</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>required</code><br><span class="gb-desc">When true, require the checkbox to be selected when participating in form submission. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#validation</span> | <code>required</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The value of the checkbox that is submitted with a form when selected. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#value</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'on'</code> |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the checkbox is checked or unchecked. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">InputEvent</span> | Fired when the checkbox is checked or unchecked. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(checkbox)</code> | The checkbox's root element. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--container-size</code> |  |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Size removed per density step. |
| <code>--icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-color</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-width</code> |  |
| <code>--state-layer-color</code> |  |
| <code>--state-layer-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--state-layer-size</code> | State layer size at density 0. |
| <code>--target-size</code> | The minimum touch target size, kept at any density. |
