Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/chip/

# Chips

Chips help people enter information, make selections, filter content, or trigger actions.

**Example: Filter chips in a labeled chip set**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Meal filters">
  <md-gb-chip type="filter" selected>Breakfast</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">Lunch</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">Dinner</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Pick the type by purpose.** [Assist](#assist-chips) chips are smart actions, [filter](#filter-chips) chips filter content, [input](#input-chips) chips are information a person entered, and [suggestion](#suggestion-chips) chips offer dynamic replies or queries.
*   **Show chips as a set.** Unlike buttons, chips appear dynamically as a group, so always place them in a [chip set](#chip-set).
*   **Elevate only for protection.** Use [elevated](#assist-chips) chips when they sit on an image or a busy background.
*   **Keep them compact.** Reduce [density](#density) when space is tight.

## Anatomy

A chip set holds chips, and each chip holds its label and optional icons.

**Example: A chip set with a chip that has a leading and a trailing icon**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Places">
  <md-gb-chip>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">place</md-gb-icon>
    <md-gb-icon slot="trailing-icon">arrow_drop_down</md-gb-icon>
    Nearby
  </md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip>Open late</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

## Examples

### Assist chips

Assist chips are smart or automated actions, such as adding an event to a calendar. They are the default `type`, can link with `href`, and can be elevated.

**Example: An assist chip with an icon and an assist chip that links to a page**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Event actions">
  <md-gb-chip>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">event</md-gb-icon>
    Add to calendar
  </md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip href="https://m3.material.io/components/chips">
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">open_in_new</md-gb-icon>
    Guidelines
  </md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

### Filter chips

Filter chips use tags or descriptive words to filter content and can replace toggle buttons or checkboxes. Set `type="filter"` and use `selected` for chosen ones.

**Example: Filter chips, one selected, one with a trailing icon**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Filters">
  <md-gb-chip type="filter" selected>Open now</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">
    Price
    <md-gb-icon slot="trailing-icon">arrow_drop_down</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

### Input chips

Input chips are discrete pieces of information a person entered, such as contacts. Set `type="input"`; add `removable` for a remove button and `editable` to let people edit the text. Icons and avatars go in the `icon` slot.

**Example: Removable input chips, one with an icon**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Attendees">
  <md-gb-chip type="input" removable>Hiking</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="input" removable>
    <md-gb-icon slot="icon">person</md-gb-icon>
    Ada
  </md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

### Suggestion chips

Suggestion chips narrow a person's intent with dynamically generated suggestions, such as possible replies.

**Example: Suggested replies**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Suggested replies">
  <md-gb-chip type="suggestion">Sounds good</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="suggestion" elevated>See you then</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

### Chip set

The chip set manages selection (`selection="single"` or `"multiple"`) and arrow-key navigation, and wraps chips by default. With `selection="single"`, add `required` so the selected chip can't be unselected, or `single-line` to scroll instead of wrap.

**Example: A single-select chip set with a heading**

```html
<h3 id="size-label">Size</h3>
<md-gb-chip-set aria-labelledby="size-label" selection="single" required>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter" selected>Small</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">Medium</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">Large</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

### Density

Set `density` on the chip set from 0 (default) to -3 to remove 4px of height per step.

**Example: A chip set with a density of -2**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Compact filters" density="-2">
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">Lunch</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip type="filter">Dinner</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

### Disabled and soft-disabled

A `soft-disabled` chip stays focusable so screen reader users can discover actions that are not available yet, such as Copy before text is selected.

**Example: A disabled chip and a soft-disabled chip**

```html
<md-gb-chip-set aria-label="Edit actions">
  <md-gb-chip disabled>Disabled</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip soft-disabled>Soft-disabled</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

## Accessibility

*   A chip set is a grid of chips: label it with [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) or [`aria-labelledby`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-labelledby).
*   Add an `aria-label` to chips whose text needs to be more descriptive.
*   The set is one tab stop; arrow keys, Home and End move between chips, and Backspace or Delete removes a removable chip.
*   Disabled chips leave the focus order; use `soft-disabled` where discoverability matters, per the [ARIA guidance on disabled controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_disabled_controls).

**Example: A chip set labelled by a heading, with chips that have a longer aria-label**

```html
<h3 id="dates-label">Dates</h3>
<md-gb-chip-set aria-labelledby="dates-label">
  <md-gb-chip aria-label="Monday" type="filter">Mon</md-gb-chip>
  <md-gb-chip aria-label="Tuesday" type="filter">Tue</md-gb-chip>
</md-gb-chip-set>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-chip&gt;

A Material Design Expressive Chip component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code> | <code>color</code> | <code>ChipColor</code> | <code>"flat"</code> |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the container height (32px); the label and icons keep their size and the touch target stays 48px (chips.md: "regardless of placement or density"). Values are clamped to that range. Density 0 inherits the density of an enclosing <code>md-gb-chip-set</code>. chips.md: don't apply density by default; let people opt in to a denser layout.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the chip is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>dragged</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the chip is being dragged (spec dragged state elevation).</span> | <code>dragged</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>editable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the text of an input chip can be edited (chips.md "Input chips": "Input chips can support editing to change their contents, such as correcting an email address"). Editing starts by interacting with the chip: a second click, Enter or Space on the selected chip, or a double click. Committing with Enter or by leaving the field changes the chip's text and fires <code>edit</code>; Escape (or emptying the text) keeps the old text.</span> | <code>editable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>elevated</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Elevated container, for chips on images or complex backgrounds. Input chips have no elevated style.</span> | <code>elevated</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>groupDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the chip's set is disabled (a disabled form fieldset).</span> |  | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>href</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The URL destination; makes an assist chip a link.</span> | <code>href</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>referrerPolicy</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Sets the underlying <code>HTMLAnchorElement</code>'s <code>referrerpolicy</code> attribute when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>referrerpolicy</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>rel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Sets the underlying <code>HTMLAnchorElement</code>'s <code>rel</code> attribute when <code>href</code> is set.</span> | <code>rel</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>removable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the chip has a remove button (input chips).</span> | <code>removable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>removeLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The remove button's accessible label. Defaults to "Remove &#123;chip label&#125;" (spec: the remove action is labeled separately).</span> | <code>remove-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>selected</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the filter (or input) chip is selected.</span> | <code>selected</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>softDisabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the chip is soft-disabled (<code>aria-disabled="true"</code> while preserving focusability).</span> | <code>soft-disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>target</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Where to display the linked <code>href</code> URL for a link chip.</span> | <code>target</code> | <code>"" | "_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top"</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>type</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The chip type: <code>assist</code> (default), <code>filter</code>, <code>input</code> or <code>suggestion</code>.</span> | <code>type</code> | <code>ChipType</code> | <code>"assist"</code> |
| <code>value</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The value a chip set submits while the chip is selected. Defaults to the label text, like a native <code>&lt;option&gt;</code>.</span> | <code>value</code> | <code>string</code> |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The chip label text. |
| <code>icon</code> | An optional leading icon, or an avatar (<code>class="chip-avatar"</code> or an <code>&lt;img&gt;</code>; input chips). |
| <code>remove-icon</code> | The remove button icon when <code>removable</code> (default: the <code>close</code> symbol). |
| <code>trailing-icon</code> | An optional trailing icon (filter chips, e.g. a drop-down arrow). |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when a filter chip's selection changes. |
| <code>edit</code><br><span class="gb-desc">CustomEvent</span> | Fired when an <code>editable</code> chip's new text is committed; <code>detail</code> has <code>value</code> and <code>previousValue</code>. |
| <code>input</code><br><span class="gb-desc">InputEvent</span> | Fired when a filter chip's selection changes. |
| <code>remove</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the remove button is activated, or Backspace / Delete is pressed on a removable chip. |
| <code>update-focus</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when <code>disabled</code> changes, so a chip set can update its tab stop. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>cancelEdit</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Ends editing and keeps the old text. |
| <code>commitEdit</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Ends editing and applies the new text (empty or unchanged text keeps the old). |
| <code>focus</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(options?: FocusOptions &amp; &#123; trailing?: boolean; &#125;) =&gt; void</span> | Focuses the chip's primary action, or its remove button with <code>&#123;trailing: true&#125;</code> (chip set navigation backwards into a chip). |
| <code>startEdit</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Turns an editable input chip into a text string to edit. Does nothing for other chips. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(chip)</code> | The root container element. |

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--avatar-opacity</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-size</code> |  |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--container-height</code> | Container height at density 0. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Container height removed per density step. |
| <code>--icon-label-space</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-color</code> |  |
| <code>--outline-width</code> |  |
| <code>--target-size</code> | The minimum touch target size, kept at any density. |
| <code>--trailing-icon-color</code> |  |

| <code>--trailing-space</code> |  |

### &lt;md-gb-chip-set&gt;

A Material Design Expressive chip set.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density of the chips, from 0 (default) to -3: each step down removes 4px from the chips' height. A chip's own non-zero <code>density</code> wins. Values are clamped to that range.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>required</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Single-select: the selected chip can't be unselected.</span> | <code>required</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selection</code><br><span class="gb-desc">How many filter chips can be selected: <code>none</code>, <code>single</code> or <code>multiple</code>.</span> | <code>selection</code> | <code>SelectionMode</code> | <code>"multiple"</code> |

| --- | --- |
| default | The chips. |

| --- | --- |
| <code>--chip-set-overflow-inset</code> | Room kept for touch targets and focus rings when a single-line set clips its overflow. |
| <code>--chip-set-space</code> | The space between chips and between lines. |

# Dialogs

Dialogs provide important prompts in a user flow.

**Example: A button that opens a dialog asking to delete messages**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-delete">Delete</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-dialog id="delete-dialog">
  <span slot="headline">Permanently delete?</span>
  Deleting the selected messages also removes them from your other devices.
  <form id="delete-form" method="dialog"></form>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" form="delete-form" value="cancel">Cancel</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" form="delete-form" value="delete">Delete</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-dialog>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-delete').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#delete-dialog').show();
});
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use them sparingly.** A dialog interrupts people to ask for a decision or to show critical information, so it blocks the rest of the app until it is dismissed.
*   **Pick the right priority.** For low or medium priority information, use a snackbar instead.
*   **Choose basic or full-screen.** Use a basic dialog by default. A [full-screen dialog](#full-screen) suits compact windows with a lot of content.
*   **Order the actions.** Put the dismissive action first and the confirming action last.

## Anatomy

A dialog has an optional icon and headline, supporting content, and actions.

**Example: A dialog with an icon, headline, supporting text and actions**

```html
<md-gb-dialog open quick>
  <md-gb-icon slot="icon">info</md-gb-icon>
  <span slot="headline">Discard draft?</span>
  Your draft will be deleted.
  <md-gb-button slot="actions">Cancel</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions">Discard</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-dialog>
```

## Examples

### With an icon

Put an `md-gb-icon` in the `icon` slot to center the headline under a hero icon.

**Example: A dialog with a hero icon**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-reset">Reset</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-dialog id="reset-dialog">
  <md-gb-icon slot="icon">restart_alt</md-gb-icon>
  <span slot="headline">Reset settings?</span>
  This returns your preferences to their defaults.
  <form id="reset-form" method="dialog"></form>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" form="reset-form" value="cancel">Cancel</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" form="reset-form" value="reset">Reset</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-dialog>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-reset').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#reset-dialog').show();
});
```

### Full-screen

Set `full-screen` for a dialog that fills a compact window, with a close button and the confirming action in its header. Above compact sizes it falls back to a basic dialog; add `always-full-screen` to keep it.

**Example: A full-screen dialog for a new event**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-event">New event</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-dialog id="event-dialog" full-screen>
  <span slot="headline">New event</span>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions">Save</md-gb-button>
  <label>
    Event name
    <input type="text">
  </label>
</md-gb-dialog>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
document.querySelector('#open-event').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#event-dialog').show();
});
```

### Return value

A button's `value` becomes the dialog's `returnValue` when it closes the dialog through its form. Read it in the `closed` event.

**Example: A dialog that reports which button closed it**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open-archive">Archive</md-gb-button>
<p id="result" role="status"></p>
<md-gb-dialog id="archive-dialog">
  <span slot="headline">Archive this thread?</span>
  It moves out of your inbox.
  <form id="archive-form" method="dialog"></form>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" form="archive-form" value="cancel">Cancel</md-gb-button>
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" form="archive-form" value="archive">Archive</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-dialog>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
const dialog = document.querySelector('#archive-dialog');
document.querySelector('#open-archive').addEventListener('click', () => {
  dialog.show();
});
dialog.addEventListener('closed', () => {
  document.querySelector('#result').textContent =
    dialog.returnValue === 'archive' ? 'Archived' : 'Canceled';
});
```

### Opening and closing

Open and close a dialog with `show()` and `close()`, or by setting `open`. Both methods return a promise that resolves after the animation. Cancel the `cancel` event to keep the dialog open.

**Example: Buttons that open and close a dialog from script**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="open">Open</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-dialog id="note-dialog">
  <span slot="headline">Reminder</span>
  This dialog closes itself after three seconds.
  <md-gb-button slot="actions" id="close">Close now</md-gb-button>
</md-gb-dialog>
```

*JavaScript*

```js
const dialog = document.querySelector('#note-dialog');
document.querySelector('#open').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  await dialog.show();
  setTimeout(() => dialog.close(), 3000);
});
document.querySelector('#close').addEventListener('click', () => dialog.close());
```

## Accessibility

*   The headline names the dialog. Add `aria-label` to a dialog without a headline.
*   A basic dialog is an alert dialog (`role="alertdialog"`) by default, as M3 asks for on the web. Set `type="dialog"` for a plain dialog.
*   Focus moves into the dialog and Tab cycles inside it. Escape closes it and focus returns to what opened it.
*   Label buttons and fields inside the dialog as you would elsewhere. In a full-screen dialog, set `close-label` to name the close button.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-dialog&gt;

A Material Design dialog component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>alwaysFullScreen</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Full-screen dialogs are for compact windows only (dialogs.md: use a basic dialog at medium and expanded). So <code>full-screen</code> applies at compact windows and the dialog is a basic dialog above, with the same slots. The host gets <code>adaptive-basic</code> while it falls back. Set <code>always-full-screen</code> to keep the full-screen variant at every window size.</span> | <code>always-full-screen</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>closeLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Accessible label of the full-screen close icon button.</span> | <code>close-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>'Close'</code> |
| <code>fullScreen</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Uses the full-screen variant: the dialog fills the window, with a header holding a close icon button, the headline and the confirm action. Meant for compact windows; use a basic dialog at larger breakpoints.</span> | <code>full-screen</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>noFocusTrap</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Turns off focus trapping, which keeps Tab and Shift+Tab cycling inside the dialog. Trapping is recommended for accessibility.</span> | <code>no-focus-trap</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Opens the dialog when set to <code>true</code> and closes it when set to <code>false</code>.</span> | <code>open</code> | <code>boolean</code> |  |
| <code>quick</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Skips the opening and closing animations.</span> | <code>quick</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>returnValue</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The dialog's return value, usually which button closed it. Set by <code>close(returnValue)</code> and by <code>&lt;form method="dialog"&gt;</code> submitters' <code>value</code>. Canceling (Escape, scrim, close button) leaves it unchanged. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/returnValue</span> |  | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>type</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The dialog's accessibility role. <code>alert</code> (<code>role="alertdialog"</code>) or <code>dialog</code> (<code>role="dialog"</code>). When empty, basic dialogs are alert dialogs, as the spec asks for on the web, and full-screen dialogs are dialogs.</span> | <code>type</code> | <code>DialogType</code> | <code>''</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The supporting text or custom content (lists, form fields). Scrolls between the pinned headline and actions when it overflows. |
| <code>actions</code> | The action buttons, dismissive first and confirming last. Basic: end-aligned below the content. Full-screen: the confirm action at the end of the header. |
| <code>headline</code> | The headline. Labels the dialog (<code>aria-labelledby</code>). |
| <code>icon</code> | An optional hero icon above the headline (basic only). Centers the headline. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>cancel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the dialog is canceled with Escape, a scrim click or the full-screen close button. Cancelable; canceling keeps the dialog open. |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the dialog begins closing; <code>returnValue</code> is already set. Cancelable. |
| <code>closed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the dialog has closed and animations finished. |
| <code>open</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the dialog begins opening. Cancelable. |
| <code>opened</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | Fired when the dialog has opened and animations finished. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(returnValue?: string, reason?: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Closes the dialog and fires a cancelable <code>close</code> event, then <code>closed</code> after the exit animation. Focus returns to the element focused before the dialog opened. |
| <code>show</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> | Opens the dialog as a modal and fires a cancelable <code>open</code> event, then <code>opened</code> after the enter animation. Focus moves to the first child with an <code>autofocus</code> attribute, else the first focusable element, else the dialog. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(actions)</code> | The actions container. |
| <code>::part(close-button)</code> | The full-screen close icon button. |
| <code>::part(content)</code> | The content container. |
| <code>::part(header)</code> | The headline region (full-screen: the header bar). |
| <code>::part(headline)</code> | The headline element. |
| <code>::part(icon)</code> | The hero icon container. |
| <code>::part(scroller)</code> | The scroll container of the content. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--action-focus-label-text-color</code> | Action label text color when focused. |
| <code>--action-hover-label-text-color</code> | Action label text color when hovered. |
| <code>--action-label-text</code> | Action label typography. |
| <code>--action-label-text-axes</code> | Action label typography font variation settings. |
| <code>--action-label-text-color</code> | Action label text color. |
| <code>--action-label-text-tracking</code> | Action label letter spacing. |
| <code>--action-pressed-label-text-color</code> | Action label text color when pressed. |
| <code>--container-color</code> | Container background color. |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> | Container box shadow elevation. |
| <code>--container-shape</code> | Container border radius. |
| <code>--header-action-label-text</code> | Full-screen action label typography. |
| <code>--header-action-label-text-axes</code> | Full-screen action label typography font variation settings. |
| <code>--header-action-label-text-color</code> | Full-screen action label color. |
| <code>--header-action-label-text-tracking</code> | Full-screen action label letter spacing. |
| <code>--header-container-color</code> | Full-screen header color. |
| <code>--header-container-elevation</code> | Full-screen header elevation. |
| <code>--header-container-height</code> | Full-screen header height. |
| <code>--header-headline</code> | Full-screen headline typography. |
| <code>--header-headline-axes</code> | Full-screen headline typography font variation settings. |
| <code>--header-headline-color</code> | Full-screen headline color. |
| <code>--header-headline-tracking</code> | Full-screen headline letter spacing. |
| <code>--header-icon-color</code> | Full-screen close icon color. |
| <code>--header-icon-size</code> | Full-screen close icon size. |
| <code>--header-on-scroll-container-color</code> | Full-screen header color when the content is scrolled. |
| <code>--header-on-scroll-container-elevation</code> | Full-screen header elevation when the content is scrolled. |
| <code>--headline</code> | Headline typography. |
| <code>--headline-axes</code> | Headline typography font variation settings. |
| <code>--headline-color</code> | Headline color. |
| <code>--headline-tracking</code> | Headline letter spacing. |
| <code>--max-width</code> | Basic dialog maximum width. |
| <code>--min-width</code> | Basic dialog minimum width. |
| <code>--scrim-color</code> | Scrim color. |
| <code>--scrim-opacity</code> | Scrim opacity. |
| <code>--supporting-text</code> | Supporting text typography. |
| <code>--supporting-text-axes</code> | Supporting text typography font variation settings. |
| <code>--supporting-text-color</code> | Supporting text color. |
| <code>--supporting-text-tracking</code> | Supporting text letter spacing. |
| <code>--with-icon-icon-color</code> | Hero icon color. |
| <code>--with-icon-icon-size</code> | Hero icon size. |

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/divider/

# Divider

A divider is a thin line that groups content in lists and containers.

**Example: A divider between two paragraphs**

```html
<p>Your order has shipped.</p>
<md-gb-divider></md-gb-divider>
<p>Delivery is expected on Friday.</p>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Group and create hierarchy.** Dividers visually group components and can imply a parent and child relationship.
*   **Full width for sections.** Use [full-width](#insets) dividers to separate larger sections of unrelated content.
*   **Inset for related items.** Use [inset dividers](#insets) to separate related content within a section, such as items in a list.
*   **Don't overuse.** Spacing and type styles often separate content well enough on their own.

## Anatomy

A divider is a single element.

**Example: A divider between two list rows**

```html
<p>Inbox</p>
<md-gb-divider></md-gb-divider>
<p>Sent</p>
```

## Examples

### Insets

Add `inset` to indent both ends by 16dp. Use `inset-start` or `inset-end` to indent only one end.

**Example: A full-width divider, a start-inset divider and a middle-inset divider**

```html
<md-gb-divider></md-gb-divider>
<md-gb-divider inset-start></md-gb-divider>
<md-gb-divider inset></md-gb-divider>
```

### Vertical

Add `vertical` for a divider between side-by-side content.

**Example: A vertical divider between two labels**

```html
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
  <span>Day</span>
  <md-gb-divider vertical></md-gb-divider>
  <span>Week</span>
</div>
```

### Class API

For plain HTML, the divider classes style a native `<hr>`. `divider()` is a Lit directive that adds them, and `dividerClasses()` returns them for other code. Pass `{vertical: true}` for a vertical divider.

**Example: A native hr styled as a vertical divider with the divider classes**

*HTML*

```html
<span>Day</span>
<hr id="rule">
<span>Week</span>
```

*CSS*

```css
@import '@material/web/labs/gb/components/divider/divider.css';

#rule {
  align-self: stretch;
}
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
import {dividerClasses} from '@material/web/labs/gb/components/divider/divider.js';

const classes = dividerClasses({vertical: true});
document.querySelector('#rule')!.className = Object.keys(classes)
  .filter((name) => classes[name])
  .join(' ');
```

## Accessibility

*   A divider is decorative and not announced by assistive technology. It has no contrast minimum.
*   Add `role="separator"` to a divider that should be announced.

**Example: A divider announced as a separator**

```html
<p>Account</p>
<md-gb-divider role="separator"></md-gb-divider>
<p>Privacy</p>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-divider&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>inset</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Indents both ends 16dp (spec: middle-inset divider).</span> | <code>inset</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>insetEnd</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Indents the trailing end 16dp.</span> | <code>inset-end</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>insetStart</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Indents the leading end 16dp (spec: inset divider).</span> | <code>inset-start</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>vertical</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether or not the divider is vertical.</span> | <code>vertical</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(divider)</code> | The divider element. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--color</code> |  |
| <code>--inset-leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--inset-trailing-space</code> |  |
| <code>--thickness</code> |  |

---

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/list/

# Lists

Lists are continuous, vertical indexes of text and images, with optional selection, reordering, expanding and swipe actions.

**Example: A segmented list of three items with supporting and trailing text**

```html
<md-gb-list segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">celebration</md-gb-icon>
    Festivals
    <span slot="supporting-text">Food, music, arts, community</span>
    <span slot="trailing-text">May 8</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">palette</md-gb-icon>
    Arts
    <span slot="supporting-text">Literature, games, music</span>
    <span slot="trailing-text">May 12</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">groups</md-gb-icon>
    Family and friends
    <span slot="supporting-text">The relationships that bring and bind</span>
    <span slot="trailing-text">May 20</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Make items easy to scan.** Keep labels short, order items in a logical way such as alphabetical or numerical, and show icons, text and actions in a consistent format.
*   **Choose a style.** A standard list is flat; a [segmented](#segmented) list separates each item into its own container.
*   **Match the item to its content.** Add [supporting text](#slots), an overline, an avatar or a leading icon to describe what an item is.
*   **Add behavior when it helps.** Lists can [select](#selection), [reorder](#reordering), [expand](#expandable-items) and reveal [swipe actions](#swipe-actions).

## Anatomy

A list holds list items. Each item has a label and slots around it.

**Example: A list item with every part filled in**

```html
<md-gb-list aria-label="Messages">
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <div slot="avatar">A</div>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">mail</md-gb-icon>
    <span slot="overline">Inbox</span>
    Ada Lovelace
    <span slot="supporting-text">Notes on the engine</span>
    <span slot="trailing-text">9:41 AM</span>
    <md-gb-icon slot="trailing">star</md-gb-icon>
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

## Examples

### Slots

An item's label is its default slot. Put an `md-gb-icon` in `leading`, a circular image or initial in `avatar`, a small line above the label in `overline`, and more detail in `supporting-text`.

**Example: Items with a leading icon, an overline and trailing text**

```html
<md-gb-list>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">mail</md-gb-icon>
    <span slot="overline">Inbox</span>
    Weekly digest
    <span slot="supporting-text">Your summary for the last seven days</span>
    <span slot="trailing-text">9:41 AM</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">mail</md-gb-icon>
    <span slot="overline">Inbox</span>
    Trip itinerary
    <span slot="supporting-text">Flights, hotel and reservations</span>
    <span slot="trailing-text">Yesterday</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Segmented

Add `segmented` to show each item in its own container, separated by a small gap.

**Example: A segmented list of three items**

```html
<md-gb-list segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item>Apples</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Bananas</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Cucumbers</md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Non-interactive items

Add `static` to an item that only displays information, so it has no hover, focus or press states.

**Example: A list of static items with dates**

```html
<md-gb-list segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item static>
    The first computer (ENIAC)
    <span slot="trailing-text">1946</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item static>
    Sputnik launched into space
    <span slot="trailing-text">1957</span>
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Selection

Add `selectable` to let people select several items with a long press, and by tapping while in selection mode. The list fires `itemselectionchange`, and selected items have `checked`. Add `selection-primary` when selecting is the main task, to always show the checkboxes.

**Example: A selectable list of photos**

```html
<md-gb-list selectable segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">image</md-gb-icon>
    Beach
  </md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">image</md-gb-icon>
    Forest
  </md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">image</md-gb-icon>
    Mountains
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Reordering

Add `reorderable` to show a drag handle on every item. People can drag it, or tap it and use the move up and move down buttons. The list fires a cancelable `reorder` event.

**Example: A reorderable list of recipe steps**

```html
<md-gb-list reorderable segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item>Preheat the oven</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Mix the dough</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Let it rise</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Bake for 40 minutes</md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Expandable items

Add `expandable` to an item and put a nested `md-gb-list` in its `nested` slot. Add `expanded` to start open.

**Example: An expandable item with three nested items**

```html
<md-gb-list segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item expandable expanded>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">checklist</md-gb-icon>
    Groceries
    <span slot="supporting-text">3 items</span>
    <md-gb-list slot="nested" segmented>
      <md-gb-list-item>Bread</md-gb-list-item>
      <md-gb-list-item>Milk</md-gb-list-item>
      <md-gb-list-item>Eggs</md-gb-list-item>
    </md-gb-list>
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Swipe actions

Put buttons in the `leading-actions` and `trailing-actions` slots to reveal them when people swipe an item. A "more" button and the arrow keys offer the same actions without swiping.

**Example: A list item with a pin action and share and archive actions**

```html
<md-gb-list segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">restaurant</md-gb-icon>
    Fresh baked breads
    <button slot="leading-actions" aria-label="Pin Fresh baked breads">
      <md-gb-icon>keep</md-gb-icon>
    </button>
    <button slot="trailing-actions" aria-label="Share Fresh baked breads">
      <md-gb-icon>share</md-gb-icon>
    </button>
    <button slot="trailing-actions" aria-label="Archive Fresh baked breads">
      <md-gb-icon>archive</md-gb-icon>
    </button>
  </md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

### Density

Set `density` on the list from `0` (default) down to `-3` to remove 4px of height per step. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

**Example: A list at density -2**

```html
<md-gb-list density="-2" segmented>
  <md-gb-list-item>Apples</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Bananas</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Cucumbers</md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

## Accessibility

*   A list has `role="list"`, and `role="listbox"` when it is `selectable`. Items have `role="listitem"`. Label a list with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when its purpose isn't clear from the page.
*   Arrow keys move between items.
*   In a reorderable list, the drag handle and the move up and move down buttons have labels built from the item's text, and moves are announced to screen readers. Change them with `drag-handle-label`, `move-up-label` and `move-down-label` when you translate the page.
*   Give swipe action buttons an `aria-label` that names the item, such as "Share Fresh baked breads".
*   Selecting and reordering must not need a gesture only: the checkboxes, the move buttons and the "more" button are the single-pointer alternatives.

**Example: A list labelled Shopping list**

```html
<md-gb-list aria-label="Shopping list">
  <md-gb-list-item>Bread</md-gb-list-item>
  <md-gb-list-item>Milk</md-gb-list-item>
</md-gb-list>
```

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-list&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the items' height (spec foundations Density: "decreasing the top and bottom padding or overall height by 4dp"). Values are clamped to that range. Like <code>md-gb-segmented-button-set</code>'s <code>density</code>.</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>ListDensity</code> |  |
| <code>reorderable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the items can be reordered. Shows a drag handle on every item.</span> | <code>reorderable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>reorderMessages</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The screen reader announcements made while reordering.</span> |  | <code>ListReorderMessages</code> | <code>LIST_REORDER_MESSAGES</code> |
| <code>segmented</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to render the list with segmented items.</span> | <code>segmented</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selectable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the user can select several items with a long press (and drag), and by tapping them while in selection mode.</span> | <code>selectable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selectionPrimary</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether selecting is the list's primary activity: a <code>selectable</code> list then always shows the selection checkboxes (on desktop).</span> | <code>selection-primary</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display list items. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>itemselectionchange</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | When the user changes the selected items of a <code>selectable</code> list (<code>ListSelectionChangeEvent</code> with <code>selected</code>). |
| <code>reorder</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | When the user drops an item at a new position (<code>ListReorderEvent</code> with <code>from</code>, <code>to</code> and <code>item</code>). Cancelable. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(drop-zone)</code> | The drop target shown while dragging. |
| <code>::part(list)</code> | The list's root element. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--gap</code> |  |

### &lt;md-gb-list-item&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>checked</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the list item is selected.</span> | <code>checked</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>disabled</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the list item is disabled.</span> | <code>disabled</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>dragging</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item is being dragged. Set by the list while reordering.</span> | <code>dragging</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>dragHandleLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The accessible label prefix of the drag handle; the item's label text is appended (e.g. "Reorder Apples").</span> | <code>drag-handle-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>"Reorder"</code> |
| <code>expandable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item expands to reveal the content in its <code>nested</code> slot. Expandable items are always interactive.</span> | <code>expandable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>expanded</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether an <code>expandable</code> item is expanded.</span> | <code>expanded</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>grabbed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item is grabbed for reordering without dragging (with the keyboard or a tap on the drag handle). Set by the list; shows the move up and move down buttons.</span> | <code>grabbed</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>moveDownLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The accessible label prefix of the move down button; the item's label text is appended.</span> | <code>move-down-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>"Move down"</code> |
| <code>moveUpLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The accessible label prefix of the move up button; the item's label text is appended (e.g. "Move up Apples").</span> | <code>move-up-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>"Move up"</code> |
| <code>nonInteractive</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the list item is non-interactive.</span> | <code>static</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>noRevealButton</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Hides the "more" button that reveals the swipe actions with a tap. Only set it when the app offers another single-pointer way to reach them (e.g. a menu), as the spec requires one.</span> | <code>no-reveal-button</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>reorderable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether to show a drag handle to reorder the item within its <code>md-gb-list</code>. Set by the list when the list is <code>reorderable</code>.</span> | <code>reorderable</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>revealButtonLabel</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The accessible label prefix of the "more" button; the item's label text is appended (e.g. "More actions Apples").</span> | <code>reveal-button-label</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>"More actions"</code> |
| <code>revealed</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The side whose swipe actions are revealed, or <code>''</code> when closed.</span> | <code>revealed</code> | <code>ListItemRevealed</code> | <code>""</code> |
| <code>rovingTabIndex</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Set by a parent <code>md-gb-list</code> to make the list a single tab stop with arrow-key navigation (roving tabindex, lists.md Keyboard navigation): <code>0</code> on the list's tab stop, <code>-1</code> on the other items, <code>null</code> (default) for an item outside a list. While set, the item's other controls (drag handle, "more" and move buttons, actions) leave the tab order and are reached with Left/Right.</span> |  | <code>number</code> | <code>null</code> |
| <code>selectable</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the item shows a selection checkbox (hover, or whenever <code>selectionVisible</code>). Set by a <code>selectable</code> parent <code>md-gb-list</code>.</span> |  | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |
| <code>selectionVisible</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Whether the selection checkbox is always shown: the list sets it when selection is the primary activity or once an item is selected (selection.md, "Click"). Otherwise the checkbox shows on hover.</span> | <code>selection-visible</code> | <code>boolean</code> | <code>false</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Used to display the item's primary label. |
| <code>avatar</code> | Used to display a circular avatar before the item's content. |
| <code>leading</code> | Used to display icons and content before the item's main content. |
| <code>leading-actions</code> | Buttons revealed by swiping toward the end. |
| <code>nested</code> | Nested items or content an <code>expandable</code> item reveals. |
| <code>overline</code> | Used to display overline text above the main label. |
| <code>supporting-text</code> | Used to display supporting text below the main label. |
| <code>trailing</code> | Used to display icons and content after the item's main content. |
| <code>trailing-actions</code> | Buttons revealed by swiping toward the start. The last one is the primary action. |
| <code>trailing-text</code> | Used to display metadata or text after the item's main content. |

#### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>reveal-change</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | When the user reveals or hides the swipe actions. |
| <code>toggle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">Event</span> | When the user expands or collapses an <code>expandable</code> item (<code>ToggleEvent</code>). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>close</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Hides the swipe actions. |
| <code>focusDragHandle</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Focuses the item's drag handle, if it has one. |
| <code>focusPrimary</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Focuses the item itself (its primary action), or its first control when the item is <code>static</code> or disabled. Used by <code>md-gb-list</code>'s arrow keys. |
| <code>reveal</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(side: "leading" | "trailing") =&gt; void</span> | Reveals the swipe actions on one side. |
| <code>rowElements</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; HTMLElement[]</span> | The item's focusable elements in visual order (start to end): leading actions, interactive <code>avatar</code>/<code>leading</code> content, the item, interactive <code>trailing</code> content, the "more" button, the move up / move down buttons, the drag handle and the trailing actions. Left/Right move through them. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(actions)</code> | The container of the revealed actions. |
| <code>::part(drag-handle)</code> | The reorder drag handle. |
| <code>::part(list-item)</code> | The list item's root element. |
| <code>::part(move-down)</code> | The button that moves a grabbed item down. |
| <code>::part(move-up)</code> | The button that moves a grabbed item up. |
| <code>::part(nested)</code> | The expandable region of nested content. |
| <code>::part(reveal-button)</code> | The "more" button that reveals the swipe actions. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--avatar-color</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-label</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-label-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-label-color</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-label-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--avatar-size</code> |  |
| <code>--between-space</code> |  |
| <code>--bottom-space</code> |  |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-height</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Height removed per density step (set <code>density</code> on <code>md-gb-list</code>). |
| <code>--label-text</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--label-text-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--leading-space</code> |  |
| <code>--overline</code> |  |
| <code>--overline-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--overline-color</code> |  |
| <code>--overline-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--supporting-text</code> |  |
| <code>--supporting-text-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--supporting-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--supporting-text-tracking</code> |  |
| <code>--top-space</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-icon-color</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-icon-size</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-space</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-supporting-text</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-supporting-text-axes</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-supporting-text-color</code> |  |
| <code>--trailing-supporting-text-tracking</code> |  |

Source: https://material-web.dev/3.0/components/menu/

# Menus

Menus show a temporary set of actions or choices, opened from a button, a text field or a context.

**Example: A button that opens a menu of file actions**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="file-menu">File</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="file-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-item>New</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Open</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item disabled>Save</md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

## Usage guidelines

*   **Use it for temporary actions.** A menu shows a short set of actions on demand. To show actions on screen at all times, use a [toolbar](/material-web/3.0/components/toolbar/).
*   **Open it from many places.** A menu can open from a button, an icon button, a split button or a text field, or as a [context menu](#context-menu).
*   **Organize long menus.** Use [groups](#groups) with labels and dividers to separate related choices.
*   **Choose a color.** The `standard` color suits most menus; `vibrant` makes the selected items stand out.

## Anatomy

A menu holds items, groups and dividers. An item holds a label and optional slots, including a submenu.

**Example: A menu with a group, an item with all of its slots, a divider and another item**

*HTML*

```html
<md-gb-button id="more">More</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="more-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-group>
    <md-gb-menu-item>
      <md-gb-icon slot="leading">share</md-gb-icon>
      Share
      <span slot="supporting-text">Send a link</span>
      <span slot="trailing-text">Ctrl+S</span>
      <md-gb-icon slot="trailing">chevron_right</md-gb-icon>
      <md-gb-menu slot="submenu">
        <md-gb-menu-item>Email</md-gb-menu-item>
        <md-gb-menu-item>Messages</md-gb-menu-item>
      </md-gb-menu>
    </md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu-group>
  <md-gb-divider></md-gb-divider>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Delete</md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

*TypeScript*

```ts
const menu = document.querySelector('#more-menu')!;
menu.showPopover({source: document.querySelector('#more')!});
```

## Examples

### Opening a menu

A menu is a popover. Point an `md-gb-button` (or `md-gb-icon-button`, or a native button) at it with `popovertarget`, or call `showPopover()` from script. The menu positions itself next to the button and closes on Escape, when focus leaves, or when an item is chosen.

**Example: A button that opens a menu of sort options**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="sort-menu">Sort</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="sort-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-item>Name</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Date modified</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Size</md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Icons and supporting text

Fill the `leading`, `supporting-text`, `trailing-text` and `trailing` slots to add detail to an item.

**Example: Menu items with leading icons and keyboard shortcuts**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="edit-menu">Edit</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="edit-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">content_cut</md-gb-icon>
    Cut
    <span slot="trailing-text">Ctrl+X</span>
  </md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">content_copy</md-gb-icon>
    Copy
    <span slot="trailing-text">Ctrl+C</span>
  </md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-icon slot="leading">content_paste</md-gb-icon>
    Paste
    <span slot="trailing-text">Ctrl+V</span>
  </md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Groups

Wrap related items in an `md-gb-menu-group`. Set `label` for a heading, and `checkable` to `single` or `multiple` to make the items selectable like radio buttons or checkboxes. Use `checked` on the selected items.

**Example: A menu with a single-select group and a multi-select group**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="view-menu">View</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="view-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-group label="Sort by" checkable="single">
    <md-gb-menu-item checked>Name</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Date modified</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu-group>
  <md-gb-divider></md-gb-divider>
  <md-gb-menu-group label="Show" checkable="multiple">
    <md-gb-menu-item checked>Hidden files</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>File extensions</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu-group>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Grouped layout

Set `layout="grouped"` to show each group on its own surface with a gap between them, instead of one surface with dividers.

**Example: A menu with two groups on separate surfaces**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="actions-menu">Actions</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="actions-menu" layout="grouped">
  <md-gb-menu-group>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Undo</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Redo</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu-group>
  <md-gb-menu-group>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Cut</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Copy</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Paste</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu-group>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Vibrant color

Set `color="vibrant"` to use the tertiary color roles instead of the surface-based `standard` style.

**Example: A vibrant menu with a checked item**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="theme-menu">Theme</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="theme-menu" color="vibrant">
  <md-gb-menu-group checkable="single">
    <md-gb-menu-item checked>System</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Light</md-gb-menu-item>
    <md-gb-menu-item>Dark</md-gb-menu-item>
  </md-gb-menu-group>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Submenus

Put an `md-gb-menu` in an item's `submenu` slot. It opens beside the item on click, Enter, Space or the Right arrow key (Left in right-to-left layouts).

**Example: A menu item that opens a submenu**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="share-menu">Share</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="share-menu">
  <md-gb-menu-item>Copy link</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>
    Send to
    <md-gb-menu slot="submenu">
      <md-gb-menu-item>Email</md-gb-menu-item>
      <md-gb-menu-item>Message</md-gb-menu-item>
    </md-gb-menu>
  </md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Context menu

Set `context-for` to the id of an element to open the menu on a secondary click, the context menu key or a long press.

**Example: A menu that opens on right-click**

```html
<div id="photo" tabindex="0">Right-click or long press this photo</div>
<md-gb-menu context-for="photo">
  <md-gb-menu-item>Open in new window</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Save as</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Copy link</md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

### Density

Set `density` from `0` (default) down to `-3` to remove 4px of height per item for each step. Submenus inherit it. Keep it off by default and let people opt in.

**Example: A menu at density -2**

```html
<md-gb-button popovertarget="dense-menu">Open</md-gb-button>
<md-gb-menu id="dense-menu" density="-2">
  <md-gb-menu-item>Rename</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Duplicate</md-gb-menu-item>
  <md-gb-menu-item>Delete</md-gb-menu-item>
</md-gb-menu>
```

## Accessibility

*   The menu has `role="menu"`, and items have `role="menuitem"`, or `menuitemradio` and `menuitemcheckbox` in checkable groups.
*   On the button that opens the menu, Up and Down open it and focus the first item; Enter and Space open it natively.
*   In an open menu, Up and Down move between items (disabled items included), Home and End go to the first and last item, and typing a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it.
*   Escape and Tab close the menu and return focus to the button. Left (Right in right-to-left layouts) closes a submenu.
*   Give a menu that has no clear visible title an `aria-label`.

## API reference

### &lt;md-gb-menu&gt;

A Material Design component.

#### Properties

| Property | Attribute | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>color</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The color style: <code>standard</code> (surface-based) or <code>vibrant</code> (tertiary).</span> | <code>color</code> | <code>MenuColor</code> | <code>MENU_COLORS.standard</code> |
| <code>contextFor</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The id of an element (in the same root) that opens this menu as a context menu on a secondary click, the context menu key or a long press (menus.md "Context menus ... usually open with a secondary click"; "Performs a specific action to trigger the menu, like right-click or press-and-hold").</span> | <code>context-for</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>density</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The density, from 0 (default) to -3 (menus.md "Density": "On web only, density levels control the spacing between elements. Increasing density decreases the top and bottom padding"). Each step removes 4px from the items' height; submenus inherit it. Values are clamped to that range. Dense items are smaller than the 48px recommended target, so don't apply density by default; let people opt in (grids-spacing.md "Avoid applying component scaling by default").</span> | <code>density</code> | <code>Density</code> |  |
| <code>filterFor</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The id of a text field (in the same root) the menu is attached to. As the person types in it, the menu opens (without taking focus) and shows only the items whose label contains the text, case-insensitively (menus.md "Filtering": "As someone types, the list of menu options filters to show relevant results"). The remaining items ease into their new position ("Menu items ease into their new position as the menu is filtered"), unless motion is reduced. Fires <code>filter</code> with the query.</span> | <code>filter-for</code> | <code>string</code> | <code>''</code> |
| <code>layout</code><br><span class="gb-desc">The layout: <code>standard</code> items on one surface, or <code>grouped</code> <code>md-gb-menu-group</code>s on separate surfaces with gaps between them.</span> | <code>layout</code> | <code>MenuLayout</code> | <code>'standard'</code> |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | The menu's items, groups and dividers. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>closeAll</code><br><span class="gb-desc">() =&gt; void</span> | Closes this menu and every menu it is a submenu of. |
| <code>filter</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(query: string) =&gt; void</span> | Shows only the items whose label contains <code>query</code>, easing the others into their new position. |
| <code>showAt</code><br><span class="gb-desc">(x: number, y: number) =&gt; void</span> | Opens the menu at a point in the viewport (a context menu), keeping it inside the window: it opens below and after the point, and flips when there is no room. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>::part(menu)</code> | The menu's root element. |

#### CSS custom properties

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code>--container-color</code> |  |
| <code>--container-elevation</code> |  |
| <code>--container-max-width</code> |  |
| <code>--container-min-width</code> |  |
| <code>--container-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--density-step</code> | Item height removed per density step (set on the items). |
| <code>--gap</code> | Space between groups in the grouped layout. |
| <code>--group-padding</code> |  |
| <code>--group-shape</code> |  |
| <code>--section-label-text</code> |  |
| <code>--section-label-text-color</code> |  |
